Visa types classify the visa status held by international students and determine whether a student is full fee paying or subsidised. Types configured here are available for selection on student records and can drive fee calculations where students qualify for a fee reduction based on their visa status. Open Visa types and create a new entry From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Academic management, expand Setup, and click Visa types. Click New in the toolbar and complete the columns to create a new visa type: Full fee paying — select this if the student is not subsidised and must pay the full tuition fee. Active — clear this checkbox if the visa type is no longer valid. Deactivating does not delete historical records (④). Save Click Save.

Student Promotion manages the financial checks and processes for students moving between academic years. It covers the automatic polling of outstanding fee balances during re-enrolment periods, blocking students who exceed a configured threshold, reviewing blocked students, applying financial check overrides with an audit reason, clearing overrides at year-end, and raising transfer certificate fees for withdrawing students.

At the start of a new year or after a promotion process, overrides set in the previous cycle need to be cleared. Add the Financial check override column to the list view From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Academic Management, expand Students, and click All students. Right-click any column header and select Insert columns (③). Search for and add the Financial check override field (④), then click Update (⑤). The column displays as a checkbox (⑦) and persists in the view for future use. Identify and clear overrides Filter or sort the list by the Financial check override column to display only students with an active override. Clear overrides using one of the following methods: Individual — uncheck the Financial check override checkbox directly in the list for each student. Bulk via Excel — click Export to Excel, clear the override values in the exported file, then import the file back into the system.

The financial check setup defines the outstanding fee balance threshold that the Student Management System uses when polling Finance & Operations to determine whether a student is cleared for re-enrolment. Thresholds are configured by fee head (dimension value), so different acceptable balance limits can apply to different fee types. Open Fee schedule parameters From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Academic Management, expand Setup, and click Fee schedule parameters. Open the General tab (③) and expand the Financial dimension section (④). Add thresholds by fee head Click + New (⑤) and complete the following for each fee type that requires a balance check (⑥-⑦): Threshold amount — enter a monetary amount. If a student's outstanding balance for this fee head is at or above this amount, they will not receive financial clearance. Dimension value — select the fee head from the dropdown. The Description field defaults to the selected fee head. Repeat for each fee head that requires a threshold. Save Click Save. When the Student Management System requests re-enrolment clearance, it checks the student's outstanding balance by fee head against each configured threshold. A student is financially cleared only if their balance for each configured fee head is below the threshold.

Where a payment arrangement is in place and the school does not want to block a student's re-enrolment, an authorised user can apply a financial check override on the student's record. This override applies to the next system poll only — it does not permanently exempt the student from the financial check. Open the student record From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Academic Management, expand Students, and click All students. Open the relevant student record. Apply the override In the Enrolment details tab, set the Financial check override toggle to Yes (④) and select an Override reason code from the dropdown (⑤). Reason codes are configured by the school (e.g., Fee check — payment plan in place) and create an audit record for the override. Click Save. On the next system poll, the student will be excluded from the financial check and their status will update to Re-enrolment open.
documents.s: Override the Financial Check for Re-Enrolment

documents.t: When a student withdraws and requests a transfer certificate, a free-text invoice is generated using the preconfigured TCINV template. In a live environment, this step is triggered by a request from the customer experience team. Create the invoice from template From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Accounts receivable, expand Invoices, and click All free text invoices. Click New from template in the Action Pane (③), select TCINV in the Template field (④), and complete the following: Customer account (⑤) — enter or select the fee payer. Create invoice by using the default values from — select Free text invoice template (⑥). Click OK. The template pre-populates the invoice line with the transfer certificate fee configuration. Complete invoice details In the Description field, enter a description (⑧). Scroll down and expand the Line details tab (⑨), then open the Financial dimensions line tab (⑩). Set the financial dimensions (⑪) — select Curriculum, School Levels, and Year Group. The Fee Head field is auto-populated based on the free-text invoice template setup. Post the invoice Click Post (⑫), set Batch processing to No (⑬), click OK, and close the page.

During re-enrolment, the Student Management System automatically polls Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations (D365 F&O) to check each student's outstanding balance. Students whose balance exceeds the configured threshold are blocked from re-enrolment — the Student Management System is notified not to issue their invitation until the balance is cleared. The threshold is configured in fee schedule parameters and must be set before the polling period begins. Identify the blocked student From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Academic Management, expand Students, and click All students. Open the relevant student record and confirm their status shows as Blocked (④&⑥). Students whose balance exceeds the configured threshold are automatically assigned a Blocked status, and the Student Management System is notified to prevent re-enrolment progression. Arrange payment and confirm clearance Contact the family to arrange payment of the outstanding balance. Once payment is received and the system polls again, confirm the student's status has updated to Re-enrolment open.

Before a student can be promoted, their academic enrolment record must show both the current grade and the next academic year record. The next academic year record is automatically received from the Student Management System after eligibility and finance checks are completed. Note: Do not edit the Academic enrolments table directly in Dynamics 365 — records are managed upstream by the Student Management System. Open the student record From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Academic Management, expand Students, and click All students. Open the relevant student record (④). Confirm enrolment status and academic records Confirm the student's enrolment status shows as Re-enrolment open. Select Academic from the Action Pane and click the Academic enrolments tab (⑤). Verify the table shows both the student's current grade/year and the next grade/year for promotion.

Subject & Event Management handles the setup and invoicing of fee-generating activities including excursions, music lessons, and other school events. Fee categories, subject and event codes, and event fee schedule templates are configured before students are enrolled into sessional classes or events. Invoicing can be set to charge a flat fee or calculated based on sessions attended. Where session numbers change after invoices have been generated, adjustment processing is available. Enrolment cancellations are also managed here.

Open the item From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Product information management, expand Products, and click Released products. Find and select the item (e.g., Piano fee) (③). Click Edit in the Action Pane (④). Set the fee category Expand the Sell section below (⑤) and set the Fee category (⑥). Save Click Save.
documents.s: Assign Fee Category to an Item

documents.t: When a student's enrolment in a sessional class or event needs to be cancelled after invoicing, the cancellation is performed from the Sessional class and event details form. The system automatically generates a credit note to reverse the original invoice. The credit note is recorded in the journal section with the same sales order details as the original invoice, and the quantity and total price on the reversed sales order appear as negative values. Open the enrolment record From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Academic Management, expand Inquiries and reports ▸ Fee schedules, and click Sessional class and event details. Locate the enrolment record for the student and event to cancel (④). Cancel and confirm Click Cancel in the toolbar (⑤). Click Yes to confirm. The system generates a credit note to reverse the original invoice. View the credit note Open the General tab (⑧) and click the Document number link (⑨) to view the reversed sales order. Open the student record. Click Invoice journal (⑩) to view the posted credit note, then click Voucher (⑪) to review the posted accounting entry.
documents.s: Sessional Class and Event Enrolment Cancellation

documents.t: Before the fee generation batch can invoice students for sessional classes or events, a fee schedule template specific to the event must be in place. Event templates are set up the same way as standard fee schedule templates but are configured with the event-specific billing interval and fee item. Open All fee schedules and create a new template From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Academic Management, expand Fee schedules, and click All fee schedules. Click New in the Action Pane. Complete the template header and fee lines Enter a Description (e.g., Event template) (④) and choose the Billing interval (⑤). Click + Add line (⑥) and complete the required fields for each line. If required, a Condition can be added to restrict the template to specific event codes or student groups. Save Click Save.
documents.s: Create an Event Fee Schedule Template

documents.t: If Session Based is not enabled, the system charges a flat fee (quantity = 1). Delete any previously generated sales orders for this event and student before rerunning the fee-generation batch. Open the fee schedule template From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Academic Management, expand Fee schedules, and click All fee schedules. Find and open the relevant fee schedule template (③). Enable and save Click Edit in the Action Pane. Enable the Session Based option (④) and click Save. Then run the fee schedule batch to generate the invoices.

Once the subject and event codes are in place, a fee schedule template must be created to link each event code to the correct fee item. The template uses conditions to restrict invoice generation to students enrolled in that event. Create a new fee schedule template From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Academic Management, expand Fee schedules, and click All fee schedules. Click New in the Action Pane. Enter a Description for the template (e.g., Zoo Excursion Fee) (④), choose the Billing interval(⑤), and match Early payment discounts with the fee categories (⑥). Add the fee line and condition Click + Add line (⑦) and complete the line (⑧): Item number — select the relevant fee item. Apply to — change to Session class and event. Condition — enable the checkbox. Click Condition in the toolbar (⑨). In the line with Code in the Field column, enter the event code in the Criteria column (⑩) by clicking +, then click OK (⑪). Save Click Save.
documents.s: Enrol a Student in a Sessional Class or Event

documents.t: Run this task after updating the session record status to Changed. Run the adjustment task From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Academic Management, expand Periodic tasks, and click Generate sessional class and event adjustments. Enter the adjustment Date (③), and expand Records to include to filter (④) for a specific student if needed (leave blank to process all records with a Changed status). Click OK (⑤). The system creates a new sales order reflecting the correct session count and the adjusted charge amount.

When a parent or guardian registers for an event in person, staff complete the enrolment directly in the system and generate the invoice from the Sessional class and event details form. Once posted, the charge is held as deferred revenue until the event date. Note: Student event registration is typically completed by the student or parent via Parent Connect, which automatically creates the enrolment record. Use this process only when a parent or guardian is registering in person at the school counter. Open Sessional class and event details From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Academic Management, expand Inquiries and reports ▸ Fee schedules, and click Sessional class and event details. Click New in the Action Pane. Complete the registration record Fill in the following: Student account (④) — select the student to register. Event Code (⑤) — select the event from the dropdown. Number of sessions (⑥) — enter the session count. Price (⑦) — enter the event price. Effective date and Expiration date (⑧) — enter the registration period. Click Save. Generate the invoice Click Generate invoice in the Action Pane (⑩). The system creates a sales order with a deferral schedule attached, recording the charge as deferred revenue until the event date. View the sales order and voucher Open the General tab (⑪), then click the Sales order hyperlink (⑫) to view the order. Click Invoice journal (⑬) to view the posted invoice, then click Voucher (⑭) to review the posted accounting entry.

A deferral date must be set against the event record before generating invoices. Until that date the charge is held in a deferred revenue account; once the event date passes, the system automatically transfers the balance to the main revenue account. Open the event record From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Academic Management, expand Setup, and click Subject and event names. Locate and select the relevant event record. Set the deferral date Click Deferrals, enable the Deferred toggle, and set the Deferral date to the event date. Click OK.

Before students can be enrolled in sessional classes or events and invoiced, the system needs the correct fee categories, subject codes, and event names configured. Each entry must be marked active before it can be used in fee processing. This setup is typically created through integration from the upstream activity module — manual entry is rarely required. Open Subject and event names From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Academic Management, expand Setup, and click Subject and event names. Click New in the Action Pane. Complete the record Fill in the following fields (④): Code — enter or create a unique code. Name — enter the subject or event name. Category — select the correct category from the dropdown. The Type field auto-fills based on the selected category. Active — check the box to activate the record. Item number — select the item number from the dropdown. Save Click Save.
documents.s: Set Up Subject and Event Names

documents.t: When a student attends more or fewer sessions than originally invoiced, update the session record status to Changed, enter the revised session count, and run the adjustment batch. The system calculates the difference and creates an updated sales order. Update the session record From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Academic Management, expand Inquiries and reports ▸ Fee schedules, and click Sessional class and events details. Locate and select the record requiring adjustment. Open the Change status dropdown in the Action Pane and change the status to Changed (⑤). Enter the revised number of sessions in the Updated sessions column (⑥) and click Save. Generate the adjustment See Generate the Session Adjustment to create the adjusted sales order.
Common problems in Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations and how to resolve them. Use the contents list on the right to jump to a section, or press Ctrl+F to search this page.
Cause — The navigation pane may have been collapsed using the hamburger menu icon. Fix — Click the hamburger menu icon (☰) at the top left of the screen to expand the navigation pane.
documents.s: The navigation pane is not visible or has disappeared

documents.t: Cause — The user may not have the correct security role or permissions to access that module, or the module may be in a different location than expected. Fix — Use the search bar at the top of the page to search for the module or form by name. If it does not appear, contact your system administrator to confirm access permissions.
documents.s: A module or page cannot be found in the navigation pane

documents.t: Cause — The default dashboard may not have been configured for the user's role. Fix — Click the Home icon at the top of the navigation pane. If the wrong dashboard loads, contact your system administrator to update the default dashboard for your role.
documents.s: The Home icon does not return the user to the correct dashboard

documents.t: Cause — The sibling order number may not be assigned to the student record, the trade agreement may not have been posted, or the line discount group has not been linked to the tuition fee item. Fix — Confirm the student's sibling order number is set under General in their student record. Verify the trade agreement has been posted and that the Line discount group on the relevant released products is set to the Sibling discount trade agreement.
documents.s: A sibling discount is not applying to a student's invoice

documents.t: Cause — The sibling order number assigned to the student does not match the correct discount group in the trade agreement. Fix — Review the student's sibling order number and compare it against the Customer price/discount groups setup under Sales and marketing ▸ Prices and discounts. Correct any mismatches and rerun the sales order batch.
documents.s: The wrong discount percentage is applying to a sibling

documents.t: Cause — The student may have been assigned a sibling order number of 2 or higher when they should have been assigned 0 (not current) or 1 (eldest/only child). Fix — Navigate to the student's record, open the General section, and check the Sibling field. Update the sibling order number to the correct value. If the student has no siblings currently enrolled, set the value to 1 or 0 per your school's configuration.
documents.s: A sibling discount is applying to a student who should not be receiving one

documents.t: Cause — The payment schedule may not have been linked to a payment option under Academic Management ▸ Setup ▸ Payment option setup. Fix — Navigate to Setup ▸ Payment option setup, confirm the payment plan has been created and linked to the correct payment schedule, and ensure the start and end dates are valid.
documents.s: The payment schedule isn't appearing in the Payment plan dropdown

documents.t: Cause — The threshold limit may not have been configured for the relevant fee head, or the dimension value assigned to the threshold does not match the fee head on the student's outstanding invoices. Fix — Navigate to Academic Management ▸ Setup ▸ Fee schedule parameters and review the thresholds configured under the Financial dimension section. Confirm the Dimension value for each threshold matches the fee head on the student's outstanding transactions.
documents.s: The financial check threshold is not blocking students as expected during reenrolment

documents.t: Cause — The student's record has not been updated prior to fee generation. Fix — Navigate to Modules ▸ Academic Management ▸ Students ▸ All students, open the student record, and update the academic year, effective date, and expiration date before running the fee generation batch.
documents.s: Student details are incorrect when generating fees

documents.t: Cause — The student's Current academic year field has not been updated after promotion or reenrolment. Fix — Open the student record in Modules ▸ Academic Management ▸ Students ▸ All students, confirm the Current academic year under Enrolment details, and update it if required before running fee generation.
documents.s: The student's academic year is still showing the previous year

documents.t: Cause — Split billing percentages have not been assigned or were entered incorrectly across the fee payers linked to the student. Fix — Navigate to the student record and scroll to the Relationships section. Adjust the paid percentages for each listed fee payer so the combined total equals 100.00 before running any fee generation batch.
documents.s: A student's Paid percentage total in the Relationships section does not equal 100

documents.t: Cause — The student may not be included in the customer filter, or the fee schedule template may not have been selected in the batch. Fix — When running the Generate Sales Order Batch Processing task, confirm that the correct customer academic year is selected under Records to include (Customers) and the correct fee schedule template is selected under Records to include (Fee schedule templates).
documents.s: Fee invoices are not being generated for some students

documents.t: Cause — The Create sale orders posting option was selected instead of Post invoice automatically, requiring a manual posting step. Fix — Navigate to Accounts receivable ▸ Sales orders ▸ All sales orders and manually post the invoices from there.
documents.s: Invoices are created but not posted

documents.t: Cause — Some students may have been excluded by the customer filter, or their records may not meet the conditions set in the fee schedule template. Fix — Review the customer filter applied during batch processing and confirm all students are assigned to the correct academic year and meet any template conditions.
documents.s: The fee generation reconciliation report shows fewer students than expected

documents.t: Cause — The Fee and charge interval selected in the batch does not match the intervals configured on the relevant students' academic enrolment records. Fix — Confirm the Fee and charge interval in the Generate Sales Order Batch Processing task matches the interval configured on each student's academic enrolment record. Only students with a matching interval will be picked up by the batch.
documents.s: Invoices are being generated for the wrong students or academic year

documents.t: Cause — The Post Sale Order Invoice batch may not have been filtered by period name, causing all terms to post together or not at all. Fix — When running the Post Sale Order Invoice batch, set the Period name filter to the specific term being posted (e.g., Term 1, Term 2). Each term must be run as a separate batch job.
documents.s: Term 2 or Term 3 invoices are not posting separately from Term 1

documents.t: Cause — The condition on the fee schedule template line may be referencing the wrong field or criteria value, or the condition may not have been enabled. Fix — Open the fee schedule template, select the relevant line, and click Condition in the toolbar. Confirm the field and criteria value are correct. If the item should apply to all students, ensure Condition is not enabled.
documents.s: A new fee schedule template is not applying conditions correctly to a student cohort

documents.t: Cause — The split percent by fee items configuration may have been set up after the sales orders were already generated, meaning existing invoices are unaffected. Fix — Set up the split configuration before running the sales order generation. For existing invoices, delete the sales order and rerun the Generate Sales Order Batch Processing task after the split configuration is in place.
documents.s: The split billing percentages are not applying correctly to a student's invoice

documents.t: Cause — The split percentages assigned to each fee payer in the student's Relationships section have not been configured correctly. Fix — Navigate to the student record, scroll to the Relationships section, and adjust the paid percentages so that the total equals 100.00 before generating invoices.
documents.s: The total paid percentage for fee payers does not equal 100

documents.t: Cause — The Pro rata field on the tuition fee item has not been enabled, or the student's effective date has not been updated to reflect their actual start date. Fix — Confirm the Pro rata field on the released product is set to any option except None. Then navigate to the student's academic enrolment record and update the Effective date to the student's actual start date before rerunning the fee generation batch.
documents.s: A new student is being charged the full term fee instead of a pro rata amount

documents.t: Cause — The student's last day at school may have been entered incorrectly when running the Calculate fee and charge adjustment task. Fix — Review the sales order adjustment and confirm the Quantity column shows a negative value reflecting the correct number of remaining school days. If incorrect, rerun the Calculate fee and charge adjustment task with the correct leaving date.
documents.s: An exiting student's refund amount appears incorrect

documents.t: Cause — The Use print management destination option may not have been enabled when confirming the sales order, or the fee payer's email address is not on file. Fix — Navigate to the sales order, click Sell in the Action Pane, then select Sales order confirmation under Journals. Open the latest confirmation, click Preview/Print, and select Use print management. Confirm the fee payer has a valid email address on their account before resending.
documents.s: The fee payer hasn't received the proforma invoice

documents.t: Cause — A price change was made to the trade agreement after the sales order was generated, so existing open orders still reflect the old price. Fix — Navigate to Academic Management ▸ Periodic tasks ▸ Recalculate Open Sales Order. Filter for the relevant student or sales order, enable Recalculate sales price, and click OK. Refresh the sales order to confirm future term lines show the updated price.
documents.s: A fee price needs updating on an already-generated proforma invoice

documents.t: Cause — The Setup menu under Academic Management may not be fully expanded, or the user does not have the correct permissions. Fix — Expand Modules ▸ Academic Management ▸ Setup ▸ Pre-admission fees and click Pre-admission types. If the option is still not visible, contact your system administrator.
documents.s: The Pre-Admission Types page is not visible in the menu

documents.t: Cause — Required fields in the record may be incomplete, or the posting logic for that transaction type has not been configured. Fix — Ensure all required columns in the record are filled in. Verify that posting logic has been set up for the relevant transaction type under Setup ▸ Pre-admission fees ▸ Pre-admission posting.
documents.s: A pre-admission fee record cannot be posted

documents.t: Cause — The posting process may not have completed successfully, or a required field such as bank account was not selected. Fix — Review the record for any error messages. Re-attempt the post after confirming all required fields are complete. Check that the correct bank account has been assigned.
documents.s: The status of a pre-admission fee does not update after posting

documents.t: Cause — Only deposits with a status of Received or Partial are eligible for forfeiture or refund. Deposits in any other status cannot be processed. Fix — Filter the Pre-admission deposits list by status and confirm the deposit shows as Received or Partial before attempting to forfeit or refund.
documents.s: A deposit cannot be forfeited or refunded

documents.t: Cause — The fee may not have a status of Posted, or the user may not have the correct permissions to perform reversals. Fix — Filter the All pre-admission fees list by Status = Posted to confirm the record is eligible for reversal. Contact your system administrator if the Cancel button remains unavailable.
documents.s: The Reverse option is not available for a pre-admission fee

documents.t: Cause — The student record may not have been progressed to Registered status in the student management system before the manual post was attempted, so the sales order was never created. Fix — Confirm the student management system shows the student as Registered. Then navigate to Academic Management ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Pre-admission fees ▸ All pre-admission fees, locate the application fee record, and click Post with Preview set to Yes. Once posted, the sales order will be available for cashier receipting.
documents.s: A registration fee receipt can't be processed — the sales order doesn't exist

documents.t: Cause — Required columns such as Code or Name may be incomplete, or the approval group has not been assigned. Fix — Ensure all required columns are completed, including Code, Name, Active, Approval, and User group, before clicking Save.
documents.s: A new scholarship or discount cannot be saved

documents.t: Cause — The discount may still be in Draft or Under Review status and has not been fully approved. Fix — Navigate to the scholarship or discount record, open the Students tab, and confirm the approval status. Select Approve from the Approval dropdown if the record is Under Review.
documents.s: The scholarship or discount is not visible on the student's invoice

documents.t: Cause — The logged-in user may not be a member of the approval group assigned to the scholarship or discount. Fix — Contact your system administrator to confirm the correct user group is assigned and that your account has been added as an approver.
documents.s: The Approve option is not available in the Approval dropdown

documents.t: Cause — The scholarship or discount may not have been linked to the correct fee items, or the student's record may not have been linked with valid effective and expiration dates. Fix — Confirm the scholarship or discount is linked to the correct fee items under the General tab and that the student has been added under the Students tab with valid effective and expiration dates.
documents.s: A scholarship or discount is not applying to a student's invoice after approval

documents.t: Cause — One or more fields in the row contain invalid or missing data that failed the system's validation on publish. Fix — Review the highlighted rows and correct any flagged fields. Common causes include missing required fields, incorrect date formats, or student account numbers that do not exist in the system. Click Publish again after correcting the data.
documents.s: Published rows in the Excel add-in import are highlighted in red and not saving

documents.t: Cause — The add-in may not have completed sign-in, or the connection to the environment has timed out. Fix — Wait for the Excel add-in to finish sign-in before clicking Design or Refresh. If the connection fails, close and reopen the file, enable editing, and allow the add-in to reconnect before proceeding.
documents.s: The Excel add-in is not connecting to the GEMS environment after downloading the template

documents.t: Cause — The user may not have the correct permissions, or the visa type already exists in the system. Fix — Search for the visa type before creating a new one to avoid duplicates. If creation is blocked, contact your system administrator to confirm permissions. Note that visa entries are typically generated automatically from Customer Engagement (CE).
documents.s: A new visa type cannot be created manually

documents.t: Cause — The visa information may not have been synced from CE, or the student record may not have a visa assigned. Fix — Scroll to the Other Information tab on the student record to locate visa details. If the information is missing, confirm whether the visa has been created in CE and that the integration is functioning correctly.
documents.s: Visa details are not visible on a student's record

documents.t: Cause — The student may not have been enrolled in the sessional class or event, or the fee schedule template may not have the correct condition configured. Fix — Navigate to Inquiries and reports ▸ Fee schedules ▸ Sessional class and event details and confirm the student has been assigned to the correct class or event with valid effective and expiration dates.
documents.s: A sessional class or event fee is not generating for a student

documents.t: Cause — The Session Based option on the fee schedule template has not been enabled. Fix — Open the relevant fee schedule template, enable the Session Based option, click Save, and delete any previously generated sales orders for the event or student before rerunning the Generate Sale Order Batch Process.
documents.s: The system is charging a flat fee instead of a session-based fee

documents.t: Cause — The record status may not have been changed from Invoice to Change before updating session numbers. Fix — Open the record in Sessional class and events details, change the status to Change using the Change status dropdown, enter the updated session numbers, save, and then run the Generate sessional class and event adjustments task.
documents.s: A sessional class adjustment is not generating after updating session numbers

documents.t: Cause — The Deferred option on the event record may not have been enabled, or the deferral date has not been set. Fix — Navigate to Academic Management ▸ Setup ▸ Subject and event names, locate the event record, click Deferrals, enable the Deferred option, and set the Deferral date to the event date. Delete any existing sales orders for the event and rerun the fee generation batch.
documents.s: Revenue is posting immediately instead of being deferred to the event date

documents.t: Cause — The financial check threshold may not have been configured correctly for the relevant fee head, or the dimension value assigned to the threshold does not match the fee head on the student's outstanding invoices. Fix — Navigate to Academic Management ▸ Setup ▸ Fee schedule parameters and review the thresholds configured under the Financial dimension section. Confirm the Dimension value for each threshold matches the fee head on the student's outstanding transactions.
documents.s: A student is blocked from reenrolment despite being within the threshold

documents.t: Cause — The system poll that checks financial clearance has not yet run since the override was applied. Fix — The override takes effect on the next system poll, not immediately. Confirm the override has been saved on the student record and wait for the next scheduled poll. If the status does not update after the poll, contact your system administrator.
documents.s: A financial check override hasn't opened the student for reenrolment

documents.t: Cause — Overrides were not cleared at the start of the new academic year. Fix — Navigate to All students, add the Financial check override column using Insert field, and clear overrides either individually by unchecking the checkbox per student, or in bulk by exporting to Excel, clearing the values, and importing the file back.
documents.s: Overrides from a previous promotion cycle are still active

documents.t: Cause — The Financial dimension fields on the invoice line may not have been set, or the TCINV template was not selected when creating the free text invoice. Fix — When creating the transfer certificate invoice, confirm the TCINV template is selected in the New from template dialog. After the invoice is created, expand Line details, open Financial dimension line, and set the required dimensions (Curriculum, School Levels, Year Group) before posting.
documents.s: A transfer certificate invoice is not posting correctly

documents.t: Cause — The invoice checkbox may not have been marked before posting the payment. Fix — Before clicking Post, ensure the correct invoices are checked in the payment form. If the payment has already been posted without allocation, review the advance payment and manually settle it against the correct invoice.
documents.s: An over-the-counter payment is not allocating to the correct invoice

documents.t: Cause — The invoice was not marked before posting, so the payment was recorded as an advance rather than applied to the outstanding balance. Fix — Locate the student's account in Modules ▸ Academic Management ▸ Students ▸ All students, click Customer in the Action Pane, then click Transactions to view the advance. Manually settle the advance against the correct invoice.
documents.s: A payment is sitting as an unallocated advance

documents.t: Cause — The date range entered may not match any due invoices, or the Method of payment filter is not set to credit card (CC). Fix — Confirm the date range covers the correct period and that the Method of payment is set to CC. Check that invoices exist within that period and have not already been paid.
documents.s: A credit card payment proposal is not returning any invoices

documents.t: Cause — The payment service provider may have rejected the request, or the card details or account setup may be incorrect. Fix — Review the failure message returned by the system. Unauthorised lines will be deleted automatically. Manually retry or review the affected transactions and contact your payment service provider if the issue persists.
documents.s: Credit card authorisation is failing during payment processing

documents.t: Cause — The Postdated check toggle may not have been enabled in the Check details window, or the cheque was not posted after entry. Fix — When processing a post-dated cheque via Cashier Receipt, ensure the Method of payment is set to Cheque, click Check details, enable the Postdated check toggle, enter the maturity date and other required fields, and post the journal.
documents.s: A post-dated cheque is not appearing in the system after entry

documents.t: Cause — An amount exceeding the invoice total was entered in the Amount field, and the excess was recorded as an overpayment. Fix — Before clicking Post, review the Overpayment field that appears after saving. If the overpayment was entered in error, correct the amount in the Amount field before proceeding to post.
documents.s: An overpayment was posted by mistake and needs to be corrected before the receipt is issued

documents.t: Cause — The Co-branded option may not have been enabled in the Cashier Receipt form, or the Advanced Discount Policy has not been configured for the relevant fee and charge interval. Fix — Confirm the Advanced Discount Policy is configured for the relevant fee and charge interval. When processing the payment, ensure the Co-branded option is enabled before selecting the method of payment. The Calculate Discount button only activates when Co-branded is enabled.
documents.s: An advance payment discount has not been calculated when processing a co-branded payment

documents.t: Cause — The payment plan may not have been applied and confirmed correctly, or the invoice was generated before the payment plan was set up. Fix — Follow the Apply Payment Plan to Fee Payer steps in full, including selecting the invoice, previewing, and confirming. If the invoice was generated prior to the payment plan setup, the plan may need to be applied and the invoice re-split.
documents.s: An invoice is not splitting into instalments after a payment plan is applied

documents.t: Cause — The payment date may be after the discount due date, or the Early payment discount eligibility setting has not been configured correctly. Fix — Ensure the payment date is set before the discount due date when settling transactions. Confirm the Early payment discount eligibility setting is correctly configured under Academic Management ▸ Setup ▸ Fee schedule parameter.
documents.s: A cash discount is not applying when a payment is processed

documents.t: Cause — The Early payment discount eligibility setting may be disabled, allowing discounts to apply even when only one invoice is paid. Fix — Navigate to Academic Management ▸ Setup ▸ Fee schedule parameter and enable the Early payment discount eligibility checkbox so that discounts only apply when all due invoices are paid together.
documents.s: A discount has been applied to an invoice but should not have been

documents.t: Cause — The date range entered in the Update early payment discount task may not have captured the correct invoices, or the early payment date was not set correctly. Fix — Rerun the Update early payment discount task with the correct date range and early payment date. Then navigate to Accounts receivable ▸ Invoices ▸ Open Customer Invoices to confirm discounts have been applied.
documents.s: Discounts are not appearing on invoices after running the bulk update task

documents.t: Cause — The Update early payment discount batch task may not have been run after the discount was assigned to the product. Fix — Navigate to Academic Management ▸ Periodic tasks and run the Update early payment discount task for the relevant date range and fee payers. Confirm discounts appear on open invoices in Accounts receivable ▸ Invoices ▸ Open Customer Invoices.
documents.s: An early payment discount isn't appearing on generated invoices

documents.t: Cause — The Financial dimensions for the account or offset account were not completed before posting the customer refund journal. Fix — Before clicking Post, click Financial dimensions above the journal lines table and set the Fee head value. Then click Financial dimensions again for the offset account and set the Cashflow field to Refund. Submit for workflow approval if required before posting.
documents.s: A fee refund cannot be posted because the fee head financial dimension has not been set

documents.t: Cause — The reversal date cannot be set to a date prior to the original posting date. Fix — Set the reversal date to a date on or after the original posting date. Navigate to the student's transaction list via Customer ▸ Transactions in the Action Pane, select the transaction, click Reverse, then Cancel payment, and enter a valid date before selecting a reason code and confirming.
documents.s: A posted payment needs to be reversed but the reversal date field is not accepting the entry

documents.t: Cause — The non-sufficient funds (NSF) payment option may not have been selected during the reversal, or the resulting journal was not posted. Fix — Confirm that NSF payment was selected (not a standard reversal) when processing the cancel. Navigate to Accounts receivable ▸ Payments ▸ Customer payment journal, enable Show user-created only, locate the journal created for the NSF reversal, open Lines, and click Post.
documents.s: A dishonoured cheque was reversed but no NSF fee appeared

documents.t: Cause — The Company field may not have been set to the correct school when creating the cashier receipt journal. Fix — When processing a Pay at Any School payment, ensure the Company field in the cashier receipt is set to the school that issued the invoice — not the school processing the payment. Once posted, confirm the Pay at Any School column on the journal header is ticked.
documents.s: A Pay at Any School receipt isn't flagged correctly

documents.t: Cause — The date range selected may not include any transactions, or the filter may be pointing to the wrong account. Fix — Confirm the start and end dates cover the correct statement period. Open the Records to include section and verify the correct fee payer account has been selected in the filter.
documents.s: A fee payer statement is generating with no data

documents.t: Cause — The journal may require workflow approval before it can be posted, or the posting account has not been configured. Fix — Navigate to General Ledger ▸ Journal entries ▸ General journals, locate the write-off journal, and review its status. If workflow is enabled, submit the journal for approval and follow the approval process before posting. If workflow is not enabled, post the journal directly.
documents.s: A customer write-off journal is not available to post after creation

documents.t: Cause — The activity filter in the events list may be set to show only open items, hiding closed or resolved notes. Fix — In the customer detail screen, open Collect ▸ Collections ▸ Show in All activities, and select Open and closed to display all notes including resolved items. Click the Notes tab to review the full history.
documents.s: A debtor note is not visible after it was created in the Collections Coordinator workspace

documents.t: Cause — The Consolidate deposit slip task may not have been filtered by the correct Method of payment, or the date range did not capture all transactions from the day. Fix — Return to Modules ▸ Accounts receivable ▸ Workspaces ▸ Customer payments and rerun the Consolidate deposit slip task, ensuring the correct date range and Method of payment filter are applied. Verify that the consolidated slip appears and that individual slips no longer show under Open deposit slips.
documents.s: Open deposit slips are still showing after the end-of-day consolidation was run

documents.t: Cause — One or more individual payments may not have been posted before the consolidation was run, or a payment was posted with the wrong method of payment. Fix — Review the open deposit slips for the date in question and confirm all payments for the day have been posted. Check that each payment was recorded against the correct method of payment. Re-consolidate if needed after correcting any errors.
documents.s: The end-of-day deposit total does not match the expected cash received for the day

documents.t: Cause — The GEMS reward balance account may already be at zero for the selected date range, meaning there is no balance to transfer. This can also occur if the task has already been run for the same date. Fix — Navigate to General Ledger ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Trial balance and confirm the GEMS reward balance account has a non-zero balance for the selected date range before running the transfer. If the balance is already zero, no transfer is required for that period.
documents.s: The Transfer GEMS Reward Balances task is not generating a journal when run

documents.t: Cause — The offset account in the journal may not have been configured correctly in the Receipt intercompany mapping, or the From date and To date do not match the trial balance dates used to verify the balance. Fix — Review the journal lines in General Ledger ▸ Journal entries ▸ General journals and confirm the credit amount equals the debit minus credit balance from the trial balance. Check the Receipt intercompany mapping setup to confirm the correct offset company and general ledger account are configured for the GEMS reward method of payment.
documents.s: The GEMS reward transfer journal has posted but the balance account has not cleared to zero

documents.t: Cause — The student may have advanced tax invoices still outstanding, or the Destination school field on the student record has not been populated by the CE system. Fix — Cancel any outstanding advanced tax invoices before attempting the transfer. Confirm the Destination school field is populated under Other Information on the student record. If the field is blank, verify the transfer has been initiated in CE and that the integration is functioning correctly.
documents.s: A credit balance transfer cannot be completed for a student moving between schools

documents.t: Cause — The intercompany channel setup may not have been completed in either the originating or destination school, or the Party ID does not match across both companies. Fix — Confirm the intercompany journal setup has been completed in both schools under Academic Management ▸ Setup ▸ Intercompany journal. Verify that the student's Party ID is identical in both the originating and destination school's records, as the system uses this to match accounts across companies.
documents.s: The intercompany transfer journals aren't generating in both schools

documents.t: Cause — The Override transaction date field may not have been set to Yes, or the Transaction date entered does not match the last day of the period being closed. Fix — When running Recognition processing, set Override transaction date to Yes and enter the last day of the relevant month in both the Cutoff date and Transaction date fields.
documents.s: Revenue recognition processing is posting journal entries to the wrong period

documents.t: Cause — Deferral schedules may not have been configured for the relevant fee items, or all eligible lines may have already been recognised for the period. Fix — Navigate to Subscription billing ▸ Revenue and expense deferrals ▸ All deferral schedules and confirm deferral schedules exist for the relevant invoices. If schedules exist but lines have already been recognised, no further action is required for that period.
documents.s: The recognition processing preview is returning no lines for the current period

documents.t: Visa Management keeps student visa records accurate and accessible within Academic Management. Visa entries are typically created automatically through the Customer Engagement (CE) integration; staff can also view visa details on individual student records and run a report listing all students with active visas across the school.

The Students with visa report gives a full list of students with active visa records across the school. Use it to review international student cohort data and filter by visa status. Open the report From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Academic Management, expand Inquiries and reports, expand Visa Management, and click Students with visa. Filter and review Use the checkboxes (④) to filter results by visa status. The report lists all students with active visa records and their visa type.

Visa details for an individual student are stored on their record under the Other Information tab. Use this to check a student's visa type, issue date, and expiry date directly from the student record. Open the student record From the F&O dashboard, open Modules ▸ Academic Management, expand Students, and click All Students. Select or search for the student account and open their record (③). View visa details Scroll down to the Other Information tab (④). The student's visa details are displayed here, including visa ID, issue date, and expiry date.
documents.s: View Visa Details on a Student

documents.t: GrowthXP is where you do your professional learning: the courses you're asked to complete, the ones you choose for yourself, your certificates and your learning deadlines, all in one place. Find help by topic below, or use the search bar at the top.

Getting started: what GrowthXP is, signing in, finding your way around, notifications, the emails you receive, themes and signing out. My courses: your courses, the catalogue, enrolling, launching and completing courses, feedback, due dates, expiry and renewal. Learning pathways: follow courses in order towards a certification. Certificates: view, download, print and share your certificates. Calendar: your due dates, feedback deadlines, expiry and renewal dates.

My team: line managers following their team's learning. People and assignments: finding people and assigning learning. Reports: learning and compliance reports. Courses: adding and managing courses. Channels, pathways and certificates: organising courses and designing certificates. Learning rules: assigning mandatory and recommended learning automatically. Access and permissions: roles and who can do what. Organisation settings: emails, reminders and feedback rules. HR integration: connecting GrowthXP to your HR system. Troubleshooting: common problems and how to resolve them. Glossary: the terms used across GrowthXP.
Start with What is GrowthXP?, then sign in and open My courses.

To change a person's role, or the unit a role covers, give the new access first and then remove the old one. Doing it in this order means they never lose access in between. You need the Organisation administrator role. Give the new access Go to Manage → Access and permissions, click Give access, and give the person the new role, or the same role for the new unit. See Give someone access. Find the old access In Who has access, search for the person by name. Both rows are listed, each with its Where. Remove the old row Click the remove icon on the old row, then Remove access. Their account, their other access and their learning records stay. See Remove someone's access.
documents.s: Change someone's role or where it applies

documents.t: Line managers see the learning of the people who report to them, and of everyone below those people. You don't give this access; it follows the manager hierarchy. You need the Organisation administrator role. List the line managers Go to Manage → Access and permissions. The Line managers note says how many people see their team automatically. Click Show line managers. Each row says Automatic, from the manager hierarchy. Know where the hierarchy comes from A person's line manager comes from your HR system, if TMRW support has switched on line managers from HR for your organisation. Otherwise, an administrator sets it in People. You can see a person's line manager in People → View details → Employment. Change it at the source To give or take away someone's line manager access, change who reports to them. If the manager comes from HR, change it in HR and it's updated at the next sync. If it doesn't come from HR, see Set a line manager. Line managers can't change anything. They can only see and export their own team's learning. A line manager whose account is disabled loses their access, and their team's escalation emails aren't sent until they're replaced.
documents.s: Check who has line manager access

documents.t: Disable an account to stop someone signing in, for example while they're away or after they've left. Their learning records, completions and certificates are kept, and you can re-enable the account at any time. You need the Organisation administrator role, or the Learning manager role given for the whole organisation. You can't disable your own account. Find the person Go to Manage → People. To find someone who is already disabled, set Status to Disabled or All, including disabled. Choose the action Open the ⋯ menu on their row and choose Disable account or Re-enable account. You can also do this from View details → Account. Give a reason and confirm Enter a Reason. It's recorded in the audit log. Click Disable account or Re-enable account. Note: A disabled person can't sign in, gets no new learning or emails, and drops out of team views and, by default, reports. Their open mandatory learning from learning rules may be withdrawn. Know how HR sync treats it If your organisation uses the HR integration, HR sync never re-enables an account you disabled. If HR sync disabled the account because the person is no longer in HR, and you re-enable it, the next complete HR sync disables it again unless HR lists them by then. People that HR sync disabled are re-enabled automatically when they come back in HR.

Give one role to one person. You can give several roles to the same person by repeating these steps. You need the Organisation administrator role. You can only give roles whose permissions you hold yourself. Open Give access Go to Manage → Access and permissions and click Give access. Choose who Under Who, type a name or email in Person. The results include people already in the platform, people imported from HR who haven't signed in yet, and sign-in accounts from your organisation's directory. Each result says which it is: Signed in, Imported from HR — not signed in yet or Directory account only. For someone imported from HR, the platform looks for the sign-in account that uses their work email. If it finds one, it says Sign-in account found, and links that account to them when you give access. If it finds none, or more than one, choose their account in Their sign-in account. For a Directory account only result, the person is added to the platform with that account. Choose the role Under Role, pick one role. Each has a one-line summary, and What exactly can they do? lists everything it allows. Roles you can't give aren't shown, and a note says why. Choose where it applies Organisation administrator, Course manager and HR manager always cover the whole organisation. For Learning manager or Report viewer, choose Whole organisation or One unit. For one unit, choose it in Unit, then leave Include child units ticked to cover the units below it too. Give access Click Give access. The Access given message confirms it, and says whether their sign-in account was linked or they were added to the platform. If the person is already signed in, they may need to reload the page to see their new pages. If the page says Access changes are not enabled, giving access is switched off for your organisation. Contact TMRW support.

Staff categories, such as Teacher, Teaching assistant, Leadership and Support staff, group people for learning rules, filters and reports. Each category has a code, which must match the code your HR system sends, and a display name. You need the Organisation administrator role to change categories. A Learning manager given for the whole organisation can view them. Open Staff categories Go to Manage → People and click Staff categories. The Defined categories table lists each code, its display name and where it came from: From HR or Added by admin. Add or rename a category Click Add category and enter the Code and display name. To rename a category, change its display name. Codes aren't case-sensitive. A category that came from HR keeps its code exactly as HR sends it, and you can only change its name. Remove a category you no longer need Click the remove icon on its row. Categories are never removed automatically. A category HR stopped sending shows Not in the latest HR sync. If HR sends it again, the next complete HR sync adds it back. Save Click Save categories. Learning rules use the new list straight away. Check people needing review People needing review lists people whose category isn't defined here, or who have conflicting categories from HR. Learning rules don't treat them as any category until this is resolved, so add the missing code or fix the value in HR. If your organisation uses the HR integration, the categories HR sends are added automatically after each complete HR sync, named from the code. You can hold up to 500 categories.

Take one role away from a person. They keep their account, their other roles and their learning records. You need the Organisation administrator role. Find the access Go to Manage → Access and permissions. In Who has access, search for the person or filter by Role. Remove it Click the remove icon at the end of the row. The confirmation names the role and where it applies. Click Remove access. The Access removed message confirms it. Line manager rows have no remove icon. To end someone's line manager access, change who reports to them. See Set a line manager. To stop someone using the platform at all, disable their account instead. See Disable or re-enable an account.

An older role, listed as Old report viewer (no effect), gives nothing beyond what a learner has. It isn't upgraded automatically, so nobody gets access that wasn't reviewed. Replace it with Report viewer, or remove it. You need the Organisation administrator role. Find the old grants Go to Manage → Access and permissions. In Who has access, set Role to Old report viewer (no effect). Give Report viewer If the person should see reports, click the give icon on their row. Give access opens with the person and Report viewer already chosen. Change Where to one unit if they should only see part of the organisation, then click Give access. Remove the old row Click the remove icon on the Old report viewer (no effect) row, then Remove access.
documents.s: Replace an old report viewer grant

documents.t: See everyone who has been given a role, where it applies and who gave it. You need the Organisation administrator role. Open Access and permissions Go to Manage → Access and permissions. The Who has access tab opens first. Find a person or a role Type in Search by name, or choose a role in the Role filter. Each row shows the Person, their Role, Where it applies (the whole organisation, or a unit), Given by and Given on. People imported from HR who haven't signed in yet are marked Imported from HR — not signed in yet. Access given to a group shows a Group tag. Check line managers The Line managers note at the top says how many people see their team's learning automatically. Click Show line managers to list them, or choose Line managers (automatic) in the Role filter. You can't change these rows here, because they follow the manager hierarchy. Learners aren't listed at all, because everyone who signs in is a learner. Tidy up older grants A row may say Old report viewer (no effect). This role gives nothing beyond a learner. See Replace an old report viewer grant. A row that says Organisation administrator (organisation-wide grant) still works. To tidy it up, give the same person Organisation administrator, then remove the older row.

Set who a person reports to. The manager then sees that person's learning in My team, and can receive manager escalation emails about them. You need the Organisation administrator role, or the Learning manager role given for the whole organisation. Open the person's details Go to Manage → People. Find the person, open the ⋯ menu on their row and choose View details. Edit their employment details In the Employment section, click Edit employment details. If the section says Maintained by your HR integration and there's no Edit employment details button, the person's employment details and manager come from HR. If the form says Line manager maintained by your HR integration, the manager comes from HR and updates with each HR sync. Either way, change it in HR instead. Choose the manager In Line manager (optional), type at least two letters of the manager's name or email and choose them. To remove a manager, clear the field. Save Click Save changes. The manager gets line manager access to this person automatically, and loses it again if the person no longer reports to them.

GrowthXP has seven roles. A person's role decides which pages they see under Manage and what they can change there. Know the roles Role Who has it What they can do Where it applies Learner Everyone who signs in Take courses, give feedback, and see their own learning, certificates and calendar Their own records Line manager Anyone with people reporting to them See their team's learning in My team, the team's deadlines and learning reports, and export them Their direct reports and everyone below them Learning manager Given on Access and permissions Add people to organisations, assign and remove learning, and follow and export progress and reports The units they're given Report viewer Given on Access and permissions See and export learning progress and reports, and see the deadlines calendar, without changing anything The units they're given Course manager Given on Access and permissions Create, edit and publish courses, channels, learning pathways and certificate templates, choose who can see each course, and revoke awarded certificates Whole organisation HR manager Given on Access and permissions Assign learning to anyone, change due dates, manage learning rules, and run and export learning reports Whole organisation Organisation administrator Given on Access and permissions Everything, including Access and permissions, People, Notifications, Settings, the HR integration, Organisation structure and the Audit log Whole organisation Every role also includes everything a learner can do. Know which access is automatic You never give the Learner or Line manager role. Everyone who signs in is a learner. Anyone who has people reporting to them in the manager hierarchy becomes a line manager for those people, and stops being one when nobody reports to them any more. To change who someone's line manager is, change their manager in HR, or in People if the manager isn't set by HR. See Set a line manager. Know what "one unit" means You can give Learning manager and Report viewer for the Whole organisation or for One unit, such as a school. A unit includes its child units if Include child units is ticked. A learning manager also gets People employment details, line managers and account controls, but only when they're given the role for the whole organisation. Check the full detail Go to Manage → Access and permissions and open the Roles explained tab. The table lists every role as a column. ✓ means they can see and change it, View only means they can see it, and Own only means only their own records. An asterisk (*) marks access a learning manager or report viewer has only when they're given the role for the whole organisation. The table is built from the permissions the system enforces, so it's always up to date.

Narrow the calendar to the deadlines you care about, for example only overdue mandatory learning. Choose event types Open Event types and tick the types to show: Assignment due, Feedback due, Expiry and Renewal due. At least one must be ticked. Choose statuses Open Status and tick, for example, Assignment overdue or Expiry: expiring soon. Assignment upcoming means not started or in progress. Narrow by course Use Classification for Mandatory or Recommended learning, Course source for courses Created in the LMS or From HR, and Channel for courses in a channel such as Compliance. Set a date range Pick a Due from and Due to date to see only deadlines between them. If the range is in another month, click Go to and the month. Clear the filters Click Clear filters to show everything again. The calendar updates as you choose. Your filters, month and view are kept in the page address, so you can bookmark a view and open it again later.

Calendar shows your learning deadlines in a month: when learning is due, when feedback is due, when completions expire and when renewals start. It doesn't show sessions or events. Open Calendar Click Calendar in the header. It opens on this month in the Month view. Move between months Use Previous month and Next month (the arrows), or Today to come back to the current month. Read the month Days with deadlines show how many there are and up to three coloured tags with course names. The colour and label show the type: Assignment due, Feedback due, Expiry or Renewal due. Pick a day Click a day. Its deadlines are listed under the calendar, each with its type, course and status, such as Overdue, Feedback pending or Expiring soon. Open a deadline Click a deadline. The Deadline details panel shows what the date means and the course's Classification. For a renewal, Learning cycle names it as My courses does, such as Renewal 1. Go to the course Click Open course to open the course's details in My courses. Dates are calendar dates, the same in every time zone. Renewal dates appear for mandatory learning only. The calendar shows the same learning as My courses, including learning given to a group you belong to, with one due date per course. You can also move around the calendar with the keyboard: arrow keys move by day and week, Page Up and Page Down by month.

The agenda lists the month's deadlines day by day, which is quicker to scan than the grid. Switch to Agenda In Calendar, click the Agenda tab. Read the list Each day that has deadlines is listed in date order, with today marked (today). Under each day you'll see each deadline's type, course and status. Open a deadline Click a deadline to see its Deadline details, then Open course to go to the course. Change month Use Previous month, Today and Next month as in the month view. If the month has nothing, you'll see No deadlines in and the month. Click Month to go back to the grid.

Find the certificate Click Certificates in the header and find the card. Click Download Click Download (the arrow icon) on the card. You can also open the certificate page and click Download at the top; it reads Preparing… for a moment. Find the file Your browser saves an image file named Certificate, your name and the certificate number, for example Certificate_Alex_Morgan_CERT-….png. The download is a high-resolution PNG image. If you need a PDF, use Print and choose to save as PDF. Your certificate always looks the way it did when it was issued, even if your organisation changes its certificate design later.

Click Print In Certificates, click Print (the printer icon) on the certificate's card. On a certificate page, click Print at the top. Use the print dialog A new tab opens with the certificate and your browser's print dialog. Choose your printer and print, or choose Save as PDF as the destination to keep a PDF copy. If nothing happens when you click Print, your browser has probably blocked the new tab. Allow pop-ups for GrowthXP and try again.

Every certificate has its own page with a permanent address, so you can point your manager or HR to it. Open the certificate page In Certificates, click the certificate's title or Open certificate page. The page shows the certificate and its details: Learner, Course or Learning pathway, Awarded, Grade and Certificate number. Copy the link Click Copy link. A message confirms Link copied. If your browser can't copy, the message shows the link so you can copy it yourself. Send it Paste the link into an email or message to the person who needs it. Note: The link isn't public. The person must sign in to GrowthXP, and only you, your line managers and people with the Organisation administrator, Course manager or HR manager role can open it. Anyone else sees Certificate not found. To share with someone outside your organisation, send them the downloaded certificate instead. The certificate email you receive links to this same page, and your HR record may link to it too.

Open Certificates Click Certificates in the header. Along the top you'll see how many certificates you have in Total, and how many are for Courses and Pathways. Read a certificate card Certificates are listed newest first. Each card shows Certified, your grade if one was recorded, the course or pathway name, whether it's a Course or Learning pathway certificate, the date it was Awarded and its certificate number. Choose what to do Click the title or Open certificate page to see the certificate. Click Download to save it, or Print to print it. If you see No certificates yet, you haven't completed a course or pathway that awards one, or the certificate is waiting for your feedback. When you renew a course you get a new certificate, and the earlier ones stay here.

Nobody needs to approve your certificate: GrowthXP issues it as soon as you meet the course's conditions. Check that the course awards one In the course details, Certificate and the message "Completing this course earns you a certificate." show that it does. Not every course awards a certificate. Complete the course Finish the course. If it has a pass mark, your score must reach it. A course that just says you've passed counts. Submit feedback if it's required If the feedback form says "Submit your feedback to receive your certificate.", the certificate waits for your feedback. Submit it, even if it's late, and the certificate is issued straight away. Find it The certificate appears in Certificates, and you may get an email with a link to it. For a learning pathway, you receive its certificate when you've completed every course in it, with any required feedback, and met the pathway's average score if it has one. Each renewal of a course earns a new certificate. Completions recorded in HR don't get a certificate in GrowthXP; complete the course in GrowthXP if you need one.

A channel shows learners the courses you put in it. A course can be in more than one channel. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the channel's courses In Manage ▸ Channels, click the Courses icon at the end of the channel's row. The window lists the courses already in it. Add a course Under Course, search for and choose a course, then click Add. Remove a course Click Remove next to a course to take it out of the channel. The course itself isn't changed. Close the window Changes save as you make them. The Courses column on the Channels list shows the new count. You can also choose a course's channels in its Edit details window.

You build a pathway from tiers: learners work through the courses in the first tier, then the next. You can also link courses as prerequisites. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the pathway In Manage ▸ Learning pathways, click the pathway's card. The editor shows the courses and tiers, for example "4 courses · 2 tiers". Each course card shows the course's duration, if it has one. Add courses Click Add course at the end of a tier, or Add new tier under the last tier. Choose a Course and click Add. If Courses not loaded appears, click Try again: you can't add courses until the course list loads. Arrange the courses Each course card has controls to Move up a tier, Move down a tier, Move left, Move right, Move to own tier and Remove. Link prerequisites Drag the handle on a course (Drag to link prerequisite) onto a course in the next tier. The card shows how many prerequisites it has. Click a link to delete it. Save Click Save changes. Nothing is saved until you do. If the changes can't be saved, Changes not saved appears above the buttons with the reason, and your changes stay in the editor. Learners only see a pathway when they can see every course in it, so check each course's audience.

A certificate template sets the look and wording of the certificates learners receive. You attach templates to courses and learning pathways. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open Certificates Click Manage in the header, then Certificates under Content, and stay on the Templates tab. If there are no templates yet, the page says No certificate templates yet. Start a template Click Create template. It's in the middle of the page when there are no templates, and in the table's toolbar when there are. Set the look Enter the Template name and choose the Orientation: Landscape or Portrait. Drop a Company logo, and choose the Primary colour, Secondary colour and Background colour. The contrast checks under the colours tell you whether the text will be easy to read. Write the text Enter the Title text and Body text. In the body you can use {userName}, {courseName}, {date}, {grade} and {certNumber}, which are filled in for each learner. Add Certified by, Certifier name and Footer text. Choose whether to Include grade, Include date and Include course name. Check and save Check the Live preview, which uses sample details. Turn on Set as default to make it your default template. Click Save template.

Channels group courses by topic, such as "Compliance", so learners can browse them on Courses. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open Channels Click Manage in the header, then Channels under Content. If there are none yet, the page says "No channels yet. Create one to organise your content." Enter the details Click Create channel at the top of the page. In Create topic channel, enter the Channel name and a Description. Create it Click Create. The channel appears in the list. Next, add courses to it. You can rename it later. A channel only groups courses for browsing. To make learning mandatory for people, assign it or use a learning rule.

A learning pathway is an ordered set of courses, such as an induction programme, with an optional certificate at the end. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open Learning pathways Click Manage in the header, then Learning pathways under Content. Existing pathways show as cards. If there are none yet, the page says No pathways yet. If it says Pathways not loaded, click Try again. Create the pathway Click New pathway. In Create new pathway, enter the Title, a Description, and a Certification (optional): the name of what learners achieve, such as "Inducted staff member". Create it Click Create. The pathway opens in the editor, ready for you to add courses. If it can't be created, Pathway not created says why and the window keeps what you typed.

You can delete a channel you no longer need. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Choose Delete In Manage ▸ Channels, click the Delete icon at the end of the channel's row. Confirm Click Delete channel. The courses in the channel aren't deleted; they just no longer appear under that channel. You can't undo this.

You can change a certificate template's look and wording, or delete it. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the template In Manage ▸ Certificates ▸ Templates, find the template, using Search templates if you need to, and click its Edit icon. Make your changes In Edit certificate template, change any field and check the Live preview. Click Save template. Know what changes Certificates issued from now on use the new version. Certificates already issued keep the version they were issued with, so learners' existing certificates don't change. Delete a template Click the template's Delete icon, then Delete template. Certificates already awarded from it are kept. You can't undo this. Check which courses and pathways use it first, and choose another template for them.

You can rename a channel or change its description. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the channel In Manage ▸ Channels, click the Edit icon at the end of the channel's row. Change the details In Edit channel, change the Channel name, the Description, or both. A channel always needs a name. Save Click Save changes. It becomes available once you've changed something. The channel keeps its courses, and learners see the new name on Courses. If the change can't be saved, Channel not saved says why and the window stays open with what you typed.

You can change a pathway's details and certificate, or delete it. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the details In Manage ▸ Learning pathways, click the pathway's card, then Edit details. Change the details In Edit pathway details, change the Title, Description, Certification and Colour. Add a certificate Under Certificate template, choose the template to award automatically when a learner completes the pathway. Under Minimum grade required (%), enter the average grade needed across its courses, or leave it at 0. A pathway certificate also needs each course's feedback rule to be met. Save Click Apply, then Save changes in the editor. Delete the pathway Click Delete pathway at the bottom of the editor, then Delete pathway again in the confirmation. If it can't be deleted, Pathway not deleted says why and the pathway stays open. Note: Learners no longer see a deleted pathway. Its courses, and pathway certificates already awarded, are kept. This can't be undone.
documents.s: Edit or delete a learning pathway

documents.t: The Awarded certificates tab lists every certificate learners have received. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role.
