Open Awarded certificates In Manage ▸ Certificates, click the Awarded certificates tab. Find a certificate Type a learner's name or a certificate number in Search learners and certificates, and use Source to choose a course or pathway. The table shows the Learner, Course / Pathway, Certificate #, Grade and the date it was Awarded. Open a certificate Click Open certificate page to view, print or download it. Issue missing certificates Certificates are issued automatically when learners complete a course or pathway that has a template. If some seem to be missing, for example after you attached a template to a course, click Check certificates. The message says how many were awarded, or No missing certificates found. Revoke a certificate Click Revoke on the certificate's row, then Revoke certificate. Note: The learner loses the certificate and can no longer download it. You can't undo this.

You add a course by uploading its SCORM package, a .zip file, and describing it. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Start adding In Manage ▸ Courses, click Add course. The window has two steps: Package and Details. Upload the package Drag the SCORM .zip file onto Course package, or click to browse. GrowthXP reads the package and fills in the Course title; change it if you need to. Choose who can see it Under Course audience, choose Everyone in the organisation or Selected organisation scopes. Under Course visibility, choose whether everyone in the audience can find it, or only people who are assigned it. See Choose who can see a course. You can also set Offering dates for your HR system. Upload and continue Click Upload and continue. When the package is accepted, the Details step opens. Processing carries on in the background while you work. Add the details Add a Description, Estimated duration (minutes), SCORM version, Tags, Skills and Channels. Under Certificate, choose a Certificate template and a Minimum grade required (%). Set an Expiry date if the course should stop being available on a date. Save the course Click Save course, or Finish later to add the details another time. The new course is a draft. Once its status is Draft, publish it with Mark ready: see Publish or unpublish a course.

Training materials are files learners can download from a course, such as handouts or policies. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the course In Manage ▸ Courses, open the row menu and choose Edit details, then scroll to Training materials. Add a file Click Add material. Drop a PDF, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, image, text or CSV file of up to 50 MB. Enter a Name, or leave it blank to use the file name, and a Purpose (optional). Click Upload material. Training materials save straight away, separately from Save changes. Wait for the malware check A new file shows Checking for malware. Click Check malware status to update it. Learners can download it once it shows Ready. A file marked Malware found can never be downloaded. Update or remove a file Open a material's menu to Download it, Upload new version, Edit details or Remove it. Learners only get the current version; earlier versions stay listed under Earlier versions for you. Files that could contain code, such as macro-enabled Office files, web pages, scripts and archives, are refused.

You can let learners add a course to their own learning from the catalogue. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the course In Manage ▸ Courses, open the row menu and choose Edit details. Turn on self-enrolment Turn on Allow self-enrolment. Learners in the course audience can then enrol themselves from the catalogue, and the course appears in their My courses as recommended learning. With it off, learners can still open the course from the catalogue, but only an assignment adds it to My courses. Check it's available Self-enrolment isn't available when Course visibility is Assigned learners in the course audience, because only assigned learners can see the course. Learners can only enrol in a published course that hasn't expired. Save Click Save changes. For courses from HR, the setting starts with HR's value until you change it here.

A course can award a certificate when learners complete it, optionally only above a grade. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the course In Manage ▸ Courses, open the row menu and choose Edit details. Choose the template Under Certificate, choose a Certificate template. Choose None for no certificate. To create a template, see Create a certificate template. Set the pass mark Under Minimum grade required (%), enter the score a learner needs for the certificate. Leave it at 0 for no grade requirement. The SCORM package decides when the course is complete; the grade only decides the certificate. Save Click Save changes. Certificates are issued automatically for each completion that meets the rule, and for renewals too. If your organisation requires course feedback first, the certificate waits for it: see Require feedback before a certificate. Nobody can award a certificate by hand.
documents.s: Attach a certificate to a course

documents.t: Every SCORM package is checked for malware and unpacked before learners can use it. You can follow its progress on the Courses page. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Find the course In Manage ▸ Courses, open the All tab. The list updates every few seconds while a course is processing. Read the status Uploaded - queued means the package arrived and is waiting. Scanning for malware and Extracting package follow. Draft means it's processed and ready for you to publish. Deal with a failed upload Blocked - malware means the scan found malware and the package was removed. Processing failed means the package couldn't be used. Expand the row and read Status detail for the reason. Common reasons are a file that isn't a SCORM .zip, unsafe file paths, or a package that's too large (more than 20,000 files or 2 GB unpacked). Fix the package and upload it again.

Two settings decide who can find and open a course: its audience, and whether they also need to be assigned it. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the course In Manage ▸ Courses, open the row menu and choose Edit details. You also set these when you add a course. Set the audience Under Course audience, choose Everyone in the organisation, or Selected organisation scopes to limit it. For selected scopes, choose up to 50 organisations under Organisation scopes. Their child organisations are included unless you tick Direct members only next to one. People without an organisation belong to the top of your organisation. Set the visibility Under Course visibility, choose Everyone in the course audience so everyone in the audience can find and open the course without an assignment. Choose Assigned learners in the course audience so only people who are assigned it can see it. With that choice, removing someone's last assignment removes their access. Save Click Save changes. An assignment never overrides the audience: someone outside it can't be assigned the course, and learning rules and bulk assignment skip them. Check the audience before you assign a course widely.
documents.s: Choose who can see a course

documents.t: Deleting removes a course and its package for everyone. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Choose Delete course In Manage ▸ Courses, open the course's row menu and choose Delete course. Confirm Read the message and click Delete course. Note: Deleting can't be undone. Learners can no longer open the course, but their records, completions and certificates are kept. To hide a course without deleting it, use Move to draft or set an Expiry date instead.

You can change how a course is described and organised at any time. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open Edit course In Manage ▸ Courses, open the row menu and choose Edit details. Edit course opens with the course's status, format and version at the top. Change the description Edit the Course title and Description (up to 500 characters), the Estimated duration (minutes) and the SCORM version. Organise it Under Tags, choose existing tags or type one in Add a tag. Tags can be used by learning rules to assign every course with a tag. Choose Skills and Channels; channels decide where learners find the course on Courses. Change the thumbnail Under Thumbnail, drop a JPEG, PNG or WebP image of up to 2 MB, or choose a Default colour. Save Click Save changes. The same window also holds the audience, self-enrolment, certificate, training materials, expiry and validity settings, each covered on its own page in this section. Training materials save on their own.

The Courses page in Manage lists every course in your catalogue, including drafts learners can't see. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open Courses Click Manage in the header, then Courses under Content. Choose a tab Draft lists courses that aren't published yet, Ready lists published courses, and All lists everything, including courses still processing. Each tab shows its count. Search and filter Type in Search courses. Under Source, choose From HR or Created in the LMS. On the All tab you can also filter by Status. Read a row Each row shows the Course title, with "v2" (or later) when it has newer versions and tags such as From HR, In person or Expired. It also shows Duration, Format (SCORM 1.2 or SCORM 2004) and when it was Added. See the details Click the arrow at the start of a row to expand it. You'll see the description, expiry, certificate rule, channels, tags, skills, versions and metadata such as who created and last uploaded it, and any Status detail. Preview or act on the course Click the Preview icon to open a ready course as a learner would. Open the row menu for Edit details, Replace or add a version, Mark ready or Move to draft, and Delete course.

A course is a draft until you publish it. Learners can only launch ready courses. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Publish a draft In Manage ▸ Courses, open the Draft tab. Open the course's row menu and choose Mark ready. A message confirms "Course is ready", and the course moves to the Ready tab. Unpublish a course On the Ready tab, open the row menu and choose Move to draft. Learners can no longer launch it, and learning rules stop assigning it. Existing assignments and records stay. If you can't publish A course needs a processed SCORM package before it can be marked ready. Courses created from HR have no package until you add one with Replace or add a version. A course that's still processing can't be published or unpublished until it finishes.

When a course's content changes, upload a new SCORM package to the same course. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open Update course In Manage ▸ Courses, open the row menu and choose Replace or add a version. Choose the kind of update Under What kind of update is this?, choose Replace — overwrite the existing package, for a fix or a correction, or New version — archive the old package, for a major update. Nothing is chosen for you. Upload the package Add a Note (optional) to say what changed, then drop the new .zip file onto Course package. Click Replace course or Add version. Check the result The new package is checked for malware before learners get it. If malware is found, the course keeps its previous package. Earlier packages are listed under Version history in Edit details, and the course list shows the version number.
documents.s: Replace or add a course version

documents.t: You can hold a course's certificate until the learner gives feedback on the course. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the course In Manage ▸ Courses, open the row menu and choose Edit details. The course needs a certificate template. Choose the feedback rule Under Certificate, set Feedback before certificate. Use the customer default follows your organisation's setting, which an organisation administrator sets in Manage ▸ Settings ▸ Course feedback (off unless they turn it on). Required holds this course's certificate until the learner submits valid feedback. Not required issues it on completion. Save Click Save changes. The rule also applies to a learning pathway certificate that includes this course. Late feedback still counts. The change applies to certificates not yet issued.

A course expiry date retires the course itself on a date, for example when its content goes out of date. It's different from how long a learner's completion is valid. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the course In Manage ▸ Courses, open the row menu and choose Edit details. Set the date Choose the Expiry date. Click Clear expiry to remove it. Save Click Save changes. From that date the course list tags it Expired, learners can't launch it, learning rules stop assigning it and learners can't enrol in it. To set how long completions stay valid instead, see Set how long a completion is valid.

Offering dates are the start and end of a course offering in your HR system. They only matter if your organisation sends courses to HR. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the course In Manage ▸ Courses, open the row menu and choose Edit details. You can also set them when you add a course. Enter the dates Under Offering dates, enter the Offering start date and time and Offering end date and time. You enter them in your own time zone: the note above the fields names it, and each label shows its short name, such as (GMT). Everyone sees the dates in their own time zone. The dates don't change who can open the course or when it expires. Check whether HR needs them If the message Add offering dates to send this course to HR appears, the HR course sync skips the course until it has dates. Learners can still use it. Save Click Save changes. Leave both dates blank for an unscheduled course, or click Clear offering dates. Once a course may have been sent to HR, you can replace its dates but not clear them. If a time doesn't exist in your time zone because the clocks go forward that night, the field asks you to choose another time.

Completion validity sets how long a learner's completion counts before it expires and needs renewing. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the course In Manage ▸ Courses, open the row menu and choose Edit details. Choose the validity Under Completion validity, choose: Use the customer default: mandatory learning uses your organisation's default (12 months unless changed); other completions never expire. Expires after a number of months, then enter Months valid from 1 to 120. Months count from the completion date; a completion on 29 February expires on 28 February. Never expires: completions never need renewing. Save Click Save changes. The change applies to completions recorded from now on; existing completions keep their expiry date. A learning rule can set its own validity for the courses it assigns. Expiring mandatory learning is renewed through learning rules: see Run a renewal check.
documents.s: Set how long a completion is valid

documents.t: GrowthXP can import courses from your HR system, such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, so the two catalogues agree. You need the Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Importing courses from HR is off unless TMRW support turns it on for your organisation. Find courses from HR In Manage ▸ Courses, set Source to From HR. Courses that came from HR have a From HR tag. A new HR course arrives as an unpublished draft with no content. Add the content Open the row menu and choose Replace or add a version to upload its SCORM package. Set it up and publish it Choose Edit details to set the audience, visibility and certificate, then Mark ready to publish it. Know what HR keeps in step The title, description and self-enrolment setting come from HR. If only HR changed them since the last sync, HR's values are taken. If both sides changed, GrowthXP keeps its own value and shows the conflict to administrators in Manage ▸ Settings ▸ Synchronisation. A course cancelled or removed in HR is never deleted here. Know about in-person courses HR courses with a classroom or location are tagged In person and imported as drafts. In-person delivery isn't supported in this version. Use HR course types in rules Learning rules can assign every course with a given HR course type. See Choose courses by tag or HR course type.

Switch GrowthXP between light and dark to suit your screen and surroundings. Open the theme menu Click the Change theme icon in the header, next to the bell. It shows a sun in the light themes and a moon in the dark ones. Choose a theme Choose Light, Light grey, Dark grey or Dark. A tick marks the one you're using. The theme changes straight away and is remembered in this browser, so set it again on another computer. The header bar stays dark in every theme.

The bell in the header gathers the things you need to act on in your learning. Open the bell Click the Notifications bell. A red number on it shows how many items you haven't read yet (it reads 9+ above nine). The Notifications panel opens, with items under Today and Previous. Read the items Overdue: mandatory learning you haven't finished was due on the date shown. Recommended learning is never overdue. Due soon: a course is due within the next seven days. Feedback required: submit feedback on a course you've finished to receive its certificate. Feedback needed: share your feedback on a course you've finished. The most pressing items come first. Act on an item Click an item. It's marked as read and takes you to the thing it's about: the course's details for due dates, or the Course feedback form for feedback. Clear the count Click Mark all as read. When there's nothing left, the panel says You are all caught up. Notifications are worked out from your courses each time GrowthXP loads, and what you've read is remembered in this browser only. On another computer or browser, items you've already read show as unread again. Emails are separate; see Emails you receive about your learning.

The dark header bar sits across the top of every page in GrowthXP. The main links Click GrowthXP (far left) to return to My courses, your home page. Next to it are My courses, Courses, Learning pathways, Certificates and Calendar. If your role includes managing or reporting on learning, you'll also see Manage. The icons on the right Your name comes first, then the Notifications bell, the Change theme icon (a sun or a moon) and Sign out. On a smaller screen When the window is narrow, the links move into a menu. Click the menu icon at the left of the header to open it. Inside a course While a course is open, the header shows only the course title and a Close course button. Close the course to get the links back. Your progress is saved when you close it.

GrowthXP uses your organisation's Microsoft account, the same one you use for email. There's no separate GrowthXP password. Click Sign in Open GrowthXP and click Sign in. The hint underneath reads Use your organisation login. Choose your account Microsoft's account picker opens. Choose your organisation account, or enter it, and complete Microsoft's sign-in, including any verification your organisation uses. Wait for your learning to load GrowthXP shows Welcome to tmrw while it loads your learning, then opens on My courses. If GrowthXP shows a message instead Your organisation isn’t licensed: GrowthXP isn't available for the organisation of the account you used. Click Sign in with another account if you have a different work account, or ask your administrator. Your account has been disabled: you can't use GrowthXP at the moment, for example because you no longer appear in your organisation's HR system. Your learning records are kept. Contact your administrator. We couldn’t sign you in or We couldn’t verify your access: click Try again. If it keeps happening, contact your IT support team.

Close any open course If you're in a course, click Close course first. Your progress is saved when the course closes. Click Sign out Click Sign out, the icon at the far right of the header. GrowthXP signs you out through Microsoft and returns to the sign-in page. On a shared computer, also close the browser when you've finished.

GrowthXP sends emails about your learning from your organisation's sender name. Your organisation chooses which ones are sent and can change their wording, so yours may differ from the defaults below. When learning is assigned to you New learning assigned: (course) arrives when a course is assigned to you personally, with an Open course button. You don't get it for courses you enrol in yourself, or for learning given to a whole group. Before and after the due date Learning reminder: (course) arrives before learning is due, by default 14 days and 3 days before. If mandatory learning becomes overdue, you get an overdue notice, by default every 7 days, up to 4 times. Recommended learning is never overdue, so it never gets overdue notices. If your organisation has turned on manager escalation, your line manager is also told when mandatory learning is still overdue after a set number of notices. When you finish Course completed: (course) confirms a completion. If the course awards a certificate, Your certificate: (course) follows, with a View certificate button that opens the certificate page. When learning needs renewing Renewal due: (course) arrives when learning that's about to expire is assigned to you again, with the new due date. When feedback is due If your organisation sets a deadline for course feedback, Feedback due: (course) reminds you before the deadline (by default 3 days and 1 day before) and once afterwards, with a Give feedback button. Reminder and overdue emails are sent once a day, only when your organisation has scheduled reminders switched on. If you aren't getting emails you expect, check your junk folder, then ask your organisation administrator. Administrators set these emails up in Choose which learner emails are sent.
documents.s: Emails you receive about your learning

documents.t: Every page about your own learning is the same for everyone. Extra areas appear only if your role needs them. Everyone is a learner As soon as you sign in, you're a Learner. You can see My courses, Courses, Learning pathways, Certificates, Calendar and your notifications. You see only your own learning. Managers and administrators also see Manage Manage appears in the header when you have another role as well: Line manager is given automatically when someone reports to you. It shows your team's learning. Learning manager and Report viewer cover the people in particular schools or units. Course manager, HR manager and Organisation administrator cover the whole organisation. Inside Manage, the side menu lists only the areas your role can use. If something is missing If you expect to see Manage, or an area inside it, ask your organisation administrator to check your access. A line manager's access follows the reporting lines from HR, so a change of manager appears after the next HR sync. For what each role can do, see Understand the roles.
documents.s: What you see depends on your role

documents.t: GrowthXP is your organisation's learning platform. It holds the training and professional development courses you're asked to complete, and the ones you can choose for yourself. It keeps track of your progress, due dates, certificates and when your learning needs renewing. Your learning in one place My courses is your home page. It lists every course you've been given, and every course you've started, with your progress and due dates. Courses are online modules that play inside GrowthXP and save your place as you go. Courses you can choose Courses is the catalogue of everything offered to you, grouped into channels such as Compliance. Some courses let you enrol yourself. Mandatory and recommended learning Learning you're given is either Mandatory (you must complete it by its due date, and you'll be reminded) or Recommended (worth doing, but never overdue). Some mandatory learning expires after a set time, such as 12 months, and is given to you again before it runs out. Pathways, certificates and deadlines Learning pathways set courses in an order that leads to a certification. Certificates holds the certificates you earn, ready to download or print. Calendar shows every learning due date, feedback date, expiry and renewal in a month view. Connected to HR GrowthXP can connect to your organisation's HR system, such as Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations. When it does, your organisation, line manager and some of your learning come from HR, and your progress can be sent back to your HR record. Managers and administrators If you manage people or run learning for your organisation, you'll also see Manage in the header. What you can do there depends on your role.
Terms used across GrowthXP and this guide.
The Manage page where organisation administrators see who has which role (Who has access), give and remove roles (Give access), and check what each role can do (Roles explained).

Where an assignment came from: a learning rule, an administrator or manager, a bulk assignment, HR, or the learner enrolling themselves. When several sources require the same learning, it shows how many.
A course or pathway given to a person, with a classification and, usually, a due date. A person has one current assignment per course, whatever its sources.
The schools or organisations whose people can see a course. A course can be open to everyone, or only to chosen units and the units below them.
The record of administrative actions and changes: who did what, to what, and when. Read only; the latest 500 entries are shown.
Applying a new learning rule to people who already matched it before the rule was activated, after previewing who it would assign.
Assigning a course to everyone in one or more organisations at once. It runs in the background, and its results are kept in Bulk assignment history.
Proof of completion, issued automatically when a learner completes a course that has a certificate, or after they give feedback if feedback is required. Each certificate has its own shareable page.
The design a certificate is printed from. Each edit creates a new version, and issued certificates keep the version they were issued with.
A collection of courses on a theme, such as Compliance, that learners browse in Courses.

Whether an assignment is Mandatory or Recommended. Classification belongs to the assignment or the learning rule, not the course, so the same course can be mandatory for some people and recommended for others. Older learning saved before classification existed shows Not set.
Whether a completion was recorded in the platform or in HR. Exports show it as LMS or HR record.

A role for people who create, edit and publish courses, channels, learning pathways and certificate templates, choose who can see each course, and revoke awarded certificates. Covers the whole organisation.
One round of a piece of learning that must be renewed. When a completion is about to expire, the next cycle is assigned, with its own due date. Earlier cycles stay in the person's training history.
The Manage calendar of assignment, feedback, expiry and renewal dates for the people you can see. Learners have their own Calendar.

An account that can't sign in. Disabled people get no new learning or emails, but their learning records, completions and certificates are kept. Disabled by an administrator or by the HR sync, and never deleted.
When an assignment should be completed. Mandatory learning past its due date is Overdue. Recommended learning is never overdue.
See Manager escalation.
Completed learning whose validity has ended. Mandatory learning that has expired needs to be completed again.
Completed learning that will expire within the organisation's warning period, usually 30 days.
The date a completion stops being valid, worked out from the completion date and the validity period. Not to be confused with a course's own end date, after which the course is no longer available.
Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations, the first HR system the HR integration connects to.
How many days after completion course feedback is due. Late feedback is still accepted and marked as late.
A tag on something that came from your HR system, such as a course draft, a staff category or an organisation membership. Things from HR are changed in HR, not in the platform.
Days added to a learning rule's starting date to give the due date. For example, a new joiner's employment start date plus 30 days.
The name your HR learning record uses for a course in a legal entity. Mapped to a platform course so learner status and completions can be matched.
The connection between the platform and your HR system that syncs people, organisations, courses, enrolments and learning records.
A role for people who assign learning to anyone, change due dates, manage learning rules, and run and export learning reports. Covers the whole organisation.
A person whose account is matched to a worker in HR. Only HR-linked people are disabled by the HR sync when they leave HR.
The rules the user sync follows: active workers only, occupied current positions, temporary positions left out, and placement by current employment. Set with TMRW support.
A tool in Synchronisation for finding one person in HR, seeing what the next sync will do to them, and importing a missing person straight away.
Everyone who signs in. Learners take courses, give feedback, and see their own learning, certificates and calendar.
See Assignment. Learning assignments is also the Manage page that lists who has which learning.
A role for people who add people to organisations, assign and remove learning, and follow and export progress and reports for the units they're given.
An ordered set of courses, sometimes with prerequisites, that learners follow towards a goal.

A rule that assigns courses automatically, as mandatory or recommended, to everyone who matches conditions such as organisation, staff category or length of service. Rules re-check people when their details change.
A company or school in your HR system. Imported from HR and linked to a unit in the organisation structure, so people are placed in the right unit.
Someone with people reporting to them. Line managers see their team's learning automatically, for their direct reports and everyone below them. This role is never given by hand.
The people a line manager can see: their direct reports and everyone below them in the manager hierarchy.
Learning a person must complete by its due date. Mandatory learning can become overdue, is reminded and escalated, and counts towards compliance. When sources disagree, mandatory wins.
An optional email to a person's line manager when their mandatory learning is still overdue after a set number of delivered overdue reminders. Off by default.
A person's place in an organisation unit. Memberships come from HR (From HR) or are added by an administrator (Added by admin).
A person the HR sync placed in a different legal entity. Their old HR memberships end and new ones begin.
The classification shown for older learning saved before mandatory and recommended existed. It's never guessed.
A person imported from HR who hasn't signed in for the first time. They can be given learning, memberships and roles before they sign in.
The whole customer, or one unit in its structure, such as a trust, a group of schools or a school. "Whole organisation" means everyone.
The role that runs the whole platform: courses, learning, people, access, notifications, settings and the HR integration.
The tree of units, such as groups and schools, used to scope access, reports and learning rules.
Mandatory learning past its due date and not completed. Recommended learning is never overdue.
See Learning pathway.
People whose staff category isn't defined, or who have conflicting categories from HR. Learning rules don't treat them as any category until it's resolved.
Learning a person is encouraged to complete. It's never overdue and isn't escalated, and it only has a due date if one is set.
A completion imported from your HR system for learning completed outside the platform. It counts as completed, but there's no certificate or evidence in the platform.
Assigning learning again before its completion expires, as the next cycle. The renewal is assigned a set number of days before expiry (the renewal lead time) and is due on the expiry date.
A role for people who see and export learning progress and reports, and see the deadlines calendar, for the units they're given, without changing anything.
The share of HR-linked people (5% by default) or number of people (200 by default) above which a user sync stops for review before disabling anyone.
The tab on Access and permissions that shows what each role can do, built from the permissions the platform enforces.
Where a role applies: the whole organisation, or one unit with or without its child units. Also the organisation you choose to look at in reports and calendars.
The standard format for e-learning packages. Courses are uploaded as SCORM packages and play in the platform.
A learner enrolling themselves in a published course that allows it. Self-enrolled learning is recommended.
A group such as Teacher, Teaching assistant, Leadership or Support staff, used by learning rules, filters and reports. Each has a code that matches your HR system.
The list of HR syncs, scheduled and manual, with what each changed. The people in each user sync are kept for 7 days or while it's one of the latest 7 runs.
One place in the organisation structure, such as a school. Roles, reports and learning rules can be limited to a unit, with or without the units below it.
The HR sync that creates and updates people from HR, places them in the right units, and disables people no longer in HR.
How long a completion stays valid, for example 12 months. Set on the course or the learning rule, with an organisation default for mandatory learning. Some learning never expires.
Everyone in your organisation. Organisation administrator, Course manager and HR manager always cover the whole organisation; Learning manager and Report viewer can too.

See every HR sync, scheduled or manual, newest first: when it ran, whether it worked, and what it changed. You need the Organisation administrator role. Open History Go to Manage → Settings → Synchronisation and open History. Sync history lists recent syncs with Requested, Status, Trigger, Direction (for example Users from HR or Courses to HR) and Result. Times are in your own time zone, with its short name. Filter Choose a Trigger: All syncs, Manual (including individual imports), Scheduled, Course changes or Not recorded. Click Reload sync history to refresh. Look at a run Expand a row for its details. A user sync shows its Stage, Trigger, the counts (Created, Updated, Moved, Re-enabled, Unchanged, Not imported, Disabled), the import rules it applied, and the Disable decision with who made it. Elapsed since request is how long the run took from start to finish, including any pauses or time waiting for review. Other syncs show their Processing time. A failed run shows its Reason. See the people in a user sync Click View run on a user sync to open its results and search the people it read and changed. To save space, these details are kept for 7 days, or for as long as the run is one of your latest 7 user syncs, whichever is longer. After that, the run shows Details removed after 7 days, and its counts stay in the history.

Connect GrowthXP to your Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations environment. Have the details from What you need to connect Dynamics 365 ready. You need the Organisation administrator role. Open the HR connection Go to Manage → Settings. The HR connection tab opens first, with Dynamics F&O chosen under HR integration. If it says No HR integrations available, contact TMRW support. Enter the connection details Fill in Connection name, Environment (Development, UAT or Production), Environment ID, Finance and Operations URL, Microsoft Entra tenant ID and Application client ID. Click Save connection. Add a certificate Under Set up application authentication, click Add certificate. The new certificate appears in the Certificates list as Active. Click Download on it to save the public .cer file. Upload it to Microsoft Entra Click Open Microsoft Entra, open the app registration that matches your Application client ID, then choose Certificates & secrets → Certificates → Upload certificate and upload the file. You may need your Entra administrator for this step. Test the connection Click Test connection. The Connection test lists Microsoft Entra authentication and each F&O data check, such as Legal entities, Staff positions, Course catalogue and Course participants. Each should say Passed, and the connection tag changes to Connected. A Failed row shows the reason. Usually the certificate isn't uploaded yet, or the service user can't read that data entity in F&O. Ask for your syncs to be switched on A connected environment doesn't sync anything until TMRW support switches on the syncs you want. See Switch on each HR sync. If you later change the environment, tenant, client ID or certificate, syncing stops until the connection passes a new test.

The HR integration keeps GrowthXP and your HR system in step, so nobody has to type staff, schools or course records in twice. The first HR system supported is Microsoft Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations (F&O). The integration is set up and run by your Organisation administrator, with TMRW support switching on each part for your organisation. Know what comes from HR What What the platform does with it Legal entities Copies your companies and schools, so you can place them in your organisation structure People and positions Creates an account for each active worker in an occupied position, and keeps their name, work email, job title, department and school up to date Employments Places each person in the legal entities they're currently employed by, and moves them when HR moves them Line managers Sets who reports to whom, which gives line managers their team automatically Staff categories Records each person's category, such as Teacher or Support staff, and adds new categories automatically Courses Brings courses created in HR in as unpublished drafts, ready for content Course participants Assigns the course to people registered on it in HR Completions recorded in HR Marks courses people completed outside the platform as completed, tagged Recorded in HR Know what goes back to HR What What HR receives Courses Courses created in the platform, with their title, description and offering dates Course participants Assignments made in the platform, once your HR team has approved writes to the participant record Learner status Each learner's status (not started, in progress or completed), whether the learning is mandatory or recommended, the assigned and due dates, and a link to the course, feedback form or certificate Know who owns what HR is the source of truth for people's HR details and their placement. Anything the platform owns stays in the platform: memberships an administrator adds, roles, learning, progress and certificates. HR sync never deletes anyone. People who leave HR are disabled and keep their learning records, and they're re-enabled automatically if they come back. See Who the user sync imports. Know the safeguards If a user sync would disable more than a set share of your people, it stops before disabling anyone and waits for an administrator. See Review people before they're disabled. When a course changed on both sides, the platform keeps its own version and lists the difference for you to review. The platform reads only the data it needs, signs in to F&O with a certificate rather than a password, and keeps the private key with TMRW. Every sync is recorded in Sync history, and the details of each user sync are kept for 7 days or for the latest 7 runs. Know when it runs TMRW support sets how often each sync runs: hourly, every 6 hours, daily or weekly, at a time that suits you. Administrators can also run any available sync by hand. See When HR syncs run. Get started Check What you need to connect Dynamics 365. Connect to Dynamics 365. Ask TMRW support to switch on the syncs you want. See Switch on each HR sync. Import legal entities and link them to your organisation structure. Run a user sync.

Some learning is completed outside the platform and recorded in HR. Importing these completions means HR and the platform agree about who has completed what. You need the Organisation administrator role. Know what's imported Each course HR records as completed is marked completed in the platform. Open learning is completed, and a completed record is added if the person didn't have the course. The completion date is the end date in HR. The completion counts for validity, expiry and renewals like any other. Each one is tagged Recorded in HR, which means it was completed outside the platform, with no certificate and no evidence in the platform. No feedback is asked for and no email is sent. Learning already completed in the platform is never changed, and nothing is ever marked as not completed. If the learner later completes the course in the platform, that completion replaces the HR record. Map the course titles HR names courses by title. Each course needs an HR course title mapping in each legal entity. See Map HR course titles. Completions for unmapped titles are skipped, with the reason. Run the import Go to Manage → Settings → Synchronisation → Courses. On Completions from HR, click Preview sync: completions from HR to see what would change, then Sync now: completions from HR. It also runs with the scheduled course sync, after courses and participants. Check the results Each row says what happened: Mark completed, Record completion, Already completed or Not imported, with a reason, such as No verified HR identity matches this person.

Copy your companies and schools from HR, so you can place them in your organisation structure. Importing doesn't create schools or change anyone's account. It only makes the legal entities available to link. You need the Organisation administrator role. Open the People sub-tab Go to Manage → Settings → Synchronisation and open People. Run the import On the Legal entities row, click Sync now: legal entities. To stop it part-way, click Pause import; click Resume import to carry on from where it stopped. Check the result The Latest result shows how many legal entities were found, new, updated and unchanged. Updated means a legal entity's name or active state changed in HR. Link them to your structure Go to Manage → Organisation structure and link each legal entity to the right place. See Link legal entities to an organisation. Do this before your first user sync, so people are placed in the right schools. After the first import, legal entities are refreshed automatically if TMRW support has scheduled it.

Find one person in HR to see how the import rules apply to them, or to bring a new starter in now instead of waiting for the next full sync. You need the Organisation administrator role. Search HR Go to Manage → Settings → Synchronisation → People and find Individual HR lookup. Enter a name or personnel number in Name or personnel number (at least 2 characters) and click Search HR. For an exact personnel number, click Check number instead. This also finds people who don't appear in the search. Check the person In the results, click the check icon on the person's row. The check shows their Account, Current organisation, HR status, where their legal entities come from, and the Proposed result: for example Create account, No change, Move to new legal entities, Re-enable account or Not imported with the reason. Import a missing person If they don't have an account yet and can be imported, click Import user. Their account is created now, without waiting for the next sync. Import user only creates missing accounts. Changes to existing people are made by the next full user sync. You can't import someone while a user sync is running, paused or waiting for review. Searching and checking still work.
documents.s: Look up a person in HR

documents.t: Your HR learning record names courses by title, separately in each legal entity. Mappings tell the platform which HR title belongs to which course. Learner status and completions from HR both use them. You need the Organisation administrator role. Open HR course titles Go to Manage → Settings → Synchronisation → Learning records and find HR course titles. The table lists each HR course title, its Legal entity, the LMS course, its Source and when it was Updated. Needs attention lists anything missing or ambiguous. Fill in mappings automatically Click Update from course export. Courses already sent to HR are mapped by the title HR holds for them. This also happens automatically every hour. Add a mapping by hand Click Add mapping. Enter the Legal entity code, the HR course title exactly as it appears in HR, and choose the LMS course. Click Save mapping. Change or remove a mapping Click Change course or Remove mapping on the row. Titles must match exactly, including capitalisation. If a course is renamed in HR, update its mapping.

Replace the certificate the platform uses to sign in to F&O before it expires, or if you need to stop using it. Add the new one before you revoke the old one, so syncs keep working. You need the Organisation administrator role. Check the expiry date Go to Manage → Settings → HR connection. The Certificates list shows each certificate's Thumbprint, Created and Expires dates. Add and upload a new certificate Click Add certificate, then Download on the new certificate. Upload the .cer file to the app registration in Microsoft Entra (Certificates & secrets → Certificates → Upload certificate). You can have up to 5 active certificates. Test Click Test connection and check every row says Passed. Revoke the old certificate Click Revoke on the old certificate, then Revoke certificate to confirm. Then remove it from the app registration in Microsoft Entra as well. Note: Revoking can't be undone. If you revoke the only certificate uploaded to Entra, syncs stop until you add and upload a new one.

If a user sync would disable an unusually large number of people, it stops before disabling anyone and waits for an administrator to check. This protects you from a wrong filter or an incomplete read in HR. You need the Organisation administrator role. A sync you started by hand can only be reviewed by you. A scheduled sync can be reviewed by any organisation administrator. Know when a sync is held A sync is held when it would disable more than 5% of the people linked to HR, or more than 200 people, whichever is reached first. TMRW support can change these limits for your organisation. While it's held, nobody has been disabled. Notice the banner User sync is paused appears on the Manage overview and on Settings → Synchronisation. It says how many people are waiting to be reviewed, and that scheduled and manual user syncs are on hold until then. No other user sync starts, scheduled or manual, until the held sync is decided. If you can't review it, the banner says who can. Open the review Click Review people to disable. The dialog says how many of your HR-linked people would be disabled, and lists them with the Reason, such as No longer in HR, Inactive in HR or No current employment in HR. Check the list Search the list and look for anything unexpected, such as a whole school, or people you know are still working. If it looks wrong, choose Keep everyone and ask your HR team to check the data before the next sync. Decide To go ahead, tick I have checked the people listed and approve disabling their accounts and click Disable people. To complete the sync without disabling anyone, click Keep everyone. Note: Disabled people can't sign in until a later sync finds them in HR again or an administrator re-enables them. Their learning records are kept. Either way, the sync completes and user syncs carry on as normal. Sync history records the decision and who made it.

A user sync brings your staff in from HR. It creates accounts for new people and updates details and placements for everyone else. User syncs also run on your schedule; run one by hand when you don't want to wait. You need the Organisation administrator role. Start the sync Go to Manage → Settings → Synchronisation and open People. On the Users row, click Sync now: users. If the button isn't available, check the row's Status: Not activated means TMRW support hasn't switched user sync on yet. Follow its progress Under the table, a progress bar shows the current step, such as Step 1 of 6: Read from HR, with a list of every step the run takes: Step What happens Read from HR Reads workers, positions, worker statuses, employments and, if used, staff categories and line managers, all at the same time. Each table's count is listed while it's read Match people Matches each worker to an account, and applies the import rules Import people Creates and updates accounts and placements, for example "7,000 of 28,000" Apply line managers Sets who reports to whom, if line managers come from HR Add staff categories from HR Adds categories HR sent that aren't defined yet Disable people no longer in HR Disables people the sync no longer imports A run only lists the steps it uses. You can leave the page; the sync carries on. Pause, resume or cancel if you need to For a run you started, click Pause sync to stop after the current step and Resume sync to carry on. Scheduled runs can't be paused. To stop any run for good, click Cancel sync, then Cancel sync again to confirm. People already imported stay, and you can start a new sync straight away. A cancelled run can't be resumed. Check the results When the run is Completed, the Latest result shows how many were imported, unchanged and disabled. Click View results for the full list: search by name, or filter by Import status, such as Not imported, Moved, Re-enabled or Disabled or to be disabled. The Reason column says why someone wasn't imported. People with no work email in HR are still imported, marked Pending: missing email. If the run stops at Awaiting review, it would disable more people than your review limit. See Review people before they're disabled.

Keep each person's HR learning record up to date with their progress, so HR and employee self-service see the same status as the platform. You need the Organisation administrator role. Know what's sent For each person and course, the platform writes the status (not started, in progress or completed), whether it's mandatory or recommended, the assigned and due dates, and a link. The link goes to the course, then to the feedback form while required feedback is outstanding, then to the certificate. An unchanged status isn't sent again, and withdrawn learning leaves the HR record as it is. Turn it on Go to Manage → Settings → Synchronisation → Learning records. Under Learner status to HR, turn on Send learner status. In Send unclassified learning as, choose Recommended or Mandatory for older assignments made before learning was classified. Click Save learner status settings. If you see Not sending, something else needs to happen first, such as TMRW support making the export available. Changes are kept and sent once it's resolved. Send existing learning To send everyone's current learning, not only new changes, click Queue current learning. Check updates Updates sent to HR lists each update as Waiting, Failed, Skipped or Sent, with the reason. Failed updates are retried automatically a few times. Click Retry on a row, or Retry failed for all of them, to send them again. A learner needs an HR identity, and the course needs an HR course title in the learner's legal entity. Otherwise the update is skipped. See Map HR course titles. Completions that came from HR are never written back, and a record HR already has as completed is never lowered.

Each part of the HR integration is switched on separately, so you can start with people and add courses and learning records later. Most switches are set by TMRW support, and one is yours. You need the Organisation administrator role. Decide what you want Sync Direction Who switches it on Legal entities From HR TMRW support Users From HR TMRW support Line managers from HR From HR, with Users TMRW support Employment details and staff categories From HR, with Users TMRW support Courses To HR TMRW support, with the F&O company and course type to use Courses From HR TMRW support Course participants Both ways TMRW support. Writes to HR also need your F&O team to approve them Completions from HR From HR TMRW support Learner status to HR To HR TMRW support makes it available, then you turn on Send learner status Disabling people who are no longer in HR, and adding staff categories from HR, are on by default once Users is switched on. Ask TMRW support Contact TMRW support with the syncs you want, the F&O legal entities to read courses and participants from, and the schedule you'd like. See When HR syncs run. Check what's available Go to Manage → Settings → Synchronisation. Each sync's Status shows whether you can run it, for example Available, Not activated or Unavailable. Expand a row to see why a sync isn't available. Turn on learner status When learner status is available, see Send learner status to HR.

Keep course enrolments in step. People registered on a course in HR are assigned it in the platform. Assignments made in the platform are written back to HR as participants, once writes are approved. You need the Organisation administrator role. Open the Course participants row Go to Manage → Settings → Synchronisation → Courses and expand Course participants. It shows whether From HR and To HR are on or held, and how many writes are waiting, written, and failed or skipped. Bring registrations in from HR Click Preview sync: course participants to see what would happen, or Sync now: course participants to run it. For courses linked to HR, each registration becomes an assignment for the matching person. By default it's recommended, or mandatory when HR marks it required, and the due date comes from HR. No assignment email is sent for registrations from HR. A course that's still a draft is assigned once it's published. Know what happens when HR cancels When a registration is cancelled in HR, the assignment is withdrawn only if it came from HR and isn't completed. Learning assigned in the platform, or required by a learning rule, stays. Write enrolments to HR When TMRW support and your F&O team have approved writes, To HR shows On, and assignments made in the platform, including self-enrolments, are written to HR. Until then they're held, not lost. Click Retry failed writes to send failed or skipped writes again.

Courses can go both ways. Courses created in the platform are sent to HR, so HR knows they exist. Courses created in HR come into the platform as unpublished drafts, ready for content. You need the Organisation administrator role. Open Course syncs Go to Manage → Settings → Synchronisation and open Courses. The Course syncs table has a row for each direction. Send courses to HR Course changes are sent to HR automatically when you save a course. To send outstanding changes sooner, click Sync now: courses to HR. Courses without the start and end dates HR needs are skipped, not failed. Add Offering dates to the course and it's sent at the next sync. Failed writes are retried once a day; the row's details show the time in your own time zone. Bring courses in from HR Click Preview sync: courses from HR to see what a sync would do without changing anything. Click Sync now: courses from HR to run it. A course created in HR becomes an unpublished draft marked From HR, with no content. Add the course content and publish it as usual. Courses delivered in person are also imported as drafts, because in-person sessions aren't supported yet. Review conflicts If a course's title, description or self-enrolment setting changed in both places since the last sync, the platform keeps its own value and lists it under Course conflicts. Check each one, change the course if HR's value is right, then click Mark reviewed. If only HR changed, HR's value is taken. Check linked courses Linked courses lists every course that exists in both places, where it was created, and its status on each side. A course cancelled or missing in HR is marked, but the platform course is never deleted.

Use this checklist with your HR and IT teams before connecting. Your F&O administrator and your Microsoft Entra administrator each have a part to play. An F&O environment You need the URL of the Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations environment to connect, for example https://oakridge.operations.dynamics.com, and its environment ID. Connect a test (UAT) environment first if you have one. TMRW support approves the environment's address before the platform can call it. A Microsoft Entra app registration In your organisation's Microsoft Entra tenant, create an app registration for the integration. Note its Application client ID and your Microsoft Entra tenant ID. You don't create a client secret: the platform signs in with a certificate it generates. You upload the public part of the certificate to the app registration when you connect. The private key never leaves TMRW. The app registered in F&O In F&O, go to System administration > Setup > Microsoft Entra applications, add the client ID, and map it to a dedicated service user. Give that user only the security roles and legal-entity access the integration needs. Access to the data entities The service user needs read access to these F&O data entities: Data entity Used for LegalEntities Your companies and schools Workers Names and work email addresses PositionsV2 Occupied positions, job titles, departments and staff categories EmploymentsV2 Current employments, which decide each person's legal entities Worker status Which workers are active. Your environment may use a custom entity for this Line manager relations Who reports to whom, if you use line managers from HR CourseTables Courses CourseParticipants Course registrations HR learning record Completions recorded in HR. This is usually a custom entity in your environment For write-back, it also needs write access to CourseTables (courses to HR), CourseParticipants (enrolments to HR, once approved) and your HR learning record entity (learner status). Grant write access only for the flows you plan to switch on. TMRW confirms the exact entity names for your environment with your F&O team during onboarding. Someone with the right role You need the Organisation administrator role in GrowthXP to connect and run the integration. TMRW support TMRW support makes the integration available to your organisation, approves your F&O environment, switches on each sync, and sets the schedule. See Switch on each HR sync. When everything is ready, connect to Dynamics 365.
documents.s: What you need to connect Dynamics 365

documents.t: Each HR sync runs on a schedule that TMRW support sets with you. Settings → Synchronisation shows the Synchronisation policy as Read only, because cadence and activation are managed by TMRW. You need the Organisation administrator role to run syncs by hand. Know the schedule Sync When it runs Users On your schedule: hourly, every 6 hours, daily or weekly, at a local time you choose with TMRW support Legal entities On your schedule, as above Course sync: courses from and to HR, course participants and completions from HR On your schedule, as one run. Completions are imported after courses and participants Courses to HR Also each time a course is saved. Failed writes are retried once a day Learner status to HR Continuously, shortly after each change A daily user sync before the working day means changes made in HR the day before are in place when staff start work. To change your schedule, contact TMRW support. Run a sync by hand Go to Manage → Settings → Synchronisation and click Sync now on any available row. Manual and scheduled runs are recorded the same way in Sync history. Know what makes a sync wait Only one user sync runs at a time. While a user sync is running, paused or held for review, the next scheduled user sync doesn't start. A sync held for review stops all user syncs until an administrator decides. See Review people before they're disabled.

The user sync follows a set of import rules, so only the right people get accounts and everyone is placed where HR says they work. TMRW support sets the rules with you when the integration is switched on. Occupied, current positions The sync starts from positions in HR. A position counts when someone is assigned to it and the assignment is current on the day the sync runs. Vacant positions are left out. Active workers only Only workers whose HR status is active are imported. Anyone else is not imported, with the reason Inactive in HR. Temporary positions left out Positions whose ID starts with an excluded prefix are ignored. By default this is T-, used for temporary positions. Someone whose only positions are excluded isn't imported, with the reason Only temporary (excluded) positions, such as T- positions. If they also hold a normal position, only the normal one counts. Placed by current employment Each person is placed in every legal entity they currently have an employment in, so someone employed by two schools is a member of both. Their job title and department come from their positions. A worker with no current employment isn't imported, with the reason No current employment in HR. Moves between legal entities When HR places someone in a different legal entity, the sync moves them. Their memberships from HR that HR no longer supports are ended and kept as history, and new ones are added. Memberships an administrator added by hand are never touched. The results count them as Moved, for example "Moved: Riverside Secondary School → Hillview Academy". Learning rules then re-check the person, so their learning follows the move. People no longer in HR After a complete sync, anyone linked to HR whom the sync no longer imports is disabled: people who have left HR, are inactive, have only temporary positions, or have no current employment. Nobody is deleted. Their learning records, completions and certificates are kept, and they're re-enabled automatically if a later sync finds them in HR again. Accounts created by hand, and accounts an administrator disabled, aren't changed. If a sync would disable more people than your review limit, it waits for an administrator. See Review people before they're disabled. Line managers and staff categories If line managers from HR are switched on, the sync sets who reports to whom, and line manager access follows. If employment details are switched on, each person's staff category comes from HR, and categories HR sends that aren't defined yet are added automatically after a complete sync. See Manage staff categories. Check one person To see how the rules apply to one person, use Look up a person in HR. It shows their HR status, where their legal entities come from, and what the next sync will do.

A learning pathway sets courses in an order, in steps, leading to a certification such as an induction programme. Open Learning pathways Click Learning pathways in the header. Each pathway has a card with its title, its certification and a short description. The footer shows your progress and the course to do next. If none have been published for you, the page says No pathways yet. Open a pathway Click the pathway's card. It opens to show the steps, and moves to the top of the page. Click it again to close it. Pick the next course Next up (or Continue, for a course you've started) names the course to do now. Click Start course or Continue course to open its details. If more courses are ready, the card says how many. Or choose from the steps The steps run from Step 1 downwards, and lines link each course to the ones it builds on. Each course is marked Done, In progress, Available or Locked. Click any course to open its details. Launch the course In the course details, click Launch course. Work through it as usual; your progress also shows in My courses. Check a locked course A Locked course still opens its details, so you can read what's coming. The details say Locked in this pathway and name the courses to finish first, and the button reads Locked instead of Launch course. Finish those courses and it becomes Available. Learning that's assigned to you, or that you've already started, is never locked by a pathway; a course that's open for that reason says Assigned to you. When you've completed every course in the pathway, and given any feedback that's required, you receive the pathway's certificate automatically if it has one. It appears in Certificates. If the page says Pathways not loaded, click Try again.

Your progress through a pathway comes from your own learning, so it matches My courses. Check the card On Learning pathways, each closed card shows a ring with the percentage done, the number of courses done out of the total (for example 2/6 courses) and a short line: Next: or Continue: and a course, how many courses are ready to start, Nothing available yet or Pathway complete. Read the marks in the steps Open the pathway. The key explains the mark on each course: Done: you've completed it. In progress: you've started it. Available: you can start it now, because the courses before it are done, it has none, or it's assigned to you. Locked: a course before it isn't done yet. See progress in a course A course you've started shows how far through it you are, for example 40% done. A course that's available only because it's assigned to you says Assigned to you. A course counts as done when you've completed it as shown in My courses. When a course is renewed, it counts as done again once you complete the renewal. Check My courses for due dates and completion dates.

A backfill checks everyone against every active rule at once, for example after people were imported from HR, or after changes to organisations or staff categories. You need the HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the backfill In Manage ▸ Learning rules, under Existing people, click Backfill existing people. If no rule is active, the window asks you to activate one first. Preview it The window checks people without changing anything: Active rules, People checked so far, New assignments, Need review and Not started yet. Click Check more people until everyone has been checked. The table lists each person, the outcome, the rules and the details. Know the due dates Due dates come from recorded employment start dates only. Anyone else is due the day they're assigned plus grace days. The date someone was imported is never used. Decide about emails Email people about their new assignments is off by default. If you tick it, emails follow the daily limit in Settings, so the rest are sent on later days. Run it Click Run backfill. A message says how many rules are running. People who already have a course keep their existing assignment.

Assignment settings are the defaults behind assignments and learning rules: classification, due dates, renewals, validity and emails. You need the HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Course managers can open the settings but not change them. Open the settings In Manage ▸ Learning rules, click Settings. Set the assignment defaults Under Assignments, choose the default Classification, which is preselected when someone assigns a course. Under When someone stops matching a rule, choose to Withdraw their open mandatory assignments or Keep their open assignments. Under Months employed counts from, choose Start of current employment or Earliest recorded employment start. Set the due dates Under Due dates for rule assignments, set the Grace days (30 by default). Choose when New joiners are due and when Existing staff when a rule is activated are due. Tick Give recommended learning a due date if you want one; it's still never overdue. Set the Renewal lead time (days): the next cycle is assigned this many days before expiry and is due on the expiry date. Set validity Under Completion validity, set the Default validity for mandatory learning (months), 12 by default (0 means it never expires), used when neither the course nor the rule sets one. Choose when learning shows as expiring soon. Set new-joiner timing and emails Under New and changed people, choose whether people whose employment hasn't started are assigned On their employment start date or As soon as they match a rule. Set Automated assignment emails per day (500 by default); emails over the limit are sent on later days, and 0 sends none. Save Check the example due dates at the bottom, then click Save settings. Changes apply to assignments and completions from now on; existing due dates and expiry dates don't change.

You can change a rule, run it again, stop it, or retire it. You need the HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Change a rule In Manage ▸ Learning rules, open the rule's row menu and choose Edit. Make your changes and click Save changes. For an active rule, the window says Changes need activation: the active version stays in force, and the rule shows Changes not activated until you preview and activate the new version. Run an active rule now Choose Run now to check everyone against the active version straight away, for example after you've fixed people's details. It's unavailable while a run is in progress. Deactivate a rule Choose Deactivate, then Deactivate rule. Nobody new is assigned by the rule. Existing assignments, including open ones, stay in place. Choose Reactivate later to turn it back on. Delete a rule For a draft or inactive rule, choose Delete, then Delete rule. The rule is retired. Assignments it created and its version history are kept.

Instead of listing courses, a rule can assign every course with a tag, or every course with an HR course type. The rule then keeps up as courses change. You need the HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the rule In Manage ▸ Learning rules, click Create rule, or open a rule's row menu and choose Edit. Choose by tag Under Courses, choose Courses with a tag, then choose up to 20 Tags. Course managers add tags to courses in Edit details; if no course has a tag yet, the field says so. Or choose by HR course type If your courses are linked to your HR system, you can choose Courses with an HR course type, then choose up to 20 HR course types. This choice only appears when courses have HR course types. Know what's assigned Every published, unexpired course with one of the tags or types is assigned to the people in that course's audience who match the rule. When a course gains or loses the tag or type, or is published or expires, it's added to or withdrawn from the rule automatically, without editing the rule. Save Click Create rule or Save changes, then preview and activate the rule.
documents.s: Choose courses by tag or HR course type

documents.t: A rule's conditions decide who it assigns. You need the HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the conditions In the rule's window, scroll to Who it applies to. Every condition you set must match. Leave a condition empty to ignore it. Choose staff categories Under Staff categories (optional), choose categories such as Teacher or Teaching assistant. Choose organisations Under Organisations (optional), choose any units of your organisation, such as a school, region or department. Tick Include people in child organisations to include the units below them. People in several organisations match when any of them is chosen; people in none of them don't match. Add other conditions Enter Worker types (optional) and Job titles (optional), separated by commas. Use Minimum months employed (optional) and Maximum months employed (optional) to target, for example, people in their first year. Know who's held for review People missing a staff category, employment start date, worker type or job title the rule needs aren't assigned. They're listed for review in the preview and under People changes, so you can fix their details on People.
documents.s: Choose who a rule applies to

documents.t: A learning rule assigns courses automatically to everyone who matches its conditions. You need the HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Start a rule Click Manage in the header, then Learning rules under Organisation. Click Create rule. Name it Enter a Rule name, such as "All teachers complete Safeguarding essentials", and a Description (optional). Choose what's assigned Under Courses, choose Specific courses, then choose up to 20 published courses in Courses to assign. To choose courses by tag or HR course type instead, see Choose courses by tag or HR course type. Choose mandatory or recommended Under Assign as, choose Mandatory (the default) or Recommended. Tick Email people the rule assigns after it is activated if people should be emailed when the rule assigns them later. Set the details Set due dates, renewals and validity and who the rule applies to. Create it Click Create rule. The rule is saved as a draft and nobody is assigned yet. Next, preview and activate it.

Learning rules assign courses automatically from people's details, such as their staff category, organisation or how long they've worked for you. HR managers and organisation administrators create and run them; course managers can see them, to know which rules use their courses. A rule chooses courses and people A rule chooses specific courses, every course with a tag, or every course with an HR course type. It applies to people who match all its conditions: staff category, organisation, worker type, job title and months employed. It assigns the courses as Mandatory or Recommended, with due dates worked out from your settings. Nothing happens until you activate it A new rule is a draft. You preview who it would assign, then activate it. Activation assigns the courses to everyone who matches, unless they already have them. Editing an active rule saves a new version that waits until you activate it; until then the active version stays in force. Active rules keep people up to date Active rules check people when they join or when their staff category, employment, organisation or job title changes. New courses with the rule's tag or HR course type are assigned without editing the rule. People whose employment hasn't started yet are assigned on their start date. To check everyone again at once, run a backfill. Your organisation can also have rules re-checked on a schedule: that's off unless TMRW support turns it on. Rules respect the course audience A rule only assigns a course to people in that course's audience, and only published courses that haven't expired. Someone who already has a course keeps their assignment. If the rule is mandatory, the course becomes mandatory for them. How rules remove learning When someone stops matching a rule, their open mandatory assignments from it are withdrawn, unless your settings say to keep them. Completed learning is never withdrawn. Deactivating a rule stops new assignments but leaves existing ones in place. You can't remove a rule's assignment on Learning assignments: change the rule or the person's details instead. Rules renew expiring learning Completed mandatory learning is assigned again before it expires. See Run a renewal check.

Before a rule assigns anyone, preview it, then activate it. You need the HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Preview the rule In Manage ▸ Learning rules, open the rule's row menu and choose Preview. The preview checks people in batches: People checked so far, Would be assigned and Need review (not assigned). Click Check more people until everyone has been checked. Check the courses and people Courses lists each course with the number of people in its audience. A warning appears if a course is open to everyone. Need review lists people missing details the rule needs, with the reasons. Would be assigned lists each person with their courses, whether they're a new joiner, existing staff or newly matching, and their due date. Activate it Close the preview, open the row menu and choose Activate (or Reactivate for an inactive rule). The window says which version you're activating. Decide about emails Email the people assigned now is off by default, so a first activation doesn't send a burst of emails. Tick it if people should be emailed about their new learning. Confirm and check the run Click Activate rule. The rule's status changes to Active and assignments are created in the background. The Latest run column shows progress, then a summary such as "40 assigned, 2 already assigned, 1 for review".

When people join or their details change, active rules check them. People changes shows who's waiting, who was checked and who needs their details fixing. You need the HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Open People changes In Manage ▸ Learning rules, scroll to People changes. Choose a list Under Show, choose Need review, Waiting for start date, Waiting to be evaluated, Evaluation failed or Evaluated. The table shows each Person, what Changed (such as New person, Organisation or Job title), when it was Recorded, and Details. Fix people needing review Need review lists people who might match a rule but are missing a staff category, employment start date, worker type or job title, or whose details conflict. They aren't assigned until the details are fixed. Fix them on People, or in your HR system if the details come from HR; the change is checked again automatically. Check people waiting to start Waiting for start date lists people whose employment hasn't started; they're assigned on their start date. Evaluation failed people are checked again after their next change or a backfill. Click Show more people to see more.

Mandatory learning that expires is assigned again when its renewal lead time starts, due on the expiry date, and the learner is emailed a renewal notice. A renewal check makes these renewals. You need the HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Check when renewals last ran In Manage ▸ Learning rules, scroll to Renewals. The line under the heading says when the latest check ran and what it did. Checks run only when someone runs them, unless TMRW support has turned on daily checks for your organisation. Preview a check Click Check renewals. The preview changes nothing: it shows Completions checked, Renew now, Not renewed and how many renew in the next few days. Click Check more completions until all have been checked. The table lists each person, course, expiry date and outcome. Run it Click Run renewal check. Each renewal is a new cycle of the course, due on the expiry date, and the learner is emailed a renewal notice. Learning that has already expired is assigned at once. Earlier completions and certificates are kept. Check what wasn't renewed Not renewed lists learning that was due but wasn't assigned again, with the Reason, such as "Not mandatory", "Employment ended" or "Outside course audience". It's renewed by the next check once the reason no longer applies.
