A rule works out each person's due date from a starting date plus grace days. You can use your organisation's assignment settings or set the rule's own. You need the HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Know where due dates start For mandatory rules, new joiners are due from their employment start date, existing staff from the day the rule is activated, and people who match later from the day they match, each plus grace days. Recommended learning is never overdue, and only has a due date if your assignment settings give recommended learning due dates. Set grace days and renewal lead time Under Due dates, enter Grace days (optional) to override the number of days added to the starting date, and Renewal lead time in days (optional) to override how long before expiry the next cycle is assigned. Both take 0 to 365. Leave them empty to use the assignment settings. Check the examples Calculation preview shows example due dates for a new joiner, for existing staff if you activate today, and for someone who starts matching today. Set the validity Under Validity, choose Use the course setting, Expires after a number of months or Never expires. This overrides each course's validity for learning assigned by this rule. Know when changes apply Changes apply to people assigned after you activate the new version. Existing due dates stay as they are.
documents.s: Set due dates and renewals on a rule

documents.t: A rule's history shows every version that was activated and every run. You need the HR manager, Course manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the history In Manage ▸ Learning rules, open the rule's row menu and choose History. Read the versions Versions lists each activated version with its Classification, Courses, when it was Activated and Activated by whom. Assignments keep the version that created them. Read the runs Recent runs lists when each run was Requested, its Trigger (Activation, Run now, Scheduled, Backfill or Course change), the Version and the Outcome, such as how many people were assigned, already assigned, held for review or withdrawn.

Courses lists every course your organisation offers you, grouped into channels. Open Courses Click Courses in the header. Choose a channel Click a channel tab, such as Compliance, to see only its courses, or All courses to see everything. Search Type in Search courses to find courses by title, description or tag. Click Clear search if nothing matches. Check the card Each card shows the course's length and when it was added, and where you stand with it: Assigned to you means it's been given to you, Self-enrolled means you enrolled in it yourself, and Open to enrol means you can enrol in it yourself. Open the course Click a card (View course) to open its details, where you can enrol or launch it. You only see published courses offered to you, which can depend on your school or organisation. Some courses appear only once they've been assigned to you.

See what's due In My courses, each card you haven't completed shows Due and the date. Cards with due dates come first, soonest first. Spot overdue learning Mandatory learning that's past its due date moves to the top of My courses with a red Overdue tag on its card. It also shows as Overdue in the Notifications bell and on your Calendar. Learning due in the next seven days shows as Due soon in the bell. Know where the date came from Whoever gave you the learning set the date. Learning from your organisation's rules is usually due a set number of days, such as 30, after you join or after the rule starts. A due date runs to the end of that day. Catch up Open the course and complete it. It stops being overdue as soon as it's completed. You'll get reminder emails before the date and overdue notices afterwards, if your organisation has them switched on. Recommended learning is never overdue. You can't change a due date yourself; if you need more time, ask your line manager or HR. If your organisation has turned on manager escalation, your line manager is told when mandatory learning stays overdue after several reminders.
documents.s: Check due dates and overdue learning

documents.t: Some learning, such as first aid or safeguarding, is only valid for a set time after you complete it. Look at the completed card In My courses, click the Completed tab. Each card shows its validity next to the completion date: Valid until and a date: your completion is current. Expires and a date: it expires soon. Expired and a date: it has expired. No expiry: it never needs renewing. See expiry dates in your calendar Calendar shows each Expiry, and for mandatory learning the date its Renewal due starts. Know how it's worked out The validity runs for whole calendar months from the moment you completed the course, for example 12 months. A completion on 29 February expires on 28 February. The length is set by the course or by your organisation, and it's fixed when you complete: later changes to the setting don't move your expiry date. Expired learning still shows as Completed; only its validity changes. Mandatory learning is usually assigned to you again before it expires. See Renew your learning. Dates are the same for everyone, whatever your time zone.

A course is complete when the course itself says you've finished or passed it. There's no button to mark it complete. Finish the course content Work through to the end of the course, including any quiz it ends with. When the course reports completed or passed, or you reach its final page, GrowthXP records your completion. Give feedback The Course feedback form opens. Fill it in now, or click Not now and come back later. See Give feedback on a course. See it completed In My courses the card shows Completed, 100% and the date you finished. If the course awards a certificate, it appears in Certificates, unless the course waits for your feedback first. Check how long it stays valid Some learning is valid for a set time, such as 12 months. The card shows Valid until and the date, or No expiry. See Check when your learning expires. Your completion date is recorded once and never changes. Click Review course to go back through a completed course; reviewing it doesn't change your completion. If a course you've finished still shows In progress, launch it again and make sure you reach its last page or result screen.

Some courses come with materials, such as handouts or slides, that you can keep. Open the course details Click the course card in My courses or Courses. Find Materials Scroll to Materials. Each file shows its name, a description, and its type and size. Download Click Download next to the file. It saves to your device with its original name. If there's no Materials section, the course has no files for you. New files appear only once they've passed a security check. If you see Materials unavailable, close the course details and open them again.

Some courses let you enrol yourself, without waiting for someone to assign them. Find a course you can enrol in In Courses, look for the Open to enrol tag on a card, then click the card. Click Enrol In the course details, click Enrol. A message confirms Enrolled. Find it in My courses The course now appears in My courses with the Self-enrolled and Recommended tags. Launch it whenever you're ready. Learning you enrol in yourself is Recommended: it has no due date unless your organisation sets one for recommended learning, and it's never overdue. If there's no Enrol button, the course doesn't allow self-enrolment or you already have it; you can still launch a course you can see, or ask your administrator to assign it. You can withdraw until you start the course.

You're asked for feedback on every course you complete. For some courses, it's required before you receive the certificate. Open the feedback form The Course feedback form opens when you complete a course. To come back to it later, click Give feedback under the course card in My courses, click the Feedback required or Feedback needed item in the bell, or use the link in a feedback reminder email. Clicking the card itself opens the course, so you can review it first. Rate the course Under Overall rating, click one to five stars. Describe your experience In Tell us about your experience, write between 10 and 1,000 characters. Say whether you'd recommend it Set Would you recommend this course? to Yes or No. It starts on Yes. Submit Click Submit feedback. It becomes available once you've chosen a rating and written at least 10 characters. A message confirms Feedback submitted, and says when your certificate is now available. Click Not now to leave the form for later; the card keeps a feedback tag and Give feedback until you submit. The form tells you if your feedback is required for the certificate and when it's due. Feedback after the due date is still accepted and is marked as late. Each renewal of a course asks for feedback again.

Each course you're given is tagged Mandatory or Recommended on its card in My courses. Mandatory learning You need to complete it by its due date. You're reminded before the date, it becomes overdue if you miss it, and it counts towards your organisation's compliance reports. If it has a validity period, it's given to you again before it expires. Recommended learning It's suggested for you but optional. It may have a due date to help you plan, but it's never overdue, you never get overdue notices for it, and it isn't renewed. Courses you enrol in yourself are always recommended. It depends on who it's for Mandatory or recommended is decided when the learning is given to you, not by the course. The same course can be mandatory for one group of staff and recommended for another. When it comes from more than one place If a course reaches you in more than one way, for example from a rule for all teachers and from your manager, you see one card. It's Mandatory if any of them makes it mandatory, and it's due on the earliest mandatory due date. The tag disappears once you've completed the course. Learning given to you before this classification existed has no tag and is treated as mandatory.

Each card in My courses sums up where you are with one course. Status and type tags The first tag is the status: Not started, In progress or Completed. Other tags can follow: Overdue, in red: mandatory learning that's past its due date. Mandatory or Recommended: how the learning was given to you (hidden once completed). Renewal 1, Renewal 2 and so on: you're on a renewal of learning you completed before. Self-enrolled: you enrolled in it yourself. Recorded in HR: completed outside GrowthXP and recorded in your HR system. Feedback required, Feedback overdue or Feedback needed: you owe feedback on the course. Up to three skills the course teaches. The details line Under the title and description you'll see the course's length, and whichever of these apply: Due and a date, until you've completed it. The date you completed it. How long the completion stays valid: Valid until, Expires (expiring soon), Expired or No expiry. When feedback is due, or since when it's been overdue. Progress The bar shows how much of the course you've done: a percentage, Not started, or Opened, no progress yet if you opened it without getting further. A completed course always shows 100%. What clicking does The last line says what happens when you click the card: Start course, Continue learning, Review course, or Not available if the course can't be opened at the moment. Clicking the card opens the course, even while you owe feedback on it. Buttons under the card Give feedback appears while you owe feedback on the course, and opens the feedback form. Training history appears once you've completed the course or have earlier cycles of it. Withdraw appears on a course you enrolled in yourself and haven't started.

When mandatory learning is close to expiring, GrowthXP gives it to you again so you can renew it before it lapses. Notice the renewal You may get a Renewal due email, and the course returns to the top of My courses with a Renewal 1 tag (then Renewal 2, and so on), the status Not started and a due date. The due date is usually the day your current completion expires. Complete the course again Launch the course and work through it as usual. Your earlier progress doesn't count towards the renewal, so you start from the beginning. Check your new validity When you complete it, a new validity period starts from the new completion date. If the course awards a certificate, you get a new one for this renewal. Renewals are for mandatory learning only. They're usually created 30 days before expiry, but this depends on your organisation's settings and on when it runs its renewal check. Your earlier completions and certificates stay on record: see View your training history. If your organisation renews your learning early, the history shows (early) next to that renewal.

Courses can teach skills. When you complete a course, you earn its skills. Check the count In My courses, the learning summary shows how many Skills earned you have. Look at your badges The Skills earned shelf, beside your courses or below them on a smaller screen, shows a badge for each skill. Each one says when you earned it and from how many courses. Find courses by skill Type a skill's name in the My courses search box to see the courses that teach it. In course details, Skills you’ll develop lists a course's skills before you start. A skill counts once, however many courses teach it. The earliest completion is the date you earned it.

Courses play inside GrowthXP and save your progress for you. Launch the course Click the course card in My courses (it says Start course or Continue learning), then click Launch course in the course details. Work through the course The course fills the page. The header shows the course title and a Close course button. Your answers and your place are saved automatically every few seconds. Close the course Click Close course when you want to stop. Your progress is saved and you return to the course details. Progress is also saved if you switch tab or close the browser. Continue later Open the course again and click Launch course. Your saved progress is restored, so most courses take you back to where you left off or offer to. If you lose your connection, GrowthXP keeps your latest progress in this browser and sends it the next time you open the course here. If you see Course could not be opened, check your connection and try again. If the course says its link has expired, close it and launch it again.

If your organisation connects GrowthXP to its HR system, courses you completed outside GrowthXP can be brought in as completed. Recognise the tag The card in My courses shows Completed and Recorded in HR, with the note "Completed outside the LMS. There is no certificate or evidence in the LMS." Know what it counts for The course counts as completed for your organisation's compliance. Its validity and any renewal are worked out from the completion date in HR. Know what you don't get GrowthXP has no certificate for it, doesn't ask for your feedback and doesn't send a completion email. Complete it in GrowthXP if you need to If you need a certificate or the course material, launch and complete the course in GrowthXP. Your GrowthXP completion then replaces the HR record, and feedback and any certificate follow as usual. This only happens if your organisation has switched on importing completions from HR.

The details dialog tells you what a course is about and is where you launch it. Open the details Click a course card in My courses or Courses. You can also get here from a notification, from Open course in your calendar, or from a course in a learning pathway. Read about the course Under the title you'll see its length, its SCORM version, when it was added and Certificate if it awards one. Then About this course, its Tags, Skills you’ll develop and any Materials to download. Check the messages Certificate: completing the course earns you a certificate. Expires or Expired: the date the course itself stops being available. After it, nobody can launch it. Not yet available: the course is still being prepared. Choose what to do Click Launch course to start or continue. Enrol appears if you can add the course to your courses yourself. If the button reads Course expired or Not available yet, the course can't be opened at the moment. Click Close to go back.

My courses is your home page in GrowthXP. It lists every course assigned to you, and every course you've opened from the catalogue, with your progress. Open My courses Click My courses in the header. Along the top, the learning summary counts your Assigned, In progress and Completed courses and your Skills earned. Filter by status Click a tab to narrow the list: All, In progress, Not started or Completed. Each tab shows how many courses it holds. Search Type in the search box (Search by course or skill) to find a course by its title or by a skill it teaches. Click Clear search if nothing matches. Work from the top Courses are ordered for you: overdue mandatory learning first, tagged Overdue, then courses with a due date (soonest first), then courses in progress, then ones you haven't started. Completed courses go to the end. Open a course Click a card to open the course's details, where you can launch it. The words at the bottom of the card tell you what happens next: Start course, Continue learning or Review course. If you owe feedback on a course, click Give feedback under its card. A course you open from Courses appears here even if nobody assigned it to you. Courses given to a group you belong to appear here too.

Training history shows every time you've been given and completed a course, including renewals. Open the history In My courses, click Training history under the course's card. It appears once you've completed the course or have earlier cycles of it. Read each cycle Each row is one cycle: First completion, Renewal 1, Renewal 2 and so on. Current marks the cycle you're on now. The columns show the Status, when it was Assigned, its Due date, when it was Completed, its Validity and the Certificate number. Close it Click the close button (X) to return to My courses. Each completion is valid for its own period. Earlier completions and certificates stay on record after a renewal; you can find their certificates in Certificates.

If you enrolled in a course yourself and haven't started it, you can take it out of your courses. Find the course In My courses, find the card with the Self-enrolled tag. Click Withdraw Click Withdraw under the card. Confirm In Withdraw enrolment?, click Withdraw enrolment, or Keep enrolment to change your mind. A message confirms Enrolment withdrawn. The course stays in Courses, so you can enrol again later. Withdraw disappears as soon as you open the course, and it never appears on learning that was assigned to you; ask whoever assigned that learning if you think you shouldn't have it.
documents.s: Withdraw from a course you enrolled in

documents.t: You can download your team's learning as a CSV file to open in Excel. It's for line managers, and covers only the people in your reporting line. Filter the list In Manage ▸ My team, set People, Search people, Mandatory learning only and Overdue only to match what you need. The export uses exactly the people and learning on screen. Choose the export Click Export summary for one row per person, with their counts and mandatory compliance. Click Export detail for one row per person and course, with the status, due date, compliance, completion date and source, expiry, validity, feedback and certificate number. Open the file The file downloads as my-team-summary.csv or my-team-detail.csv. If you see Export failed, try again.

If people report to you, GrowthXP gives you the Line manager role automatically, so you can follow their learning. This page explains who's in your team and what you can see. Know who's in your team Your team is everyone who reports to you directly, plus everyone who reports to them, all the way down. The reporting relationships come from your HR system, or an organisation administrator sets them on the People page. When someone joins or leaves your team, your access changes straight away. Know when you get the role You get the Line manager role as soon as one person reports to you, and you lose it when nobody does. Nobody can give or remove it by hand on Access and permissions. If someone is missing from your team, ask your organisation administrator to check that person's line manager on People. Find your team's learning Click Manage in the header. In the side navigation under Organisation you'll see My team, Deadlines calendar and Learning reports. If line manager access is your only management access, Manage opens on My team. Know what you can and can't do You can see each person's progress, mandatory compliance, due dates, validity, feedback status and certificates. You can open their certificates and export your team's learning to a CSV file. You can't assign, remove or change anyone's learning: ask a learning manager, HR manager or organisation administrator to do that. You never see the comments people write in course feedback, only whether they've given it.

Learning reports gives totals and a detailed list of your team's learning, with more filters than My team. It's for line managers, and covers only the people in your reporting line. Open Learning reports Click Manage in the header, then Learning reports under Organisation. If you also hold an organisation or HR role, choose Your line reports under People. Read the totals The Totals tiles count the People, their Learning, how much is Completed, how much mandatory learning is compliant, and what's Overdue or Expired. Under Totals by, choose Course, School or Staff category to break the numbers down. Narrow the report Use Search people and the filters, such as Course, Classification, Status and Compliance. Click More filters for validity, feedback and date ranges. See Filter a learning report. Export it Click Export summary or Export detail. As a line manager you can export your team's report. See Export a learning report.

If your organisation has turned on manager escalation, GrowthXP emails you when someone in your team still hasn't completed their overdue mandatory learning. It's for line managers. Manager escalation is off unless an organisation administrator turns it on. Know why you got the email The person has mandatory learning that's past its due date, and they've already been sent a set number of overdue reminders (two, unless your organisation chose a different number). You're emailed at the next daily check, once for that course. By default the subject is "Overdue learning:" followed by the person's name and the course, and the email says how many days overdue it is and how many reminders they've had. Your organisation can change the wording. Open their learning Click View their learning in the email. It opens the person's page in My team, where you can check the course's due date, status and history. Follow it up Talk to the person about completing the course. You can't change their due date or remove the course yourself. If the due date should change, ask an HR manager or organisation administrator. Know when it stops You won't be emailed again about the same overdue course. An email that hasn't been sent yet is cancelled if the person completes the course, the course is removed or renewed, the due date changes, or they leave. Recommended learning is never overdue, so it never sends these emails. You're only emailed while you're the person's current line manager.
documents.s: Respond to an overdue learning email

documents.t: The deadlines calendar shows when your team's learning is due, when course feedback is due, and when completions expire or need renewing. It's for line managers; other roles use the same calendar for wider groups of people. Open the calendar for your team In Manage ▸ My team, click Team calendar. You can also click Deadlines calendar in the side navigation. People shows Your line reports. If you also hold an organisation or HR role, choose Your line reports under People to see only your team. Pick a month and a view Use Previous month, Today and Next month to move around. Month shows a grid with the selected day's deadlines listed underneath. Agenda lists every day in the month that has deadlines. See who's due Each course appears once a day for each type of deadline, with a summary such as "1 overdue · 3 in progress". Click it to open the panel on the right, which counts the people in each state and lists them, most urgent first. Click a person to see their deadline, then Back to all people. Narrow the deadlines Use the filters at the top, such as Event types, Status and Classification, to focus on what matters. See Filter the deadlines calendar for every filter.

A team member's page lists every course they have, how far they've got and whether their mandatory learning is up to date. It's for line managers, and only for people in your reporting line. Open the person In Manage ▸ My team, click the person's name. The page title is their name, with their job title and reporting line underneath. Read the summary tiles The tiles count their Not started, In progress and Completed learning. Mandatory compliant shows how many mandatory courses are up to date, with how many are overdue or expired underneath. Tick Mandatory learning only to list only mandatory courses. Read each course Classification is Mandatory, Recommended, or Not assigned for a course they started without being assigned it. Status is Not started, In progress or Completed. A Recorded in HR tag means the completion came from your HR system, with no certificate in GrowthXP. Compliance shows Compliant, Due, Overdue or Expired for mandatory learning. Validity shows when a completion expires. Feedback shows whether they've given course feedback, and when it's due. A renewed course shows "Cycle 2" (or later) under its title. Open a certificate Click the number in the Certificate column to open the certificate page, where you can view, print or download it. See the training history Click the Training history icon at the end of a row. The window lists every cycle of that course: when it was assigned, when it was due and completed, its validity and its certificate. Earlier completions and certificates stay on record after a renewal. Go back Click Back to my team to return to the list, or Team calendar to see your team's deadlines.

My team shows one row for each person in your reporting line, with counts of their learning and mandatory compliance. It's for line managers: you have access when people report to you. Open My team Click Manage in the header, then My team under Organisation. A line above the table says how many people are in view, for example "12 people in your reporting line". Choose who to show Under People, choose All reports (the default) or Direct reports only. Type in Search people to find someone by name or email. Tick Mandatory learning only to count only mandatory learning, or Overdue only to list only people with overdue mandatory learning. Your choices stay in the page address, so you can bookmark the view. Read the counts Reporting line shows Direct report, or who the person reports to. Assigned, Not started, In progress and Completed count the person's current learning. Mandatory compliant shows how many of their mandatory courses are up to date, for example "3 of 4". Overdue and Expired count mandatory learning only and are highlighted when they're above 0. Open a person Click a name to see that person's courses, due dates and certificates. If the list is long, click Show more at the bottom to load more people.

Add a unit, such as a school, a group of schools or a head office, to your organisation structure. You need the Organisation administrator role. Start adding Go to Manage → Organisation structure and click Add organisation. Fill in the details Choose the Type, for example School. For a type that isn't listed, choose Custom and enter a Custom type in lower-case letters, digits or hyphens. Enter the Name, then choose the Parent organisation it sits under. Add it Click Add organisation. It appears in the tree. To put people in it, add them in People with Add to an organisation, or link it to a legal entity from your HR system so people are placed automatically. See Link legal entities to an organisation.

Learner emails are sent when something happens to a learner's learning. Switch each one on or off for your whole organisation. You need the Organisation administrator role. Open Learner emails Go to Manage → Notifications and find Learner emails. Switch emails on or off Email When it's sent New course assigned When a course is assigned to a learner Completion email When a learner completes a course Renewal notice When learning that's about to expire is assigned again Certificate email Once for each certificate issued, with a link to the certificate page A Customised tag means the wording has been changed from the default. To change it, click Edit template. See Edit an email template. Save Click Save changes at the top of the page. Reminders, overdue notices, manager escalations and feedback reminders are set in their own sections on the same page. See Set up learning reminders.
documents.s: Choose which learner emails are sent

documents.t: Change what an email says. Placeholders such as {courseName} are replaced with each person's details when the email is sent. You need the Organisation administrator role. Open the template Go to Manage → Notifications. Find the email in its section and click Edit template. Change the wording Edit the Subject (up to 160 characters), Heading (up to 120) and Message (up to 2,000). To insert a placeholder, put the cursor where you want it and click the placeholder under Placeholders. Some emails need a placeholder in the message: the link to the certificate, the feedback form or the person's learning. These are marked Required in the message. Use placeholders Each email offers only the placeholders that make sense for it. Placeholder Replaced with Used in {recipientName} The learner's name Learner emails, reminders {courseName} The course or pathway title All emails {dueDate} The due date, in your organisation's time zone Assignment, reminders, renewal, feedback, escalation {days} The number of days before or after the due date Reminders, feedback reminder {timing} When it's due, for example "is due in 14 days" or "is 3 days overdue" Reminders, feedback reminder {senderName} The sender display name All emails {certificateUrl} The link to the learner's certificate page Certificate email (required) {feedbackUrl} The link to the course feedback form Feedback reminder (required) {managerName} The line manager's name Manager escalation {learnerName} The person whose learning is overdue Manager escalation {daysOverdue} How many days the learning is overdue Manager escalation {remindersSent} How many overdue reminders the person has been sent Manager escalation {teamMemberUrl} The link to the person's learning in My team Manager escalation (required) Check the preview Preview shows the email with your logo, as it will look. To see it in your own inbox, click Send test email. Apply and save Click Apply template, then Save changes at the top of the page. The email is tagged Customised. To go back to the original wording, open the template again and click Reset to default. The Overdue notice uses the Deadline reminder wording until you customise it. Its button is Use deadline reminder template instead of Reset to default.

Legal entities are the companies and schools in your HR system. Linking one places it in your organisation structure, so the people HR places in that legal entity are put in the right unit at each HR sync. You need the Organisation administrator role. Your organisation must use the HR integration, and the legal entities must have been imported. See Import legal entities. Select the parent Go to Manage → Organisation structure and select the organisation the legal entities should sit under. Find the legal entities In the Legal entities table, use Search legal entities, or filter by Linked here or Unlinked. Tick and type Tick Linked for each legal entity you want here, and choose its Type, for example School. You can link up to 20 at a time. Save Click Save links. Each linked legal entity becomes a unit under the selected organisation, named after the legal entity. You can rename it later. If a legal entity is already linked somewhere else, Move legal-entity links? asks you to confirm the move. Users, memberships and learning history stay as they are. To stop linking a legal entity, untick it and click Save links. The unit, its people, their access and their learning history stay. Discard changes throws away links you haven't saved.
documents.s: Link legal entities to an organisation

documents.t: The organisation structure is the tree of units, such as your trust, its groups and its schools, that the platform uses to scope access, reports and learning rules. You decide the shape and what each unit is called. You need the Organisation administrator role to change the structure. Learning managers and report viewers given access for the whole organisation can view it. Open the structure Go to Manage → Organisation structure. The Organisation hierarchy tree is on the left, with each unit's type beside its name. Select a unit to see its details and linked legal entities on the right. Rename a unit or change its type Select the unit and click Edit organisation. Change the Name or the Type (Organisation, Group, Cluster, School, Classroom, or Custom with your own type), then click Save changes. Types are labels only, and don't limit what can sit under a unit. Learning rules and reports use School to recognise schools. Move a unit Select the unit and click Move organisation. Choose the new Parent organisation and click Review move. The review shows how many units move with it, the memberships and grants that are kept, and any access people gain or lose because of the move. Click Move organisation to confirm. Moving a unit changes access that comes from the units above it. A learning manager given a parent unit with child units included gains or loses the moved unit. Check the review before you confirm. If you see Read-only, organisation changes are switched off for your organisation. Contact TMRW support.

Send yourself a copy of any email to check its wording and look. The test uses the wording on the page, even if you haven't saved it yet. You need the Organisation administrator role. Find the email Go to Manage → Notifications and find the email in its section. Send the test Click Send test email on the email's row, or inside Edit template. The message Test sent says who it was sent to: always you, the signed-in administrator, never a learner. Check your inbox If the Delivery and branding tag says Not sent or Not set up, the test isn't delivered. If it says Test inbox, it goes to the environment's test inbox instead of yours. Test not sent gives the reason.

Decide, for your whole organisation, whether learners must give feedback before they get a certificate, and when feedback is due. A course can override the certificate rule in its own settings. You need the Organisation administrator role. Open Course feedback Go to Manage → Settings and open the Course feedback tab. Require feedback before certificates Turn on Require feedback before certificate to hold each certificate until the learner submits a valid rating and comment. This is the default for every course and its pathways. Set a deadline Turn on Feedback deadline and enter Days after completion (1 to 365). Late feedback is still accepted and marked as late. A change applies to new completions only. Save Click Save feedback settings. To remind learners before and after the deadline, click Set feedback reminders in Notifications. See Set feedback reminders. The other Settings tabs, HR connection and Synchronisation, are for the HR integration. See How the HR integration works.

Remind learners to give course feedback before it's due, and once after. Reminders stop as soon as the learner submits valid feedback. You need the Organisation administrator role. Check there's a feedback deadline Go to Manage → Notifications and find Feedback reminders. If it says There is no feedback deadline, so no feedback reminders are sent, click Set a feedback deadline in System settings first. See Set course feedback rules. Set reminders before the deadline Under Reminders before the due date, enter Days before the due date and click Add another. You can have up to 5. The default is 3 days and 1 day before. Set the overdue notice Turn on Overdue feedback notice and set Days after the due date (1–30). One notice is sent, and late feedback is still accepted. Check the preview and the email Use the Schedule preview with an Example completion date to see when reminders would be sent. Make sure the Feedback reminder email below is switched on. Save Click Save changes at the top of the page. Scheduled emails must be switched on for your organisation for feedback reminders to be sent. If you see Scheduled emails are not switched on on the page, contact TMRW support.

Choose who the platform's emails come from and the logo they carry. These settings apply to every email the platform sends to learners and managers. You need the Organisation administrator role. Open Notifications Go to Manage → Notifications. Delivery and branding is the first section. Check delivery The tag shows where emails go in this environment: Sending means they reach the people they're for; Test inbox and Not sent are for test environments; Not set up means emails aren't sent. If you see Emails are switched off for your organisation, no emails on the page are sent. Contact TMRW support to switch them on. Set the sender Enter the Sender display name, for example "Oakridge Learning". The Reply-to address is optional. When you set one, replies to the platform's emails go there. Add your logo Drag a PNG or JPEG of up to 2 MB onto Email logo, or browse for it. It's converted to an email-safe PNG. Click Remove to go back to the default logo. Save Click Save changes at the top of the page. One save applies everything on the Notifications page, including the logo. If you try to leave with unsaved changes, the platform asks first.
documents.s: Set the email sender and logo

documents.t: Remind learners before their learning is due, and follow up while mandatory learning is overdue. Reminders are checked once a day at your send time, in your organisation's time zone. You need the Organisation administrator role. Open the reminder settings Go to Manage → Notifications and find Reminders and overdue notices. If you see Scheduled emails are not switched on, no reminders, overdue notices, manager escalations or feedback reminders are sent yet. You can still set them up here. Contact TMRW support to switch on scheduled emails for your organisation. Set the send time Time zone shows your organisation's time zone. If it's wrong, contact TMRW support. Set the Daily send time. A day that's missed isn't sent late. Set upcoming deadline reminders Turn on Upcoming deadline reminders. Under Reminders before the due date, add up to 10 reminders by entering Days before the due date and clicking Add another. The default is 14 days and 3 days before. Mandatory learning is always reminded. Also tick Recommended learning with a due date or Self-enrolled learning if you want those reminded too. A learner who has the same course more than once, for example directly and through a group, gets one reminder. Set overdue reminders Turn on Overdue reminders, then set Repeat every (days) (1–30, default 7) and Maximum reminders (1–20, default 4). Overdue reminders are only sent for mandatory learning, because recommended learning is never overdue. Check the preview Under Schedule preview, change Example due date to see the dates each reminder would be sent. Save Click Save changes at the top of the page. The Deadline reminder and Overdue notice emails below the schedule show On or Off to match. To change their wording, click Edit template. To tell line managers about learning that stays overdue, see Turn on manager escalation.

Manager escalation emails a person's line manager when their mandatory learning is still overdue after a set number of overdue reminders. It's off until you turn it on. You need the Organisation administrator role. Check overdue reminders are on Escalation counts overdue reminders, so Overdue reminders must be on. See Set up learning reminders. Scheduled emails must also be switched on for your organisation. If you see Scheduled emails are not switched on, contact TMRW support. Turn on escalation Go to Manage → Notifications and find Manager escalation. Turn on Escalate overdue learning to line managers. Set the threshold In Overdue reminders before escalating, enter a number from 1 to 10. The default is 2. Only reminders that were delivered count; failed or blocked emails don't. Note: Once this is saved, line managers are emailed about real people's overdue learning at the next daily check. Check who gets it and when The email goes to the person's current line manager, the same manager who sees them in My team. It's sent at the daily check after the threshold is reached, once for each assignment. It covers mandatory learning and older learning with no classification. Completing, withdrawing or renewing the learning, a new due date, or the person leaving stops an escalation that hasn't been sent yet. Save Click Save changes at the top of the page. To change the email's wording, click Edit template on the Manager escalation email in this section. Check the last daily check Last daily check shows how many escalations were sent and why any weren't, for example No line manager recorded or Manager has no email address. Escalations that weren't sent are tried again at the next daily check. To fix a missing manager, see Set a line manager.

The audit log records administrative actions and changes: who did what, to what, and when. Automatic actions, such as an HR sync disabling someone, are recorded too. You need the Organisation administrator role. Open the audit log Go to Manage → Audit log. Entries are listed newest first, with When, Category, Action, Target, Details and By. Find an entry Type in Search actions, targets and people, or choose a Category: Course, Assignment, Channel, Pathway, Role, Certificate, User or System. The Details column says what changed. For example, the reason you give when you disable an account appears there. The audit log shows the latest 500 entries and can't be edited.

You can add a person to a school, department or other organisation, for example someone who works across two schools. You need the Learning manager or Organisation administrator role. Learning managers can add people to the organisations they're responsible for. Start adding In Manage ▸ People, click Add to an organisation. You can also choose Add to an organisation from a person's row menu or their details, which fills in the person for you. Choose the person Under Person, search by name or email. You can add people who have signed in, and people imported from HR who haven't signed in yet. Adding someone to an organisation gives them no access by itself. Choose the organisation and end date Under Organisation, choose where they belong. To make it temporary, enter an End date (optional): the last day they belong to it. Leave it empty to keep them until someone ends it. Add them Click Add to organisation. The membership starts straight away and shows Added by admin on the People list. Active learning rules check the person again, so they may be assigned learning for their new organisation. You can't add someone who's disabled, or who already belongs to that organisation for the same dates.

You can ask someone to renew completed learning before it expires, for example after a policy change. You need the HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the assignment In Manage ▸ Learning assignments, find the completed assignment, open the row menu and choose View details. Assign the renewal Under History, click Assign renewal now on the completed cycle. The button only appears when the learning can be renewed. Check the result A message confirms the renewal, or says the person already has one. The renewal is a new cycle, due on the date the previous completion expires. No email is sent. Earlier completions and certificates stay on record.

Bulk assignment gives a course to everyone in one or more organisations at once. You need the Learning manager or Organisation administrator role. Bulk assignment is off unless TMRW support has turned it on for your organisation; until then the form says Bulk assignments unavailable. Open the form In Manage ▸ Learning assignments, click Assign learning, then choose Assign to ▸ Organisations. Choose the organisations and course Under Learner organisations, choose one or more organisations. Tick Include child organisations to include the schools or departments below them. Under Course, choose a published course. Choose mandatory or recommended, and a due date Choose Mandatory or Recommended under Classification. A Due date (optional) applies only to new assignments: people who already have the course keep their due date, progress and completion. Start the assignment Click Start assignment. GrowthXP finds the people in the background, then assigns the course. It checks each person's organisation and the course audience, and skips anyone who isn't eligible or already has the course. You can close the window and check back later. Check the results The window shows Scan progress, Recipients found and Assignment progress, then Learner results with each person's Result, an Explanation and What you can do. Assignments made this way stay in Growth Experience Platform and aren't sent to your HR system.

You can assign a course to one person at a time. You need the Learning manager, HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Learning managers assign to people in the organisations they're responsible for; HR managers and administrators can assign to anyone. Open the form In Manage ▸ Learning assignments, click Assign learning. If you see Assign to, choose People. Choose where to find the person If you assign in more than one organisation, choose one under Find people in, and tick Include child organisations to include the schools or departments below it. HR managers and administrators can choose Whole organisation. Choose the person and course Under Person, search by name or email. You can assign to people imported from HR who haven't signed in yet. Under Course, choose a published course. GrowthXP checks that the person can see the course; if not, This person cannot access the course explains why. An assignment never overrides a course's audience. Choose mandatory or recommended Under Classification, your organisation's default is preselected. Mandatory counts towards compliance and becomes overdue after its due date. Recommended is never overdue. Set a due date and assign Enter a Due date (optional) and click Assign learning. If the person already has the course, nothing changes, unless you chose Mandatory for a course they had as recommended: then it becomes mandatory for them, and the message says so.

You can give someone more time, or bring a deadline forward. You need the HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Open Change due date In Manage ▸ Learning assignments, find the assignment, open the row menu and choose Change due date. You can also click Change due date in the assignment's details. Completed learning has no due date to change. Pick the date Choose the new Due date. Mandatory learning becomes overdue from the day after this date. Recommended learning is never overdue. Save it Click Save due date. A message confirms the new date. Reminders follow the new date, and an overdue escalation email that hasn't been sent yet is cancelled.

You can look back at bulk assignments and see who was assigned or skipped. You need the Learning manager or Organisation administrator role. Learning managers see the jobs they started. Open the history In Manage ▸ Learning assignments, click Bulk assignment history. Choose a job Under Assignment history, choose a job. Each one shows the course, when it was requested and its status. Read the results The progress bars show how many people were found and processed: how many were assigned, skipped and failed. Learner results lists each person with their Result (Assigned, Skipped, Not recorded, Not processed or Pending), an Explanation, and What you can do. For example, someone who already had the course is skipped and needs nothing more. Close it Click Close. If you need help from support, open Support reference to find the job's reference.

You can end a membership that was added in GrowthXP. You need the Learning manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the person's details In Manage ▸ People, click the person's name. End the membership Under Organisations, click End membership next to the organisation. Only memberships added in Growth Experience Platform have this button. Memberships from HR say "Managed by HR sync — change it in HR." Confirm Click End membership. The person no longer belongs to that organisation, and it moves to Past in their details. Their learning records stay. If it was their last organisation, they belong to the whole organisation again. Active learning rules check the person again, so open mandatory learning that only applied to that organisation may be withdrawn.

The summary above Learning assignments gives exact counts for the learning in view, and each tile works as a filter. You need the Learning manager, Report viewer, HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Read the counts The tiles count Overdue, Due in the next 30 days, In progress and Completed learning for the organisation and filters you've chosen. Overdue is highlighted when it's above 0. Learning due in the next 30 days is also counted as not started or in progress; overdue learning is counted only as overdue. Filter by a tile Click a tile to show only that status in the list. The Status filter changes to match. Click the same tile again to show every status. Choose a smaller organisation if the counts don't show For very large organisations the tiles show a dash and a message that counts are shown only up to a number of people. Choose a smaller organisation under Show people in to see them. The list below is always current.

The filters narrow the deadlines calendar to what you need, such as overdue mandatory learning in one school. You need the Line manager, Learning manager, Report viewer, HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Choose the event types Under Event types, choose any of Assignment due, Feedback due, Expiry and Renewal due. If you clear them all, the calendar asks you to choose at least one. Narrow by status and course Under Status, choose states such as Assignment overdue, Feedback pending or Expiry: expiring soon. Under Classification, choose Mandatory or Recommended. Under Course source, choose Created in the LMS or From HR. Under Channel, choose one or more channels. Narrow by people Under School or organisation, choose units within the people in view. Under Staff category, choose categories such as Teacher or Support staff. Set a date range Enter Due from and Due to. If the range is outside the month you're looking at, the calendar offers a button to go to that month. Clear the filters Choices within one filter are combined with "or"; different filters must all match. If nothing matches, the calendar says No deadlines match these filters. Click Clear filters to start again.

The People page lists everyone in the organisations you can see: where they belong and whether they've signed in. You need the Learning manager or Organisation administrator role. Open People Click Manage in the header, then People under Organisation. The table title shows how many people are in view, for example "248 people". Choose the organisation Under Show people in, choose an organisation. Learning managers see the organisations they're responsible for. Include child organisations is ticked where you can see them, so choosing a trust or region also shows its schools. The line under the field says exactly who's included, for example "Members of Riverside Secondary School and its child organisations." Search and filter Type a name or email in Search. Under Status, the default Signed in or not yet shows everyone who can use GrowthXP. Choose Signed in, Not signed in yet (imported from HR and waiting for their first sign-in), Disabled, or All, including disabled. Read the list Each row shows the person's name and email, their Status, and the Organisations they currently belong to. From HR means the membership comes from your HR system; Added by admin means someone added it in Growth Experience Platform. Hover over Disabled to see why the account was disabled. Open their details Click the person's name, or click the row menu and choose View details. Click Refresh list to reload the page after changes made elsewhere.

You can withdraw learning that was assigned in GrowthXP. You need the Learning manager, HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Learning managers can remove learning for people in the organisations they're responsible for. Choose Remove In Manage ▸ Learning assignments, open the row menu and choose Remove. You can also click Remove assignment in the assignment's details. Check whether it can be removed here You can remove learning that an administrator or manager assigned, one by one or in bulk, and learning someone enrolled in themselves. Learning from HR shows "Managed by HR — cancel the registration in HR". Learning from a rule shows "Assigned by rule" and the rule's name, because the rule would assign it again: change the rule or the person's details instead. Confirm Read the message, then click Remove assignment. Any progress, completion and certificate stay on record. If other sources also require the course, such as a learning rule, only what was assigned in GrowthXP is removed and the person keeps the course; the dialog says Stays assigned when this will happen.

When many people have the same course due on the same day, the deadlines calendar shows it once, so a course due for hundreds of people stays one line. You need the Line manager, Learning manager, Report viewer, HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Find the course In Manage ▸ Deadlines calendar, find the course on its day. The line shows the type of deadline, the course, the number of people and how many are in each state, for example "1 overdue · 3 in progress · 20 not started". The most urgent state is shown at the end. Open it Click the course. The panel on the right shows the date, the number of People, and a count for each state. People lists everyone, most urgent first. For more than 50 people, use Search people to find someone. Open a person Click a person to see their own deadline, with their classification and learning cycle. Click Back to all people to return to the group. Work on the list Click View in Learning assignments to open the list of assignments for that course, filtered to the same people. It's shown when you're looking at Everyone or An organisation; line reports don't have this link.
documents.s: See who is due for a course

documents.t: Every assignment is either Mandatory or Recommended. This classification belongs to the assignment or learning rule, never to the course itself, so the same course can be mandatory for some people and recommended for others. It's for anyone who assigns or reports on learning. Know what mandatory means Mandatory learning is required. It counts towards compliance, so it can be Compliant, Due, Overdue or Expired. People get reminders before and after the due date, and if your organisation has turned on manager escalation, their line manager is told when it stays overdue. Know what recommended means Recommended learning is suggested and shows in the person's My courses. It's never overdue, and its due date is optional. Courses people enrol themselves in are recommended. Know what "Not set" means Not set marks assignments made before classification existed. They're treated as mandatory for compliance, reminders and escalation. Know which one is preselected When you assign a course, the form preselects your organisation's default classification. You can change it each time. Organisation administrators and HR managers set the default in Learning rules ▸ Settings. Know what happens when sources overlap A person can be given the same course by several sources, such as a learning rule, an administrator and HR. They still have one assignment. It's mandatory if any source says so, and due by the earliest mandatory due date. The assignment's details list every source under Why they have it.

The deadlines calendar shows when learning is due, when course feedback is due, and when completions expire or need renewing, for the people you can see. You need the Line manager, Learning manager, Report viewer, HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the calendar Click Manage in the header, then Deadlines calendar under Organisation. It opens on the widest group of people you can see. Choose whose deadlines to show Under People, choose Your line reports (if people report to you), An organisation (learning managers and report viewers) or Everyone (HR managers and organisation administrators). For An organisation, choose it under Organisation; if you have only one, it's chosen for you. Tick or clear Include child organisations. Changing People clears the School or organisation and Staff category filters. Choose the month and view Use Previous month, Today and Next month. The Month tab shows a grid; click a day to list its deadlines underneath. The Agenda tab lists every day in the month that has deadlines, with "(today)" on today. Open a deadline Click a deadline to see it in the panel on the right. Deadlines for the same course on the same day are grouped: see See who is due for a course. Dates are calendar dates in UTC. Share the view The month, view and filters are kept in the page address, so you can bookmark or share it. Someone else only sees the people they're allowed to see.

A person's details show who they are, every organisation they belong to or belonged to, and the roles they hold. You need the Learning manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the details In Manage ▸ People, click the person's name. Person details opens on the right. Check who they are The top of the panel shows their Email, Status, Job title and HR record (Linked to HR or Not linked to HR). For a disabled account, Reason says why and since when. Check their organisations Organisations lists the organisations they belong to now, with dates and where each membership came from. Starting later lists memberships that haven't started yet, and Past lists the ones that have ended. A membership from HR says "Managed by HR sync — change it in HR." Someone with no organisation belongs to the whole organisation. Check their roles Roles lists any roles they hold, such as Learning manager for a school. Line manager shows as "Automatic, from the manager hierarchy". Everyone who signs in is a learner, so a person with no roles shows "No roles. Everyone who signs in is a learner." Check employment and account If you can see the whole organisation, Employment shows their staff category, line manager and employments, and Account lets an administrator disable or re-enable the account. The Access and permissions section of this help covers those tasks.

An assignment's details show why the person has the course, how far they've got, and every cycle of it. You need the Learning manager, Report viewer, HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the details In Manage ▸ Learning assignments, click the row menu and choose View details. Assignment details opens on the right with the course name as the title. Read the summary The top shows the Person, Status, Classification, Due date and when it was Assigned. A renewal shows its Cycle. See why they have it Why they have it lists each source: a learning rule, an administrator, a bulk assignment, HR or self-enrolment, with its classification, due date and who added it. When several sources require the course, it's mandatory if any of them says so and due by the earliest mandatory due date. Check their progress Progress shows the status and percentage, Last activity, Score, Completed date, Validity, Certificate number and Feedback. Check the history History lists every cycle of the course, with its status and dates. The current cycle has a Current tag. Change or remove it Use Change due date or Remove assignment at the bottom, if your role allows. These open their own window and close the details.

Learning assignments is one list of everyone's learning: who has which course, how far they've got and when it's due. You need the Learning manager, Report viewer, HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Report viewers can look but not change anything. Open Learning assignments Click Manage in the header, then Learning assignments under Organisation. Choose whose learning to see Under Show people in, choose an organisation. HR managers and organisation administrators start on Whole organisation; learning managers and report viewers start on the first organisation they're responsible for. Tick or clear Include child organisations to include or leave out the schools and departments below it. Filter the list Type a person or course in Search. Choose a Course, a Status (Not started, In progress, Overdue, Due in the next 30 days or Completed), Mandatory or recommended (Mandatory, Recommended or Not set) and Assigned by (Learning rule, Admin, Bulk assignment, HR or Self-enrolled). Changing the organisation clears the course filter. Read each row Person links to the person's details; a Group tag means a group assignment. Course shows "Renewal 1", "Renewal 2" and so on under renewed learning. Status is a coloured tag, with Recorded in HR when the completion came from your HR system. Classification shows Mandatory, Recommended or "Not set". Due shows the date and a note such as "Due in 5 days", "Due today" or "Overdue". Recommended learning past its date shows "Due date passed" because it's never overdue. Assigned by shows who or what assigned it. Act on a row Click the row menu to View details. HR managers and organisation administrators also see Change due date. Remove appears for people who can remove assignments. Click Refresh list to reload.

The totals table compares compliance across courses, schools or staff categories. You need the Line manager, Learning manager, Report viewer, HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Choose the breakdown In Manage ▸ Learning reports, under Totals by, choose Course, School or Staff category. Read the table Each row shows its People and Learning, how much is Not started, In progress and Completed, and for mandatory learning how much is compliant, Due, Overdue and Expired. People in more than one school are counted under each school, so school rows can add up to more than the totals. Calculate totals for large reports For more than 2,000 people, the page says Totals are calculated in the background. Click Calculate totals. The rows below still load page by page while you wait, and the line above the totals says when they were calculated. Totals are reused for an hour.

You can download a learning report as a CSV file. You need the Line manager, Learning manager, Report viewer, HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Learning managers and report viewers export the learning of the organisations they're given, and of their child units only if their access includes them. Set up the report In Manage ▸ Learning reports, choose People and set the filters. The export contains exactly what you've filtered. Choose the export Click Export detail for one row per person and course, including completion source, expiry, feedback and certificate number. Click Export summary for the totals by course, school and staff category. Download it For up to 2,000 people the file downloads straight away. For more, a message says Your export is being prepared and the file appears under Exports at the bottom of the page as Detail export or Summary export. Its Status goes from Queued to Preparing… to Ready. Then click the Download icon within 24 hours. Note: Only you can download your export, and each file is deleted when it expires, 24 hours after it's ready. Download it before the date under Available until. Tidy up Click the delete icon to Cancel export while it's being prepared, or Delete file once it's ready. You can have up to three exports being prepared at once.

Filters narrow a learning report, for example to overdue mandatory learning for teachers in one school. You need the Line manager, Learning manager, Report viewer, HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Use the main filters In Manage ▸ Learning reports, type a name or email in Search people, or choose a School or organisation, Staff category, Course, Classification (Mandatory, Recommended or Not assigned), Status (Not started, In progress or Completed) and Compliance (Compliant, Due, Overdue or Expired). The choices only include people and courses in the report. Use more filters Click More filters to add Validity (for example Expiring soon), Feedback (for example Overdue), Learner status and the Assigned, Due and Completed date ranges. Learner status includes everyone by default; choose Deactivated or disabled to see people who've left or whose account is disabled. Include earlier cycles Tick Include earlier cycles to add previous cycles of renewed courses to the detail and exports. Totals always count current learning only. Clear the filters Choices within one filter are combined with "or"; different filters must all match. Click Clear filters to start again, or Fewer filters to hide the extra ones.

Learning reports shows course completion and mandatory compliance for the people you can report on, with totals and a detailed list. You need the Line manager, Learning manager, Report viewer, HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Open Learning reports Click Manage in the header, then Learning reports under Organisation. Choose whose learning to report on Under People, choose Everyone (HR managers and organisation administrators), An organisation (learning managers and report viewers) or Your line reports (if people report to you). For An organisation, choose it under Organisation and tick or clear Include child organisations. Until you choose an organisation, the page asks you to. Read the totals Totals shows the People with learning in the report, their Learning (current courses, one per person), how much is Completed, how much mandatory learning is compliant, and how much is Overdue or Expired. Overdue and Expired count mandatory learning only. Read the detail People and courses lists one row per person and course, with their School, Staff category, Classification, Cycle, Status, Compliance, Due date, Validity and Feedback. Click Show more to load more rows. Refresh the data The line above the totals says when the data was read, for example "Data as of 25 Oct 2026, 09:30." Click Refresh to read it again.

The overview is the first page of Manage: learning activity, compliance and the state of the catalogue at a glance. You need the Course manager, HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Open the overview Click Manage in the header, or Overview in the side navigation. Under Period, choose All time, Last 30 days, Last 90 days or Last 12 months. Act on overdue learning If any learning is overdue, a message says how many assignments are overdue. Click View assignments to open Learning assignments. Read At a glance Overdue counts learning not completed by its due date. Completion rate shows how many assignments are completed. Learners counts people assigned at least one course, and Assignments counts assignments across all courses. Read Catalogue In pipeline counts courses processing or still in draft, Ready counts courses available to learners, and Total courses counts the whole catalogue. Failed or Quarantined appear only when a course needs attention. Read engagement and attention Course engagement shows Learners who opened a course, Sessions, Completions and the Average completion rate, with courses ranked by learners. Requires attention lists courses below full completion, lowest first. Recently added courses lists the newest courses and their status.

HR managers and administrators can see compliance and course charts on the Manage overview, without opening Learning reports. You need the HR manager or Organisation administrator role. Course managers see only the overview. Open the Compliance tab Click Manage in the header, then the Compliance tab. It's the same report as Learning reports, with the same People choice, filters, totals and exports. See Open learning reports. Open the Courses tab Click the Courses tab for charts across the whole organisation: Completion overview, Course performance (courses per channel, completion rate and average score per course), Activity trends (learner activity in the last 30 days), Skills and channels, and Assignment growth (assignments created in the last 6 months). Go back to the overview Click the Overview tab to return to the at-a-glance tiles.
Common problems in GrowthXP, one page each. Pick the one that matches what you see.

Signing in, your courses, due dates and certificates. I can't sign in: "Your organisation isn't licensed" I can't sign in: "Your account has been disabled" I don't see Manage in the header My new role isn't showing I can't see a course My course has no due date A course says "Recorded in HR" and has no certificate My certificate hasn't been issued

Manage pages, assignments, calendars and reports, teams, access and emails. A page I expect is missing from Manage I can't remove an assignment I can't change a due date or export a report The deadlines calendar or learning report is empty Someone is missing from My team I can't change someone's line manager A role isn't offered in Give access "Access changes are not enabled" I can't find someone in Give access Someone has "Old report viewer (no effect)" No emails are being sent Reminders aren't being sent A manager escalation wasn't sent Feedback reminders aren't being sent

The connection to Dynamics 365 HR and the syncs that run over it. "User sync is paused" A sync says "Not activated" or "Unavailable" Test connection fails Syncing stopped after I changed the connection Someone wasn't imported Someone was disabled but still works for us Someone is in the wrong school Someone shows "Pending: missing email" Staff are in "People needing review" A course wasn't sent to HR Learner status updates are skipped A completion from HR wasn't imported Enrolments aren't going to HR A sync run says "Details removed after 7 days" A sync failed

Cause — An administrator disabled your account, or the HR sync disabled it because HR no longer lists you as active in a current position. Fix — Your learning records are kept. Ask your administrator to check. If HR has you wrong, it's fixed in HR, and the next HR sync re-enables you automatically. If an administrator disabled you, they re-enable you in People.
documents.s: I can't sign in: "Your account has been disabled"

documents.t: Cause — Each course has an audience, and you only see courses whose audience includes your school or organisation, or that are assigned to you. Some courses are only visible to people they're assigned to. Unpublished (draft) courses aren't visible to learners. Fix — Ask your learning manager or course manager to assign it to you, or to check the course's audience and that it's published.

Cause — Your organisation, or the course, needs your course feedback before the certificate is issued. Or the course has no certificate. Fix — Open the course and give your feedback. The certificate is issued as soon as valid feedback is submitted.

Cause — Recommended learning usually has no due date. Learning rules give recommended learning a due date only if Give recommended learning a due date is on, and an administrator can assign learning without one. Fix — Expected. Recommended learning is never overdue, with or without a due date. If the learning should be mandatory, ask your learning manager or HR manager.
documents.s: My course has no due date

documents.t: Cause — Manage only appears if you have a role beyond learner, or people report to you. Everyone else is a learner. Fix — Expected for most staff. If you should have a role, ask your organisation administrator. See Understand the roles.
documents.s: I don't see Manage in the header

documents.t: Cause — The page was loaded before the role was given. Fix — Reload the page. If it still doesn't show, ask the administrator to check Who has access, including Where the role applies.

Cause — GrowthXP isn't available for the organisation your Microsoft account belongs to, or you signed in with a personal or different work account. Fix — Sign in with your work Microsoft account. If the message stays, ask your administrator to contact TMRW support to check your organisation's access.
documents.s: I can't sign in: "Your organisation isn't licensed"

documents.t: Cause — The course was completed outside the platform and recorded in your HR system, so the platform has no evidence or certificate for it. Fix — Expected. The completion still counts. If you need a certificate, complete the course in the platform; that completion replaces the HR record.
documents.s: A course says "Recorded in HR" and has no certificate

documents.t: Cause — Giving access is switched off for your organisation. Fix — Contact TMRW support.

Cause — If you're a learning manager or report viewer, you choose which organisation to look at, and nothing is shown until you choose one. The calendar says No organisation chosen, and the report says Choose an organisation. Fix — Choose your school or unit in Organisation, and tick Include child organisations if you want the units below it. In the calendar, also check at least one event type is chosen.
documents.s: The deadlines calendar or learning report is empty

documents.t: Cause — Changing due dates is for HR managers and organisation administrators. Learning managers and report viewers can export reports, but only for the organisations they're given, so the export buttons don't appear for other organisations. Fix — For a due date, ask an HR manager or administrator. For an export, choose one of your own organisations under People, or ask an administrator to check where your role applies. See Understand the roles.
documents.s: I can't change a due date or export a report

documents.t: Cause — The person's Employment section says Maintained by your HR integration and has no Edit employment details, or the form says Line manager maintained by your HR integration. The manager comes from HR and updates with each sync. Fix — Change the manager in HR. It's updated at the next HR sync.
documents.s: I can't change someone's line manager

documents.t: Cause — The person hasn't been imported from HR yet, or your directory couldn't be searched. In that case the form says Directory not searched. Fix — Search by their work email. If they're a new starter, import them with Individual HR lookup first. See Look up a person in HR.
documents.s: I can't find someone in Give access

documents.t: Cause — Learning registered in HR, or assigned by a learning rule, can't be removed in Learning assignments, because HR or the rule would assign it again. The message says which: "Managed by HR — cancel the registration in HR" or "Assigned by rule … — change the rule or the person's details". Fix — Cancel the registration in HR, or change the learning rule or the person's details.

Cause — Escalation is off by default, or the person has no line manager who can be emailed. Last daily check shows the reasons, such as No line manager recorded or Manager has no email address. Fix — Turn escalation on and fix the line manager. It's tried again at the next daily check. See Turn on manager escalation.
Cause — There's no feedback deadline, so no feedback reminders are sent. Fix — Set a deadline in Settings → Course feedback. See Set course feedback rules.

Cause — My team shows the people who report to you in the manager hierarchy, and everyone below them. Disabled people are left out. Fix — Ask your administrator to check the person's line manager in People, or ask HR if line managers come from HR. See Set a line manager.
documents.s: Someone is missing from My team

documents.t: Cause — The Delivery and branding section shows why: Emails are switched off for your organisation, or a delivery tag of Not sent or Not set up. Fix — Contact TMRW support to switch emails on for your organisation.
Cause — An older role that gives nothing beyond a learner. Fix — See Replace an old report viewer grant.

Cause — Each page under Manage belongs to particular roles. For example, Notifications, Settings and Audit log are for organisation administrators, and Learning rules for HR managers, course managers and administrators. Fix — Check what your role includes on Access and permissions → Roles explained, or ask your organisation administrator.
documents.s: A page I expect is missing from Manage

documents.t: Cause — Scheduled emails are not switched on for your organisation, or Upcoming deadline reminders or Overdue reminders are off. Overdue reminders are only for mandatory learning, and recommended or self-enrolled learning is only reminded if it's ticked. Fix — Check the reminder schedule on Notifications. Contact TMRW support to switch on scheduled emails. See Set up learning reminders.
Cause — You can only give roles whose permissions you hold yourself. The form lists the hidden roles under Not shown with the reason. Fix — Ask another organisation administrator to give it.
documents.s: A role isn't offered in Give access

documents.t: Cause — The HR course title isn't mapped, the person has no verified HR identity, or the course is still a draft. Fix — Check the reason in the preview, then map the title or publish the course.
documents.s: A completion from HR wasn't imported

documents.t: Cause — It has no start and end offering dates, and HR needs them, so it was skipped. Fix — Add Offering dates to the course. It's sent at the next sync.
documents.s: A course wasn't sent to HR

documents.t: Cause — In HR, they're inactive, have only temporary positions, or have no current employment. Fix — Correct the record in HR. The next sync re-enables them automatically. To restore access straight away, re-enable the account in People. The next complete sync disables it again unless HR lists them by then.
documents.s: Someone was disabled but still works for us

documents.t: Cause — Writes to the HR participant record are held until your F&O team approves them. The row shows To HR as Held. Fix — Nothing is lost while writes are held. Contact TMRW support when your F&O team is ready to approve them.
