Open Onboarding checklists From the Dynamics 365 (D365) navigation pane, go to Modules ▸ Human Resources ▸ Task Management ▸ Onboarding checklists. Select or create a checklist Select an existing checklist to modify, or click New to create one. Edit the checklist Click Edit to enter edit mode. For each task, configure: Task name and description Assigned to — a specific person, a user group, or left blank for manual assignment at hire Due date offset from start date — the due date, calculated as a number of days relative to the employee's start date Assign to a group If using a group assignment, right-click to View Details to see its members filtered by legal entity. Select one member and click Make Primary — tasks route to the primary only, not all group members. If the primary has an active delegation configured, the delegated person automatically receives the task. Save Click Save to apply the configuration.

The Personnel action types form controls which hire action types automatically trigger an onboarding checklist when a worker completes an action. Enable this flag on each relevant action type. Open Personnel action types In Dynamics 365 (D365), search for and open Personnel action types. Locate the hire action type Filter or scroll to find the action type used for new hires — for example, Regular. Enable the checklist flag Enable the Auto apply onboarding checklist flag for this action type. When a worker completes this action type, the system automatically applies the nominated onboarding checklist to the new employee record. Save Click Save. Repeat for any additional action types that should trigger onboarding checklist assignment.
documents.s: Configure personnel action types for onboarding

documents.t: Pre-onboarding checklists define tasks that must be completed by Human Resources (HR) and support teams before a new employee's start date — for example, collecting credentials or sending welcome documents. These checklists are assigned when the hire worker action is processed, and tasks are visible in both the Dynamics 365 (D365) task management workspace and EmployeeXP. Pre-onboarding checklists are configured separately from onboarding checklists. They follow the same structure but are scoped to tasks that occur before the employee joins. Open Pre-onboarding checklists From the D365 navigation pane, go to Modules ▸ Human Resources ▸ Task Management ▸ Pre-onboarding checklists. Select or create a checklist Select an existing checklist to modify, or click New to create one. Edit the checklist Click Edit to enter edit mode. For each task, configure: Task name and description Assigned to — a specific person or a user group (see Configure task user groups for group setup) Company — the legal entity (school) this task applies to. Tasks with no company set apply to all legal entities. Offset date — the number of days before the target date by which the task should be completed. When the checklist is assigned on a worker action, the system calculates individual task due dates automatically from this offset. Set dependencies (optional) If a task should be blocked until another task is finished, scroll right to the Dependency column and select the prerequisite task. See Set checklist task dependencies for full steps. Save Click Save to apply the configuration.

Tasks within an onboarding checklist can be scoped to specific legal entities (schools), so only relevant tasks appear for employees at each school. Tasks with no company restriction apply to all schools. Open the onboarding checklist Go to Modules ▸ Human Resources ▸ Task Management ▸ Onboarding checklists and select the relevant checklist. Select the task to scope Click the task you want to restrict to specific schools. Set the applicable companies In the Company field, select one or more legal entities (schools) this task applies to. Employees onboarding at other schools will not see this task on their checklist. Save Click Save to apply the change.

User groups allow multiple employees to be assigned to a checklist task together. When any one member of the group completes the task, it is automatically marked complete and removed from the task lists of all other group members. The Resolved By column in the task management workspace records which group member completed the task. This is useful for Human Resources (HR) and admin teams where several people share responsibility for tasks such as collecting documents or setting up system access. Open User Groups From the Dynamics 365 (D365) navigation pane, go to Modules ▸ Human resources ▸ Task management ▸ Group assignment. Select or create a group Select an existing group to update, or click New to create a group. Give the group a meaningful name that reflects its role or school (for example, WSO HR Pre-Onboarding Team). Add members In the group detail view, the employee list shows all available members filtered by legal entity. Use the available filters to narrow the list by position, job title, or name, then select the employees to add to the group. Save Click Save to apply the group membership. Groups are scoped by legal entity — employees from other schools are not visible unless their legal entity context is switched. Assign this group to checklist tasks in the Assigned To field when configuring an onboarding or pre-onboarding checklist.

Dependencies prevent a task from being completed until a prerequisite task is finished first — for example, setting up a laptop depends on the Active Directory account being created. Open the checklist Go to Modules ▸ Human Resources ▸ Task Management ▸ Onboarding checklists, select the relevant checklist, and click Edit. Select the task to configure Click on the task that should be blocked until another task is completed first. Add a dependency Click Set Dependency and select the task that must be completed beforehand. A task can have multiple dependencies. Save Click Save to apply the configuration. In EmployeeXP, employees will see the dependent task in their list but it is locked until all dependency tasks are complete. The task detail view shows which tasks are blocking progress and who is responsible for completing them.

The Human Resources parameters form controls which onboarding checklist is applied automatically when a hire worker action is completed, and how many days the new employee has to complete their onboarding tasks. Open Human Resources parameters In Dynamics 365 (D365), in the Human Resources module, under Setup, open Human Resources parameters. Go to the Recruitment tab Select the Recruitment tab on the left. Nominate the default onboarding checklist In the Onboarding checklist field, select the checklist to apply automatically when a hire worker action of the configured type is completed. Only one checklist can be nominated as the default. Set the completion period In the Number of days field, enter the number of days the new employee has to complete their onboarding tasks from their start date. Save Click Save.

Some onboarding tasks cannot be started until other tasks are finished first — for example, configuring your laptop depends on your Active Directory account being set up. Tasks with unmet dependencies are visible but locked until the prerequisites are done. Identify a blocked task In your task list, a task with unresolved dependencies clearly shows it cannot be progressed yet. Open the blocked task Click on the task to open its detail view. Review the dependencies The detail view shows: The list of dependency tasks that must be completed first The current status of each dependency Who each dependency is assigned to The target completion date for each dependency Wait for dependencies to clear You cannot complete the blocked task until all listed dependency tasks are finished. If a task is overdue, contact the person responsible for the dependency to follow up.

The growth and performance matrix is the grid employees are placed on during the year — GEMS Star, High Performer, Inconsistent - Talent Risk and the rest. Each measure occupies a box on the matrix, the employee gets rated into a particular box. The layout is not fixed. Each measure's position on the grid is configurable, so you can match the matrix to the framework your organisation has agreed. Open the matrix setup In Dynamics 365 (D365), type Growth and performance matrix into the search box at the top of the screen and open the result. Or follow the pathway: Human resources ▸ Competencies ▸ Setup ▸ Growth and performance matrix. Review the measures The matrix defines the Measures and identifies their Performance Matrix Positions. The positions of each measure can be edited Keep each value to one box Define each value only once across the matrix—the system enforces this, so you cannot place the same measure in two boxes. If you are moving measures around, clear a value from its old position before reusing it. This form configures the matrix but is not where you use it. Human Resources (HR) and managers place employees on the matrix and move them between boxes from the manager view in EmployeeXP — see Use the growth and performance matrix in the EmployeeXP guide. The placements made there are written back to the employee's talent review record in D365, covered in View talent review records.
documents.s: Configure the growth and performance matrix

documents.t: Employees don't create reviews —Human Resources (HR) or Information Technology (IT) releases them across the organisation by running a batch job. You run it once per stage: once to release goal setting, again for the mid-year review, and again for the end-of-year review. Find the batch job In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to System administration ▸ Periodic tasks ▸ GEMS periodic ▸ Batch and open the Performance review job. All custom batch jobs—probation, performance, talent review—are grouped here, so this is the one place to look rather than searching for each job by name. Select the performance period Choose the period you are releasing — goal setting, mid-year review, or end-of-year review — and enter its Start date and End date. For a goal-setting run, these would be the period dates you configured, for example, 1 January to 31 March. Set the creation date The Creation date must fall inside the date range of the performance period you selected. A creation date outside the period will not produce reviews, so check this before running the job — it is the most common reason a run comes back empty. Select the review template Choose the review Template that matches the period. Releasing the goal-setting period with the mid-year template attached produces reviews with the wrong goals, and the mismatch isn't obvious until employees open them. Choose who the reviews are generated for To generate for a single employee, expand Records to include and enter their Personnel number. This is useful for testing or for catching up one person. Leave the personnel number blank to generate reviews for everyone in the legal entity. This is the normal run at the start of a stage. Run the job Click OK. The job creates one review per employee in scope, with the goals from the review template already copied onto each one. Check the results Go to Human Resources ▸ Performance ▸ Reviews and refresh. Your generated reviews appear in the list. Open one and check that the goals have copied across — a template with seven goals should produce a review with those seven goals populated. Once generated, the reviews appear in EmployeeXP for employees to complete. You can follow their progress from the same Reviews list — see Track performance reviews in D365.

When managers submit end-of-year reviews for calibration, each record lands in the calibration inquiry. It is the central list Human Resources (HR) uses to see how many records are waiting, what ratings they came in with, and how far along each one is in the release process. This form reports on calibration — the calibration itself is done from the HR view in EmployeeXP. Open the calibration inquiry In Dynamics 365 (D365), open the calibration inquiry under Human Resources ▸ Performance ▸ Calibration inquiry. Filter to the performance year Filter by performance year. Years accumulate as you use the system, so filtering keeps the list to the cycle you are working on. Read the columns Each line is one review submitted for calibration: Column What it tells you Review ID The review the record came from Employee ID The employee being calibrated Final employee rating The rating the manager gave at the point of submission Calibrated rating The rating after calibration — blank until the employee has been calibrated Manager The manager who submitted the review Released to manager Whether HR has released the calibrated ratings back to the manager Released to direct reports Whether the manager has published the ratings to their employees Identify who still needs calibrating A blank calibrated rating means that employee has not been calibrated yet. Filtering on blanks gives you the outstanding list. HR carries out calibration in EmployeeXP, HR view, where ratings are shown against the expected curve and can be adjusted — see Calibrate performance ratings in the EmployeeXP guide.

Goal templates are the library of goals available to your organisation. Nothing in the performance cycle works until this library exists — review templates pull their goals from here, and those goals are then copied onto every review the batch job generates. This setup is for Human Resources (HR), HR administrators, and Information Technology (IT) only. Employees never see these forms. Open the goal templates form In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Human Resources ▸ Performance ▸ Setup ▸ Goal templates. Create a goal Add a record for each goal you want available. Complete: Field What it holds Name The goal as it will appear to employees and managers Level The level the goal applies at Goal category The grouping the goal belongs to Status Whether the goal is currently available for use Goal classification The type of goal — see the next step Set the goal classification Goal classification is what separates the different kinds of goals your reviews carry — objectives, competencies, performance improvement plan (PIP) and personal development plan (PDP) goals all sit here. The classifications available come from the goal types already defined in the existing system, so the list mirrors what your organisation uses today. Add as many goals as you need There is no practical limit. Build out the full library before moving on — you can add more later, but doing it up front means your review templates are complete the first time. Once your library is in place, group the goals into the reviews that use them — see Set up review templates.

Performance periods divide the performance year into the stages you actually run. You select a period when you generate reviews, and the period dates control when you can create those reviews. Open the performance period form In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to the Performance period setup under Human Resources ▸ Performance ▸ Setup ▸ Performance period. Create a period for each stage Create three records — goal setting, mid-year review, and end-of-year review — and set the Start date and End date for each. For example, a goal-setting period might run 1 January to 31 March. The dates matter beyond record-keeping: when you generate reviews, the creation date you enter must fall inside the period's date range. See Generate performance reviews. Attach the performance year Set the Performance year on every period. This is the step most easily missed, and a period without its year attached does not function — link each one before you save. Note: Like the performance year itself, periods are set up once when the year starts and then left alone until the following year.

A review template defines one stage of the performance cycle — what goals it carries and how it is rated. You need one for each stage you run: goal setting, mid-year review and end-of-year review. Open the review templates form In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Human Resources ▸ Performance ▸ Setup ▸ Review templates. Create a template for each stage Create as many templates as needed. For example, create three templates — one for goal setting, one for the mid-year review, and one for the end-of-year review. Name each one for the stage it covers; you select the template by name when you generate reviews, so the naming needs to be unambiguous. Add the goal templates Open the template and use the + Add goal template button to bring in goal templates from your goal library. You are shown the list of goals already set up — select the ones this review should carry and click OK. Add every classification the stage needs. A goal-setting template, for example, typically includes both objectives and competencies. The goals you add here are copied onto each individual review when the batch job runs, so a template holding seven goals produces reviews with those seven goals already populated. Set the rating model Go to the General tab and select the Rating model the stage uses. The standard model applies unless your organisation has defined its own. Switch on the rating weight factor On the same tab, enable the rating weight factor. This allows the system to calculate an employee's average score and total score across the performance cycle — without it, the scores shown at the end-of-year review are not produced. Review templates are only half the setup—the system also needs to know which year and period a review belongs to. See Set up the performance year and calibration framework.

The performance year ties the whole cycle together — every review period and every generated review belongs to one. It also includes the calibration framework, the expected distribution of ratings Human Resources (HR) compares actual results against during calibration. This is a once-a-year task. Set it up when the school year starts, and it needs no further attention until the next year. Open the performance year form In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to the Performance year setup under Human Resources ▸ Performance ▸ Setup ▸ Performance year. Create the year Create a single record for the year and set: Field What it holds Start date The first day of the performance year End date The last day of the performance year Rating model The rating model used across the year — the standard model unless your organisation has its own You can choose the start and end dates, so the performance year can follow the school year rather than the calendar year. Open the Gaussian curve framework With the year selected, click Gaussian framework from the Action Pane. Enter the expected distribution Enter the percentage of employees expected to fall into each rating band. This is the curve calibration works against — during calibration, HR sees expected against actual side by side, so a band set to 20% showing 30% of employees is immediately visible as a gap. Set up the framework before the end-of-year reviews are submitted. Calibration has nothing to compare against until these percentages are in place. Next, divide the year into the stages you will run — see Set up performance periods.
documents.s: Set up the performance year and calibration framework

documents.t: The Reviews list is where Human Resources (HR) confirms the batch job worked and follows reviews as employees and managers complete them. Everything submitted from EmployeeXP is visible here, including comments and ratings from both sides. Open the Reviews list In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Human Resources ▸ Performance ▸ Reviews. If you just ran the batch job, refresh the list to load the new records. Check a review's status The status tells you where the review has reached: Status What it means Not started The review has been generated, but the employee has not submitted it Ready for review The employee has submitted; it is now with the manager Completed The manager has submitted their feedback and the stage is closed Status changes are driven by the standard workflow engine, so allow a moment after a submission before expecting the list to update. Open a review to see the details Open a record to see the goals it carries and the responses against each one. Both sides are visible — the employee's comments and the manager's comments sit together, so you can see the full exchange without switching screens. Manager comments are visible to HR here but are not all exposed to the employee in EmployeeXP. Check the ratings Go to the Ratings tab to see every rating recorded against the review, along with its weight. Scroll down for the totals — the weightings should sum to 100. Two things are worth knowing when reading this tab: PIP and PDP goals carry no rating and no weight. These are released ad hoc to support an employee's development, so they are deliberately excluded from the scoring. Total and average scores are calculated on submission. They show as zero or blank until the manager submits the end-of-year review, so an empty score mid-cycle is expected rather than a fault. Confirm goal setting has no manager rating At the goal-setting stage, the manager provides comments only — they do not give a rating. A goal-setting review with no manager ratings recorded is correct.

Talent reviews are completed from the EmployeeXP manager view, but Dynamics 365 (D365) stores the records against the employee. This gives Human Resources (HR) a full picture at any point in time without needing the EmployeeXP screens. Open the employee record In D365, go to Human Resources ▸ Workers ▸ Employees and open the employee. Go to the talent review In the Action Pane, go to the Work tab and under Talent review, click Employee talent mapping. Read the talent review detail The general information holds everything captured against the employee during the talent review: Field What it holds Comments The free-text notes recorded by HR or the manager Risk of loss How likely the employee is to leave Impact of loss The effect on the organisation if they did Position The employee's placement on the growth and performance matrix — key performer, high potential, or neutral Identified successor The person identified to succeed them Employee readiness How long until the successor is ready — for example, two years Every comment entered over time is visible here, so you can read the history, not just the latest entry. Open the attachments Click the Attachment button at the top of the record. Any file uploaded with the talent review in EmployeeXP is stored against the employee here. Check a matrix move has landed When an employee is moved between boxes on the growth and performance matrix in EmployeeXP, the new position is written to this record. If a move doesn't appear right away, wait a moment and refresh—the update isn't instant. The matrix itself is configured in D365 — see Configure the growth and performance matrix.

Probation review settings are configured by staff level and category, controlling when Stage 1 and Stage 2 reviews are triggered for different employee types. Open the probation configuration form In Dynamics 365 (D365), navigate to the Staff Levels for probation configuration (accessible from the Human Resources module setup area). Select a staff level and category combination Each row in the form represents a unique combination of Staff Level and Default category (for example, Teacher + Grade 1). Probation parameters differ per combination. Set the review days For the selected combination, configure: Probation Review Days — Stage 1: the number of days from the employee's start date when the Stage 1 review should be generated Probation Review Days — Stage 2: the number of days from the employee's start date when the Stage 2 review should be generated Select the review template In the Template field, select the review template to apply to this combination. The template defines which competencies are included and what rating model (e.g., Meets Expectations, Concerns, Needs Improvement) is used. Save Click Save to apply the configuration.

The Generate Probation Reviews batch process scans employee records for upcoming probation dates and creates the review records, routing them into the approval workflow for the assigned manager. Navigate to the batch process In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to System Administration ▸ Periodic tasks ▸ Batch and select Generate probation review. Set the horizon Enter a value in the Probation Horizon Days parameter. The batch generates reviews for any employee whose Stage 1 or Stage 2 probation date falls within this many days from today. For example, setting the horizon to 10 days will capture any review date falling within the next 10 days. If a probation date has already passed, no review is generated for it. Run the batch Click Run to execute the batch manually. Alternatively, schedule the batch to run nightly so no manual action is required on an ongoing basis. Confirm the outcome After the batch runs: The Review 1 Generated or Final Review Generated flag on the employee record is set to Yes. A probation review record is created and submitted to the workflow. The review appears in the manager's EmployeeXP queue under Team Probation Review Requests.

Human Resources (HR) can view all probation reviews — in progress or completed — from a central form in Dynamics 365 (D365), including workflow status, manager ratings, and employee feedback. Open the HR Probation Reviews form In D365, navigate to the Probation Reviews form within the Human Resources module. Find the review Use the filter options to locate reviews for a specific employee, or view all active reviews across the organisation. Review the record For each review, you can see: Employee name and review type (Stage 1 or Stage 2) Manager's competency ratings and comments Employee feedback comments Current workflow status: Processing, Assigned, or Completed For Stage 2 reviews: the Review Outcome (Meets Expectations/Performance Concerns) Stage 2 records show Stage 1 comments alongside Stage 2 comments for comparison. View workflow history Click View History to trace the full workflow routing — who took each action, which workflow conditions evaluated to true or false, and when each step completed. Confirm successful completion When a Stage 2 review is completed with "Meets Expectations", HR is notified. Update the employee's Probation Status to Confirmed on their employee record to finalise the process. Where the outcome is "Performance Concerns", the workflow routes directly to HR only — the employee is not notified of the outcome, and HR takes the appropriate next steps.

Probation fields are automatically populated in an employee's record when the employee is created in the system. Human Resources (HR) can view and update these fields at any point during the process. Open the employee record In Dynamics 365 (D365), navigate to the relevant employee record within the Human Resources module, Human resources ▸ Workers ▸ Employees. Locate the probation fields In the navigation bar below the Employee's name, select Work history. The following probation fields appear on the employee record: Field Description Probation Review Stage 1 Date Auto-calculated from start date and Stage 1 review days Probation Review Stage 2 Date Auto-calculated from start date and Stage 2 review days Probation End Date Defaulted from probation parameters Template The review template linked to this employee's staff level and category Review 1 Generated Set to Yes by the batch when the Stage 1 review is created Final Review Generated Set to Yes by the batch when the Stage 2 review is created Probation Status Updated manually to Confirmed by HR after successful completion Exclude from Probation Set to Yes to bypass the probation process for this individual Exclude an employee from probation If an employee should not go through the standard probation process, set Exclude from Probation to Yes. The batch process will skip this employee when generating reviews. Confirm successful completion After Stage 2 completes with a "Meets Expectations" outcome, HR receives a notification. Update Probation Status to Confirmed on the employee record to finalise the process.
documents.s: Probation fields on an employee record

documents.t: The offboarding exit survey is generated automatically via a batch job that detects employees assigned to an offboarding checklist. Run this batch to assign the exit questionnaire to departing employees. Navigate to the questionnaire schedule From Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Questionnaire ▸ Periodic Question ▸ Questionnaire Schedule for Offboarding Employee. Run the schedule Click OK to trigger the batch job. The job: Finds all employees who have been assigned an offboarding checklist. Generates a questionnaire for each employee based on the offset dates defined in the checklist. Assigns the questionnaire to each employee for completion in EmployeeXP. Note: This batch can be configured to run nightly as a recurring job — no manual intervention is required once scheduled. Run it manually only when you need to trigger it outside the normal cycle. Confirm generation After the batch runs, a questionnaire ID is generated for each affected employee. Employees will see the questionnaire appear in their EmployeeXP portal under the Questionnaires tab. To check the answers in D365, go to Questionnaire ▸ View and analyse results ▸ Answers by person. Filter the name required, then click Answers in the Action Pane. Use the questionnaire number as a reference.

Questionnaire schedules target a questionnaire to specific employees across one or more legal entities. Schedules are typically created in the GCO entity and can be released to individual schools or across all companies. Open the Questionnaire module From the Dynamics 365 (D365) navigation pane, go to Modules ▸ Questionnaire ▸ Distribute ▸ Questionnaire schedules. Create a new schedule Click Questionnaire schedules in the left menu, then click New. Select the questionnaire In the Questionnaire field, select the questionnaire to distribute. The questionnaire must already exist in the system before it can be scheduled. Set up the questionnaire details Click Setup details in the Action Pane. Select the person, teams or business segments to specify which school or group of schools the questionnaire is released to. Set the date range Enter a Start date and End date for the questionnaire window. Respondents will only see the questionnaire within this active period. Start the schedule Click Start to activate the schedule. The questionnaire will appear for targeted employees in the EmployeeXP portal under their Questionnaires tab.

As your retention conversation with an employee progresses, update their status in the Intentions Inquiry to keep the record up to date. Open the intentions inquiry Navigate to Human Resources ▸ Workers ▸ Inquiries and Reports ▸ Employee Intention Survey Result and locate the employee. Edit the record Click Edit to put the record into edit mode. Most fields are read-only. Only the Retention Status and Comments fields are editable. Update the retention status Select the appropriate status from the Retention Status dropdown: Status When to use HR Discussion A retention conversation has been initiated Retained successfully The employee has agreed to remain Exit confirmed The employee is confirmed as leaving — triggers the recruitment process Add a comment Enter any relevant notes in the Comments field to document the outcome of conversations or actions taken. Save Click Save to record the change.

The Employee Intention Survey Result form displays all employees who answered "Yes" to the intention-to-leave question in the Intention Questionnaire. Responses are captured live as employees submit the survey through EmployeeXP. Navigate to the intentions inquiry From the Dynamics 365 (D365) navigation pane, go to Human Resources ▸ Workers ▸ Inquiries and Reports ▸ Employee Intention Survey Result. Review the list The form displays all flagged employees. Columns include: name, search name, school, school code, business segment, position, job, email, intention to leave response, and retention status. The list is pre-loaded with historical data and receives new live submissions as employees complete the questionnaire. You can build filters to segment employees by retention status stage or school. Open a record Click on an employee's record to open the full detail view, including their questionnaire response and current Retention Status.

Request types define what employees can request through the EmployeeXP portal, which fields appear on the submission form, what is required before submitting, and which approval workflow the request follows. Open the Human Resources (HR) request types form In Dynamics 365 (D365), navigate to the HR request types form within the Human Resources module: Human resources ▸ Setup ▸ HR request types. Select a request type Choose the request type to configure — for example, Police Clearance Certificate, Early Exit, or Home Location Change. Configure the fields Click Header setup. For each field on the request type, set: Toggle What it does Visible Shows the field on the employee's EmployeeXP submission form Mandatory Requires the employee to complete this field before submitting The Attachment option is present on every request type by default — employees can always attach a file, so it does not appear in the field list. Assign a workflow Return to the main request page. Select the approval Workflow to apply to this request type from the dropdown. If multiple workflows exist, choose the appropriate one for this type (for example, routing to the WSO HRBP approval group). Control EmployeeXP visibility Toggle WebESS display to show or hide this request type in the employee portal. Request types that HR initiates internally should be set not to display in EmployeeXP. Set the display order Enter a value in the ESS display order field. Lower numbers appear first in the EmployeeXP request list (e.g., 1 = first). Assign a high number to push a request type to the bottom of the list. Save Click Save to apply the configuration.

When an employee submits a request through EmployeeXP, it is routed to the Human Resources (HR) team via the configured workflow. HR reviews the submission, provides feedback, and marks it complete. Open the HR Request form In Dynamics 365 (D365), navigate to the HR Request form within the Human Resources module. Click Refresh to load any new submissions. Each submitted request has a system-generated request number. Open the request Click on a request to open its detail view. You can see: The employee's submitted field values (e.g., destination, date, reason) Any file the employee attached, which you can open or download Review the submission Read through the employee's details and verify the request before taking action. Enter HR Feedback In the HR notes field, enter your response or notes. This text is visible to the employee when they view their completed request in EmployeeXP. Attach a document (optional) If you need to provide the employee with a document — such as an approval letter — click Attach to upload a file. The employee will be able to download it from their request in EmployeeXP. Approve and complete the request Click Approve to approve the request, then click Complete to mark it as done and close the workflow. Note: After completing a request there is typically a 3–5 minute delay before the updated status appears in EmployeeXP. The EmployeeXP cache refreshes on a 5-minute cycle — this is by design.

When an employee's recorded times are wrong—the biometric machine wasn't working, or they raised an Human Resources (HR) request for a late arrival or early exit—you correct the attendance log and re-run the summary. Use this route for a one-off correction; for bulk corrections, load them through the import instead. Open the attendance logs In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ Attendance log. Find the record Filter to the employee and the date you are correcting. Apply the filter before you edit so you don't accidentally change anyone else's record. Edit the times Click Edit and change the Clock in date time to the correct values. Make sure the Code remark in column matches the correct action. Save Click Save. Re-run the summary batch job Go to Time and attendance ▸ Periodic tasks ▸ Execute attendance summary and click OK. Wait for the message centre to confirm completion. This step is not optional. The attendance log is the raw record; this job calculates the work duration, regular minutes, and overtime everyone uses. Until it runs again, your correction exists only in the log. Check the corrected record in D365 Go back to Time and attendance ▸ Attendance details, or to Employees ▸ Work ▸ Attendance ▸ View attendance on the employee, and confirm the corrected times and the recalculated duration. Check it in EmployeeXP Open the employee's attendance in EmployeeXP and check the same date. EmployeeXP refreshes with a five-minute delay rather than instantly, so allow a moment before deciding the change hasn't taken effect. The interval is deliberate—the attendance feed arrives once a day, so refreshing the portal221 every minute would cost performance for no gain.

An employee's attendance and overtime are visible to, and approved by, whoever sits above them in the attendance and overtime hierarchies. You set that on the employee's position. Until you do, only the line manager sees them. Open the employee In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Human Resources ▸ Positions ▸ All positions and open the employee whose approver you are setting. Open their position Open the employee record and open the Reports to position tab. You will see the line manager already recorded. Add the attendance and overtime hierarchy Open the Relationships tab. Click + Add to assign the person or position that will approve the employee's attendance and overtime. This is often the same person as the attendance approver, but it doesn't have to be. Save Click Save. The employee now appears under that approver when they switch to the hierarchy view in the attendance details and overtime details forms in D365, and under Hierarchy on the team attendance screens in EmployeeXP. Where the line manager is also the attendance and overtime approver, you can leave these unset — the employee will appear under the line view instead. An employee who is in neither your line nor your hierarchy does not appear for you at all, by design.
documents.s: Assign attendance and overtime managers to a position

documents.t: Three people approve overtime in sequence: the manager first, then Human Resources (HR), then finance. Each stage sees only what the previous stage approved, so the list gets shorter as it moves along. Open the HR approval form In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to the HR approval form. Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ HR approval. Review what has reached you Only the records the manager has already approved appear here. If a manager approved three records, you'll see the same three— everything else they left is not on your list. The Last modified by and date and time columns show who approved the record before you and when. Approve as HR Select the records HR is approving and approve them. You do not have to approve everything that reaches you — approving two of three records sends only those two on. Save Click Save. Open the finance approval form Go to the Finance approval form. Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ Finance approval. Approve as finance The records HR approved are the ones listed here. Review the date, time, and punch location for each, then approve. Overtime that has cleared all three stages is what gets sent out for payroll processing. Check with your system administrator how it is handed to payroll.
documents.s: Complete the HR and finance overtime approvals

documents.t: Two parameter settings drive the whole time and attendance process: the hierarchies that decide who approves attendance and overtime, and the threshold below which overtime is not worth raising. Set both before you load any attendance data. Open the human resource parameters In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Human Resources ▸ Setup ▸ Human resources parameters and open the General tab. Set the attendance and overtime hierarchies In the hierarchy area, you will find two fields — one for Attendance and one for Overtime. Select the position hierarchy you want each to use. These exist because the person who approves attendance is not always the line manager. If a separate designated employee handles attendance or overtime, the hierarchy you select here routes it, and you assign individuals to that hierarchy based on their position. If the line manager approves attendance and overtime, you can point both fields to the line hierarchy—there is no problem with that. Save the parameters Click Save. Set the minimum overtime threshold Go to Human Resources ▸ Setup ▸ Human resources shared parameters and enter the minimum number of minutes to treat as overtime. Anything below the value you enter here will not show up as overtime. This keeps trivial daily overruns—five minutes past the end of a shift, for example—out of the overtime forms so approvers see only overtime that matters. Save the shared parameters Click Save. The threshold applies from the next run of the attendance summary batch job. Next, put people into those hierarchies — see Assign attendance and overtime managers to a position.

If you need attendance logs for employees with no punch data—because they aren't on the biometric system or a period needs backfilling—you can have Dynamics 365 (D365) generate them from a default start and end time and a working time calendar. It creates one punch in and one punch out for each applicable working day in the range. Open the attendance logs form In D365, go to Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ Attendance log. Open the generation form Click Generate attendance log in the Action Pane. Set the punch in details Enter the Start date time—the date the range begins and the time to use as the punch in (for example, 10 August at 07:00) —and set the Code remark in to Punch in. Set the punch out details Enter the End date time using the punch out time (for example, 17:00), and set its Code remark out to Punch out. The start and end date and time define the punch in and punch out times used on every generated record. Set the generate-to date Enter the Create till date — for example, 14 August. This is how far forward the records are generated. Select the working time calendar Choose the working time calendar to apply. It determines which days in the range count as working days, so non-working days produce no records. Select the workers Under the workers area, narrow to the employees you want. Available criteria include position, tier, department, staff category, and staff level, or you can select named employees from the list. Generate Click Generate attendance log. A notification confirms how many employees were processed. Check the generated records Refresh the attendance logs form and filter to the personnel numbers and the entry dates you generated. You should see a punch in and a punch out for each applicable working day in the range, with the code remarks you set. The process is safe to re-run over the same period. Re-running with the same parameters does not create duplicates — existing records are left unchanged, and only records that are missing, for example, a day someone has deleted, are generated again. Generated records feed the normal process from here. Run the attendance summary batch job over them as you would over imported punch data — see Run the attendance summary batch job.

Attendance data reaches Dynamics 365 (D365) as punch records — a clock-in and a clock-out per employee per day. An integration with the biometric system delivers these automatically, so you won't run this import daily or weekly. Use it when the integration isn't in place yet, or to correct or add records in bulk. The Excel or comma-separated values (CSV) import below is how the data gets in. Open a data import project In D365, go to System administration ▸ Workspaces ▸ Data management and click Import. Name the project Give the project a Group name. If you are duplicating an existing project, give it a different name so you don't overwrite the original. Select the entity and file type Set the file type to CSV and select the Time and attendance entity. Upload the file Click Upload and select your file, then apply it to the project. Map the remaining columns You may see a warning that the entity is not fully mapped. Map any outstanding fields — the code remark, the timestamp, the device ID and the device location — then apply the mapping. Run the import Click Import now. The file loads into the attendance log table. Check the loaded records Go to Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ Attendance log and review what came in. Each row holds the entry date, employee ID, clock-in date and time, code remark in, any remark passed through from the time and attendance clock, the clock-out date and time, and the location and device it was recorded on. Work duration is not calculated at this point. The attendance log is only the raw record of a punch-in and punch-out—durations, regular minutes, and overtime are calculated by the summary batch job. To run the summary, see Run the attendance summary batch job.

Overtime details is the manager's view of overtime in Dynamics 365 (D365), and the first of the three approval stages. It is the same approval the manager can do from EmployeeXP — whichever route is used, the record is the same. Open the overtime details form In D365, go to Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ OverTime detail. Understand what you are seeing Only employees with overtime records appear here. The form includes a filter option in the overtime minutes column to view employees with logged overtime, so it is a working list rather than a full roster. Overtime below the threshold set in the human resource shared parameters is excluded too — see Configure time and attendance parameters. Narrow to a date range Set a From date and To date and click Get data to see overtime between those dates. Switch between the line and hierarchy views As with attendance details, Line shows your direct reports and Hierarchy shows the people assigned to you through the overtime hierarchy in your position. Check who last changed the record The Modified by and Modified date and time columns show who last touched each overtime record, so you can see whether an entry has been amended and by whom before you approve it. Approve Click Edit, then select the records you want to approve. You can select one record, or several for the same employee, and approve them together. Click Approve. The Total approved minutes updates as you approve records. Approving here is the manager stage. The record then has to pass Human Resources (HR) and finance before it reaches payroll — see Complete the HR and finance overtime approvals. An overtime record approved by the manager in EmployeeXP appears here as soon as it is approved — the two screens show the same data, not a copy. See Approve your team's overtime in the EmployeeXP guide.

The attendance details form is the summarised view of who worked what, one record per employee per day. The summary batch job builds it from the attendance logs, so anything you see here reflects the last time the job ran. Open the attendance details form In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ Attendance detail. Read a record Each row shows the date, clock-in and clock-out times, work duration in minutes, regular minutes, overtime minutes, and the location, location ID, and device name the punch came from. Switch between the line and hierarchy views The form shows the employees who report to you, and you can view them in two ways. Line shows your direct reports. Hierarchy shows the people who report to you for attendance through the attendance hierarchy of their position. These are usually different sets of people, and that is the point of the two views — a designated attendance manager sees their attendance reports under Hierarchy even though those people report to somebody else on the Line. Search for a specific employee Filter on the Name column to find one person. If the employee doesn't appear, they aren't in your line or attendance hierarchy—that is a deliberate restriction, not a data problem. View one employee's own record To look at a single employee's attendance from their record instead, go to Human Resources ▸ Workers ▸ Employees, open the employee, and under the Work tab in the Action Pane, go to Attendance ▸ View attendance. This shows all their attendance and overtime information—work duration, regular minutes, and overtime minutes—in one place, and it's the view an employee sees for themselves.

An employee who punches in in the morning but never punches out in the evening leaves an incomplete day. The missing attendance form collects these so you can chase and correct them, rather than quietly producing an incorrect duration. Open the missing attendance form In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to the Missing attendance form under time and attendance. Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ Missing attendance. Read the exceptions Each row is a day when one half of the pair is missing: a punch in with no punch out, or a punch out with no punch in. Both cases are recorded as missing attendance. Switch between the line and hierarchy views As on the other attendance forms, Line shows your direct reports and Hierarchy shows the people assigned to you through the attendance hierarchy. Correct the record Once you have established what the missing time should have been — from the employee, their manager, or an Human Resources (HR) request for a late arrival or early exit — correct it in the attendance logs and re-run the summary batch job. See Adjust an attendance record.

Attendance logs contain only raw punch records. The Execute attendance summary job reads them and creates the summary record for each employee and day—their work duration, regular minutes, and overtime minutes—which every other attendance screen and the EmployeeXP portal read from. In normal operation, this runs as a recurring batch process right after the data feed, so nobody runs it by hand. Run it manually when you have just imported, generated or adjusted attendance logs and want the results now. Open the job In Dynamics 365 (D365), go to Time and attendance ▸ Periodic tasks ▸ Execute attendance summary. You can also search for Execute attendance summary in the search bar. Run it Click OK. Wait for the message centre to confirm The message centre tells you when the run is complete. Check the results Go to Time and attendance ▸ Inquiries and reports ▸ Attendance ▸ Attendance detail and find an employee in the batch. Each day's record shows the clock-in and clock-out times, work duration, regular minutes, and any overtime minutes. For example, an employee who clocked in at 08:00 and out at 17:05 shows a work duration of 545 minutes, 480 regular minutes, and 65 minutes of overtime. Their location, location ID and device name carry through from the imported log. Run this job again any time you change an attendance log. Editing the log on its own changes nothing downstream — see Adjust an attendance record.
documents.s: Run the attendance summary batch job

documents.t: Overtime eligibility is decided by staff level, not person by person. Flag the categories that can claim overtime once, and every hire into a position in one of those categories picks up the flag automatically as their worker action completes. Open the staff levels form In Dynamics 365 (D365), open the Staff levels form (Human resources ▸ Setup ▸ Staff levels) and find the staff position category and staff category you are setting — for example, transport support and support staff. Tick the overtime flag Set Overtime applicable against that category. Only staff in categories flagged here are treated as eligible for overtime. Unflagged categories produce no overtime records, no matter how many extra minutes their attendance logs show. Save Click Save. The setting takes effect for worker actions completed from now on — it does not retrospectively update people already hired. Complete the hire worker action as usual Hire the employee through the normal worker action process, with a position whose staff position category and staff level match the one you flagged. Submit the action to workflow and let it be approved. The worker action has to be completed, not just submitted. The flag is written to the employment record during action processing, so it isn't there while the workflow is still running. Check the flag on the employee Once the employee record has been created, open it and go to the Employment history area. Eligible for overtime is set to Yes. Amend the flag where it doesn't fit Click Edit and change the flag on the individual employee where the staff level rule isn't right for them, then Save. The staff level sets the default; the employee record records exceptions.
documents.s: Set overtime eligibility on staff levels

documents.t: Common problems in Dynamics 365 Human Resources (HR) and how to resolve them. Use the contents list on the right to jump to a section, or press Ctrl+F to search this page.

Cause — A personal or non-GEMS Microsoft account is being used, or the portal link is wrong. Fix — Sign in with your GEMS Microsoft 365 email address. The portal URL is provided by your system administrator. Where single sign-on is in use and you are already signed into Microsoft on the device, you are signed in automatically.
documents.s: I can't sign in to D365 HR

documents.t: Cause — Module visibility depends on the security roles attached to your account. Fix — Use the search bar at the top of the screen to search for the form by name. If it still doesn't appear, contact your system administrator to confirm your role.
documents.s: The Human Resources module isn't in the module list

documents.t: Cause — The pane has been collapsed. Fix — Click the hamburger menu (☰) at the top-left of the screen to expand it again. The Home icon in the pane returns you to your home page at any time.

Cause — The record is not in edit mode. Most Dynamics 365 (D365) forms open read-only. Fix — Click Edit in the Action Pane, make your changes, then click Save. The Back, Save/Edit, and New buttons stay anchored at the top of the record as you move between tabs.

Cause — A questionnaire must already exist in the system before it can be scheduled. Fix — Create the questionnaire first, then return to Questionnaire ▸ Distribute ▸ Questionnaire schedules and select it.
documents.s: The questionnaire I want isn't in the Questionnaire field

documents.t: Cause — The schedule hasn't been started, the current date sits outside the schedule window, or the recipients weren't set. Fix — Open the schedule and check three things: that Setup details names the right people, teams or business segments; that today's date falls between the Start date and End date; and that Start has been clicked to activate the schedule.
documents.s: Employees can't see the questionnaire in EmployeeXP

documents.t: Cause — Recipients are chosen in Setup details by person, team or business segment. Schedules are normally created in the GCO entity and can be released to one school or across all companies. Fix — Reopen Setup details on the schedule and correct the selected teams or business segments.
documents.s: The questionnaire went to the wrong schools

documents.t: Cause — The Employee Intention Survey Result form only lists employees who answered Yes to the intention-to-leave question. Fix — Check whether the employee has submitted the Intention Questionnaire at all. Responses appear live as employees submit through EmployeeXP.
documents.s: An employee isn't showing on the intentions inquiry

documents.t: Cause — Most fields on the Employee Intention Survey Result form are read-only by design. Fix — Click Edit in the Action Pane. Only Retention Status and Comments can be changed.
documents.s: I can't edit the fields on an intentions record

documents.t: Cause — The exit survey is generated by a batch job that only picks up employees who have been assigned an offboarding checklist. Fix — Confirm the employee has an active offboarding checklist, then run Questionnaire ▸ Periodic Question ▸ Questionnaire Schedule for Offboarding Employee. The batch can also be scheduled to run nightly.
documents.s: The offboarding exit survey hasn't been issued

documents.t: Cause — Answers are held separately from the schedule record. Fix — Go to Questionnaire ▸ View and analyse results ▸ Answers by person, filter to the employee, then click Answers in the Action Pane. Use the questionnaire number as your reference.
documents.s: I can't find an employee's questionnaire answers

documents.t: Cause — Either no default checklist is nominated in HR parameters, or the action type used for the hire doesn't have the checklist flag enabled. Fix — Check both: Human Resources parameters ▸ Recruitment must name an Onboarding checklist, and the relevant entry in Personal action types must have Apply onboarding checklist enabled.
documents.s: No onboarding checklist was applied when the hire completed

documents.t: Cause — Checklist tasks route to the group's primary member, not to everyone in the group. Fix — This is expected. To change who receives tasks, right-click the group, choose View Details, select the correct member, and click Make Primary.
documents.s: Only one member of the group received the task

documents.t: Cause — The primary group member has an active delegation configured. Fix — Delegated tasks route automatically to the delegate. Check the primary member's delegation settings if this wasn't intended.
documents.s: The task went to someone outside the group

documents.t: Cause — The task has a dependency on another task that hasn't been finished. Fix — The task detail view in EmployeeXP shows which tasks are blocking progress and who is responsible for them. The task unlocks once all dependencies are complete.
documents.s: An employee can't complete a task in EmployeeXP

documents.t: Cause — The task's Company field is either set to the wrong legal entity or left blank. Tasks with no company set apply to all schools. Fix — Open the task in the checklist and set Company to the specific legal entities the task should apply to.
documents.s: A task is appearing for the wrong school

documents.t: Cause — User groups are scoped by legal entity. Employees at other schools aren't visible in the current context. Fix — Switch legal entity context to the relevant school, or use the position, job title and name filters to narrow the visible list.
documents.s: I can't see the employees I want when building a user group

documents.t: Cause — Onboarding and pre-onboarding checklists calculate dates differently. Fix — Onboarding tasks use due date offset from start date — days after the employee starts. Pre-onboarding tasks use an offset date — days before the target date set when the checklist is applied. Check which type of checklist you're editing.
documents.s: The task due dates are wrong

documents.t: Cause — The Process type in the checklist assignment dialog is set to Pre-onboarding. Fix — This is expected — only checklists matching the selected process type are listed. The onboarding checklist is applied automatically once the worker action is fully approved and completed.
documents.s: Only pre-onboarding checklists are available on the worker action

documents.t: Cause — Dropdown values come from the Visa master setup tables, which were pre-loaded during migration. Fix — Add the missing value under Human Resources ▸ Setup ▸ Visa master — Visa Type, MOL Profession, MOE Profession, or Contract Type as appropriate — then click Save.
documents.s: A visa type or profession is missing from the dropdown

documents.t: Cause — Codes on their own are ambiguous. Fix — Descriptions are displayed alongside codes in every dropdown selection. If a description is missing, add it to the profession record in the Visa master setup.
documents.s: I can't tell the profession codes apart in a dropdown

documents.t: Cause — Alerts are driven by the saved expiry date and the threshold configured for that document type. Fix — Confirm the expiry date is recorded on the visa or identification record. Thresholds — how far ahead the alert triggers — are configured per document type in system setup, so a passport alert may start 50 days out while another type starts closer to expiry.
documents.s: No expiry alerts are appearing for an employee's documents

documents.t: Cause — No documents currently fall within the configured expiry threshold. Fix — No action needed. Open Human Resources ▸ Workspaces ▸ Personnel management to see the tiles for each document type.
documents.s: The Expiring Records tile is empty

documents.t: Cause — ABC Category is derived from the visa type. Fix — Change the Visa Type on the worker action and the ABC Category updates automatically.
documents.s: The ABC Category field won't let me change it

documents.t: Cause — Identification records carry over to the Pending Worker Visa Information form, but only publish to the employee record when the worker action is completed. Fix — Open Pending Worker Visa Information, find the worker, and click View Documents to confirm the records are present. Then complete the worker action through the standard workflow. Afterwards, verify in Employee Visa Information and in the employee's Person Identifications.
documents.s: The applicant's passport details didn't carry over to the new employee

documents.t: Cause — The form only holds pending worker actions that are not yet complete. Fix — If the worker action has already been completed, look at the employee record instead. If the hire hasn't been initiated, start the worker action first.
documents.s: A worker isn't listed on the Pending Worker Visa Information form

documents.t: Cause — The WebESS display toggle is switched off for that request type. Fix — Open the request type in Human resources ▸ Setup ▸ HR request types and switch WebESS display on. Request types that HR initiates internally are deliberately hidden from EmployeeXP.
documents.s: A request type isn't showing in EmployeeXP

documents.t: Cause — The list is ordered by the ESS display order value. Fix — Set a lower number to move a request type towards the top of the list, and a high number to push it to the bottom.
documents.s: Request types are in the wrong order in EmployeeXP

documents.t: Cause — The field is set to Visible but not Mandatory. Fix — Open Header setup on the request type and switch the Mandatory toggle on for that field. Employees then can't submit until it's completed.
documents.s: Employees are submitting requests without the information we need

documents.t: Cause — Attachments are available on every request type by default, so the option isn't listed as a configurable field. Fix — No action needed. Employees can always attach a file to any request.
documents.s: The Attachment option isn't in the field list

documents.t: Cause — No approval workflow has been assigned to the request type. Fix — Open the request type, select the appropriate Workflow from the dropdown, and save.
documents.s: A submitted request isn't going to anyone for approval

documents.t: Cause — The list holds its loaded state. Fix — Click Refresh on the HR Request form to pull in new submissions. Each has a system-generated request number.
documents.s: New submissions aren't appearing on the HR Request form

documents.t: Cause — The EmployeeXP cache refreshes on a five-minute cycle. Fix — Allow 3–5 minutes for the updated status to appear. This delay is by design.
documents.s: The status still shows as pending in EmployeeXP after I completed the request

documents.t: Cause — The response was recorded somewhere other than the field EmployeeXP surfaces. Fix — Enter your response in the HR notes field. That text is what the employee sees on their completed request. Any file you add with Attach is downloadable by the employee from the same place.
documents.s: The employee says they can't see our response

documents.t: Cause — One of several things stops the batch creating a review: the review date falls outside the horizon, the date has already passed, the employee is excluded, or the batch hasn't run. Fix — Check in order — that Exclude from Probation is set to No on the employee record; that the Stage 1 or Stage 2 date falls within the Probation Horizon Days value; and that Generate probation review has run under System Administration ▸ Periodic tasks ▸ Batch. Reviews are not generated retrospectively for dates that have already passed.
documents.s: No probation review was generated for an employee

documents.t: Cause — Probation parameters are set per combination of Staff Level and Default category, and the employee's combination may be configured differently — or may not match the one you expect. Fix — Check the employee's staff level and category, then review that row's Stage 1 and Stage 2 review days and template in the probation configuration form.
documents.s: The probation dates or template are wrong for an employee

documents.t: Cause — Reviews are routed into the manager's queue by the batch, not created directly on the employee record. Fix — The review appears in the manager's EmployeeXP queue under Team Probation Review Requests once the batch has run and the Review 1 Generated or Final Review Generated flag is set to Yes.
documents.s: The manager can't find the review

documents.t: Cause — Probation status is not updated automatically. Fix — After a Stage 2 review completes with a Meets Expectations outcome, HR is notified. Open the employee record, go to Work history, and set Probation Status to Confirmed.
documents.s: An employee has passed probation but their status still isn't Confirmed

documents.t: Cause — Where the outcome is Performance Concerns, the workflow routes to HR only. Fix — This is by design — the employee is not notified. HR takes the appropriate next steps directly.
documents.s: The employee wasn't told their Stage 2 outcome

documents.t: Cause — The review record shows the current status, not the full routing history. Fix — Open the review in HR Probation Reviews and click View History to trace each action, which workflow conditions evaluated true or false, and when each step completed.
documents.s: I need to see who actioned each step of a review

documents.t: Cause — An attachment is mandatory for that document type at that company, and no file has been uploaded. Fix — Upload the supporting file and the Submit button becomes available. To change the rule, update Attachment mandatory for company on the identification type.
documents.s: The Submit button is disabled in EmployeeXP when adding an identification document

documents.t: Cause — Mandatory fields are configured separately for each identification type. Fix — This is expected. A passport asks for issue date, end date and place of issue; Khamra asks for an agency rather than a country; medical insurance requires no issuing agency.
documents.s: Different document types are asking for different fields

documents.t: Cause — Rules are scoped by legal entity (company) and by Worker region. Fix — Open the identification type and check both scoping settings so the requirement only applies to the intended schools or locations.
documents.s: An identification rule is applying to the wrong staff

documents.t: Cause — Components with no Reward Type set are excluded from the statement. Fix — Open the component in Human Resources ▸ Setup ▸ Compensation ▸ Component master, click Edit, set a Reward Type, and save.
documents.s: A component isn't showing on the employee rewards statement

documents.t: Cause — The Reward Type value determines which category the component appears under. Fix — Change the Reward Type to the correct option — Fixed Allowance, Living, or Other — and save.
documents.s: A component is showing in the wrong category

documents.t: Cause — The component master lists every component regardless of configuration. Fix — Filter the Reward Type column to where the value is not empty. That shows everything currently included in the rewards statement; clear the filter to find components still to be configured.
documents.s: I can't tell which components have already been configured

documents.t: Cause — The checklist must exist and have a primary task owner before it can be assigned. Fix — Go to Human Resources ▸ Task Management ▸ Offboarding checklists, select or create the checklist, assign the monitoring group under Assigned to, select a user and click Make Primary, then save.
documents.s: I can't assign an offboarding checklist

documents.t: Cause — The Process type in the Apply checklist dialog is set to something other than Offboarding. Fix — In Actions ▸ Checklists ▸ Apply checklist, set Process type to Offboarding, choose the checklist, and click OK.
documents.s: The offboarding checklist isn't available on the employee's action

documents.t: Cause — Task dates are calculated from the target date set when the checklist is applied. Fix — Set the Target date to match the termination end date entered on the personnel action. Individual task dates are then derived from each task's offset.
documents.s: The offboarding task due dates look wrong

documents.t: Cause — Nothing has been received from GEMSU for that employee, or the message failed to import. Fix — Open the GEMSU integration log for the employee. If there is no entry, confirm with the GEMSU team that the course was assigned at source. If there is an entry in an error state, raise it with the GEMSU team — the message arrived but couldn't be written to the course tables.
documents.s: An employee's GEMSU courses aren't showing on their record

documents.t: Cause — The status update hasn't come through from GEMSU yet. Fix — Check the integration log for a more recent message against that employee. If the latest message imported successfully and still shows the old status, the source record in GEMSU hasn't been updated.
documents.s: The employee says the course is complete but D365 shows it in progress

documents.t: Cause — GEMSU course records are written by the integration and are not maintained by hand in D365. Fix — Correct the record in GEMSU and let it flow through, or load the correction through the GEMSU course data entity.
documents.s: I can't edit a course record on the employee's tracker

documents.t: Cause — The tracker on the employee record is scoped to that employee. Fix — Use the all-employee GEMSU course form and filter by course status or course type — for example, to list everyone with an outstanding mandatory course.
documents.s: I need to see course status across the workforce, not one employee at a time

documents.t: Cause — The most common reason is an employee ID in the file that doesn't match a personnel number in D365. Fix — Review the failed rows reported against the import project, correct the employee IDs and any field mapping, then re-run just the failures.
documents.s: My Excel import of course data failed

documents.t: Cause — The integration carries current course data; it does not backfill history. Fix — Load the historical records through the GEMSU course data entity. See Import GEMSU course data manually.
documents.s: Historical course data from before go-live is missing

documents.t: Cause — Either the plan is hidden at header level, the leave type is restricted, or the employee isn't enrolled. Fix — Check the EmployeeXP visibility flag on the leave plan header, then the restriction on the individual leave type — either one hides the type on its own. If both are set correctly, check the employee's enrolment under Leave and absence on their record.
documents.s: An employee can't see a leave plan in EmployeeXP

documents.t: Cause — The dropdown follows the sort order set on each leave type. Fix — Set the sort order on the leave types so the most commonly requested appear first.
documents.s: Leave types appear in the wrong order in EmployeeXP

documents.t: Cause — The hire action ran without the leave plan flag, or no plans are configured against their staff level. Fix — Check that the personnel action type has Update leave and absence plan set to Yes, and that the staff level for that position has leave plans assigned for the legal entity. Enabling the flag afterwards does not retrospectively enrol the employee — the enrolment has to be corrected separately.
documents.s: A new starter has no leave plans

documents.t: Cause — A promotion adds the new staff level's plans alongside the existing enrolment; the old ones go when the previous position is retired. Fix — Retire the previous position if that is your process. Retiring the position also retires the plans attached to it.
documents.s: A promoted employee kept their old leave plans

documents.t: Cause — The workflow has no condition on the system generated leave flag. Fix — Open the Leave and absence request workflow for that legal entity and add the condition that auto-approves requests where system generated leave is Yes.
documents.s: Calendar-change requests are sitting in review instead of auto-approving

documents.t: Cause — Balances recalculate when the system-generated request completes, not at the moment the holiday is moved. Fix — Wait for the adjustment requests to reach completed, then check the balance again as of a date after the change.
documents.s: I moved a holiday but the balance hasn't changed

documents.t: Cause — The filters were cleared or select all was used on an unfiltered list. Fix — The requests are created and approved immediately, so they have to be cancelled individually. Filter by position type, department or staff category and confirm the selection before clicking Assign leave.
documents.s: Bulk leave requests were created for the wrong staff

documents.t: Cause — They are still within probation, where a certificate is required from the first day. Fix — Check their probation status on their work history. The threshold on the leave type only applies once the employee is Confirmed.
documents.s: An employee is being asked for a medical certificate on a short absence

documents.t: Cause — The leave falls outside the cancellation window, which is measured from the leave start date. Fix — Cancel it in D365 on their behalf, or adjust the parameter if the window is consistently too short for your schools.
documents.s: An employee can't cancel leave they need reversed

documents.t: Cause — The most common reason is that no fare record matches the employee. The calculation needs a record in the airfare setup for their legal entity, their route, their ticket class and their ticket type, covering the dates the batch was run for. Fix — Check the air ticket location from and to fields on the employee's profile against the From city and To city on the fare records for their company. If those match, confirm the employee has a confirmed worker benefit enrolment — eligibility is derived from it, and employees without one are skipped.
documents.s: No airfare was calculated for an employee

documents.t: Cause — The active dependent flag is not set to Yes, the dependent has no valid from date, or the number of active dependents exceeds the entitlement on the benefit enrolment. Fix — Open Personal contacts on the employee record and check the active dependent flag first — dependents without it are skipped entirely. Then check the valid from and valid to dates, and the entitlement on the enrolment: self + 3 covers three dependents, and a fourth is not calculated.
documents.s: A dependent has no calculated line

documents.t: Cause — The entitlement doesn't cover the whole airfare period, so the fare has been reduced by days. Fix — This is expected. The calculation is the full fare divided by the days in the year and multiplied by the days covered — counted from the employee's employment start date, or from the dependent's valid from date. See Review calculated airfare.
documents.s: The amount is less than the full fare

documents.t: Cause — Their birth date means they crossed an age group boundary during the period. Fix — This is expected. The days before the birthday are paid at the lower fare and the days after at the next one, and the line carries the combined amount. Check the bands in Human Resources ▸ Setup ▸ Age group setup if the split doesn't look right.
documents.s: A dependent was paid at two different fares

documents.t: Cause — The calculation runs from the dependent's valid from date, which is the date the record became valid rather than the date of birth. Employees often add a dependent weeks after the birth, once the paperwork is through. Fix — Correct the valid from date on the personal contact, delete the employee's existing calculated lines, and run the batch again for that employee.

Cause — A duplicate check blocks a second record for the same legal entity, the same from and to city, and the same dates. Fix — Find the existing record for that combination and amend it, or delete it before creating the replacement. The same check applies to rows loaded through the data entity.
documents.s: I can't save a new fare record

documents.t: Cause — Records are being created by hand. Fix — Use the data entity instead. On the Airfare setup form, click Open in Microsoft Office in the Action Pane and select the airfare data entity. The year's rates can be loaded across every legal entity in a single upload. See Set up airfare rates.
documents.s: The whole year's fares need loading and there are too many to key in

documents.t: Cause — The batch writes new lines; it doesn't overwrite the existing ones. Fix — Delete the employee's existing lines on the calculated airfare form first, then run the batch again for that employee and the same period.
documents.s: I corrected the data but the amounts haven't changed

documents.t: Cause — The daily rate is the fare divided by 365 regardless of how long the period actually is. In a 366-day period the days covered are counted for real but still divided by 365, so the last day or two of cover makes no difference to the amount. Fix — This is how the calculation is specified. A full-period entitlement takes the full fare directly, so it is never overpaid; only part-period lines in a leap-year period round up like this.
documents.s: An employee covered for almost the whole of a leap year got the full fare

documents.t: Cause — The from date and to date used when running the batch don't match the period on the fare records. Fix — The pro-rata is measured against the dates entered on the batch, so a mismatch skews every line. Rerun with the dates set to the airfare period held in the airfare setup.
documents.s: The calculated amounts don't reconcile with the fare table

documents.t: Cause — The creation date falls outside the performance period selected. Fix — The creation date must sit inside the start and end dates of the period you are releasing. Check it against the period dates and run the job again. See Generate performance reviews.
documents.s: The performance review batch ran but no reviews were created
