documents.t: A sourcing project takes a purchase requisition raised in D365 Finance & Operations and runs it as an request for proposal (RFP) or request for quotation (RFQ). You build out the project with technical specifications, terms, a price sheet and vendor assessments, then publish to invite vendors to bid. Start a new project Open Projects and click Create new project. Enter a Project description, set the Price visibility option, then select the purchase requisition from the list — each requisition can hold multiple line items, which become the items vendors bid on. Click Save project. Build the project content Work through the content sections in order. In Technical, enter the introduction text — click Copy from library to reuse a saved version, or Generate with AI to draft one from a description. Add the Scope of work and any Additional requirements the same way. In Technical document, enter or upload the specifications vendors must meet. In Terms and conditions, click Import from Template to reuse an approved set or Add item to write new terms for this project. In Price Bid, select the Currency and enter the number of items the project covers. Set up the project Open Service providers and select the vendors to invite. Prospective vendors can be included — they receive the invitation email but must complete full onboarding before their bid can be accepted. Optionally, in Collaboration, add any users who will work on the project with you and set their access level. Also, optionally, in Assessments, select the Company type, then select the required assessments — the assessments that apply depend on the company type, so a service company may need only a few or none. Schedule, review, and publish the message Open Schedule and set the submission close date — the last day vendors can submit. Open Project Messages to review the invitation email to be sent to vendors and add any additional information as needed. Click Publish, then Confirm. Note: Publishing sends an invitation email to every selected vendor and prospective vendor. This cannot be undone.

This page is for vendors invited to participate in a sourcing project. Internal staff can use it to walk a vendor through the process when the vendor needs support. Note: Prospective vendors must complete the onboarding process before submitting a bid. See the Vendor Registration guide for further information on the process. When a sourcing project is published, invited vendors receive an email with a link to the vendor portal and a username and password. Everything a vendor needs to submit their bid is contained within that email — no prior access to the system is required. The bid has four parts to complete: technical, terms and conditions, assessments, and price bid. All must be filled in before the bid can be submitted. Log in and open the project Open the invitation email and log in to the vendor portal using the Username and Password provided in the email. Once logged in, click RFQ/Auction in the navigation — this is where all sourcing projects to which the vendor has been invited are listed. Select the project and click Participate to begin. Complete the bid The Overview page lists the documents the buyer has provided — review them and attach any requested supporting documents. Then work through each section: Technical — review the technical specifications the buyer has sent and attach the vendor's technical documents in response. Terms and conditions — read and accept the terms set by the buyer. Assessments — answer the questionnaires. The questions shown depend on the company type the buyer selected for the project, so they may vary between projects. Price — enter the Unit price for each item. Attach a supporting price document if one is required. Submit the bid Once all sections are complete, click Submit to submit the bid. Note: Once submitted, the bid is visible to the buyer immediately and cannot be recalled. Each invited vendor submits independently using their own credentials.

The Staff Experience Place, StaffXP is your day-to-day hub for school tasks — attendance, notices, wellbeing, activities, reporting, and more, all in one place. Find help by topic below, use the search bar up top, or ask Felix, the in-app assistant.

Navigating the platform — sign in, find your way around the nav bar, your MyDay home page, themes, and settings. Attendance — take the daily roll (on the page or through Felix), view analytics, run emergency rolls, and (for leaders) the whole-school view. Notices — read the noticeboard, follow the categories you care about, RSVP to events, and create and manage notices. Activities — plan excursions, camps, visits and trips, and book venues and resources against a shared calendar. Extra-curricular — browse, request, and run extra-curricular activities, tracked on a calendar. Wellbeing — create and track wellbeing notes, tasks and cases, with category trends. Notifications — your messages and alerts. Student & parent profiles — look up student and parent information. AI & Felix — what Felix can do for you, how to prompt it, and the rewards dashboard. Troubleshooting — common problems and how to resolve them. Glossary — the terms used across StaffXP.
Start with your MyDay home page — it pulls the day's essentials together. Then dip into each topic as you need it, or just ask Felix — see How Felix and the AI agents work.

Felix is the assistant in StaffXP's chat panel. Behind Felix sits a set of agents — each one handles a single job, such as writing a notice, drafting a class update, or logging a reward. You do not choose an agent; you describe what you want, and Felix hands the request to the right one. Open Felix and describe what you want Open the Felix panel and type what you are trying to do — for example create a notice, log a reward for Sophie, or what notices did I miss? You can also use voice input instead of typing, or select from pre-added prompts in the chat panel. The Felix panel is on the right of the screen, or you can click the icon at the bottom right to open the chat panel. Note: No agent has a navigation entry point. Menus, buttons and tiles will not take you to them — prompting Felix is the only route. Use the keyword that names what you want Felix matches your wording against what each agent does, so include the word that identifies the job. Dashboard on its own returns nothing, because it could mean almost anything; rewards dashboard or attendance risk dashboard works. You do not have to phrase it exactly as written in this guide — close and near matches are recognised. Give as much detail as you have The more your first prompt contains, the less Felix has to ask you. A short prompt such as create a notice is fine — Felix simply asks you the questions it needs, one step at a time. A fuller prompt such as create a cultural event notice for Years 5 and 10 on Thursday lets Felix fill in most of the form and go straight to a preview for you to check. Note: Whichever way you start, Felix circles back for anything required that is still missing before it will let you finish. Confirm the student when Felix asks When you name a student, Felix confirms who you mean before doing anything — it shows the full name and student ID. If several students match, they are all listed for you to pick from. Minor typos are usually resolved, but not always: a misspelling that is also a real word cannot be told apart from what you meant, so check the name Felix offers before you confirm. Check and edit before you commit Every agent shows you a preview before anything is created, sent or published. You can edit fields directly, prompt Felix to change something (add the location, add some next steps), or cancel. Nothing reaches a parent or student until you confirm. Know what Felix can see Felix works only within your access. A teacher sees the students in the classes they teach; a school leader sees their whole school. There is no cross-school view. Note: Some agents — such as the attendance compliance checker — do not run when you ask. They run on a schedule your school admin sets in Customer Engagement (CE), and show you the results of the last run. Look for the last updated and next update labels.
documents.s: How Felix and the AI agents work

documents.t: What you want to do Prompt something like Page See your rewards activity show me the rewards dashboard View the rewards dashboard

Felix is best when you don't know where to go. It scaffolds a process you have not done before and asks for what it needs, so a new starter can publish a notice without first learning where the form lives. If you already know the screen and use it every day, the form route is often the quicker one — the agent does not replace it. Felix also cannot see outside StaffXP and the school's own data. Its suggestions for values, categories and next steps come from what your school has configured and from the information in the prompt — not from a search of the internet.
documents.s: What Felix is good at, and what it is not

documents.t: The dashboard shows what you have logged this term and where the gaps are — which students you have recognised, which you have not, and how your rewards balance against your consequences. Ask for the dashboard Open Felix and prompt show me the rewards dashboard. Felix will send a link to open it. Note: Include the word rewards. Dashboard on its own returns nothing, because StaffXP has several. Read your term totals The dashboard covers: Rewards/Consequences logged — rewards and consequences, split out. Reward-to-consequence ratio — how positive your logging has been. Points issued. Students recognised — how many individuals, not how many logs. Milestones reached - if any students have reached milestones this week. Check the trends A weekly trend chart shows your logging over the term, and a breakdown shows rewards and consequences across your classes and by value. The picture becomes more useful the more regularly you log. Act on the insight The dashboard flags students not recognised for three or more weeks. You can ask Felix to suggest a reward for them. Log from the dashboard Buttons at the top of the dashboard start a reward, a consequence or a bulk entry without going back to the chat panel.

School leaders and admins get a wider version of the same dashboard, covering every class and teacher in their school rather than just their own logging. What a teacher sees is limited to their own classes.

The All venues list shows every venue the school can run activities at, both Approved and Declined. Any staff member with activity access can browse it — it's where you check whether the place you need is already approved before starting a request. Open the venues list On the Activities overview, open the All venues tab. Read the table Each row shows Venue name, Address, Learning area, Phone, and Status. The list opens filtered to Approved, so by default you see only venues you can use right away. Find a venue Search by name, and narrow the list with the Status filter (Approved / Declined) and the Learning area filter. Switch the status filter to Declined to see venue requests that were rejected. Open a venue or check declined notes Open any venue to view its full details read-only. For a Declined venue, use its row action to view the declined notes — the reason the request was turned down. If the venue you need isn't listed, click Request venue on the overview to submit it for approval first.

The Booking status tab on the Activities overview lists the equipment and resources booked against activities, so you can see what's reserved, who has it and when it's due back. Open Booking status On the Activities overview, open the Booking status tab. Any staff member with activity access can view it. Read the table Each row shows the booking's Event, the Resource booked, the Quantity, who it was Picked up by, its Return date and its Status. Find a booking Search by event name and filter by booking status to narrow the list down to the bookings you care about. This tab is read-only — it shows the state of each booking but doesn't let you change one. Resources are booked from within an activity request, on its Resource booking step.

If you run the same activity again — an annual excursion or a repeat camp — reuse a past one as the starting point instead of filling in the whole form from scratch. The new request opens already filled in from the original, so you only set the new dates and change whatever's different. Find the activity to reuse On the Activities overview, open the Your requests tab and find an Approved request, then use its row action Replicate. You can also start from a row in All activities using the Duplicate action. Open the pre-filled request The request form opens pre-filled from the activity you chose — the name, attendees, location, resource bookings and risk details all carry over. The dates and times are cleared, so you set fresh ones rather than copying the old schedule. Set the new dates and times Enter the new start and end dates (and the start/end or meeting and pick-up times the activity type needs). These are required, so Submit stays disabled until they're filled in. Adjust anything that's changed Work through the steps and update whatever's different this time — student groups, lead staff, venue, bookings or risks. Everything is editable; the copy is just a starting point. Submit as a new request On Review and submit, click Submit. This creates a brand-new request that goes to a coordinator as Pending — the original activity is untouched.

You can reopen a request to change it, and delete one you no longer need — provided it's still a draft. The row action you get depends on the request's status. Find the request On the Activities overview, open your request table — Your requests for general staff, or All requests for coordinators and leaders. Each row shows one action icon, set by the request's status. Edit a draft Click the Edit (pencil) action on a New / Draft request. The request reopens in the same guided form with your values filled in. Make your changes, then Submit to send it for approval, or Save and exit to leave it as a draft. Edit a request that needs more info If a coordinator has sent a request back as More info, click its name to reopen it. The request opens in the form ready to edit; make the changes the coordinator asked for and Submit to resubmit it. Delete a draft Click the Delete (bin) action on a New / Draft request, then confirm in the pop-up. A success message confirms the request was deleted and it leaves the list. Note: only New / Draft requests show Edit and Delete. Once a request is Pending, Approved or Rejected it can't be deleted here — a Rejected or More info request reopens (to read the review notes or edit) instead.

The request table on the Activities overview is where you find every activity you've requested and see where each one is up to. Open your requests On the Activities overview, open the Your requests tab. As an activity coordinator or school leader you instead see an All requests tab (everyone's requests) plus a My requests tab for just your own submissions. Read the table Each row shows the request's name under Requests, its Activity lead, its Type (Excursion, Visit, Camp or Overseas trip) and its Status. Narrow the list Search by request name, Filter by Status (Pending, Approved, Rejected or More info) and Type, and set how many rows show per page (10, 25, 50 or 100). Open a request Click a request's name to open it. Where it opens depends on its status — a draft reopens for editing, an approved request opens its activity details, and a Pending or Rejected request opens read-only. Use the row action to act on it Each row has a single action icon that matches its status: New / Draft rows offer Edit and Delete; Approved rows offer Replicate (start a new request from this one); More info and Rejected / Denied rows offer View review notes to read why. Coordinators get a Review action on Pending rows. Know what each status means The coloured Status tag tells you the stage: New / Draft (gray) is started but not yet submitted; Pending (amber) is submitted and awaiting a coordinator's decision; Approved (green) is signed off and confirmed; More info (blue) means a coordinator has asked you to update and resubmit; and Rejected / Denied (red) was declined — open View review notes to see what was said.

The Activities overview is the hub for out-of-class events — excursions, visits, camps and overseas trips — along with the venues and resources used for them. Three action cards sit across the top, and a set of tabs sits below. Open Activities Click Activities in the navigation bar. Anyone with activity access can open it. The page opens on the action cards and the tabs below. Use the action cards Three cards run across the top: Request venue — "Not listed in Approved Venues? Request a venue first." Opens the venue request. Calendar view — "Check your preferred date before submitting a request." Opens the read-only activities calendar so you can pick a free date. Request activity — "Plan a new activity with risk assessment." Opens the activity-type dropdown (excursion, visit, camp or overseas trip). Find the request queue The first tab is your request table. General staff see Your requests — only the requests you submitted. Activity coordinators and school leaders see All requests instead, plus a separate My requests tab for their own submissions. Browse the other tabs The remaining tabs are: Booking status — resource bookings tied to activities. All venues — approved and declined venues. All activities — every approved activity org-wide. This tab only shows for activity coordinators and super admins. Parent volunteers — parent helper sign-ups awaiting review. A notification can deep-link you straight to a specific tab — for example, open the overview with All venues already in focus.

A camp is one of the activity types you request from the Activities overview. It uses the same four-step guided form as an excursion — Activity details → Resource booking → Risk management → Review and submit — with a few camp-specific fields (a meeting and pick-up time, multiple off-site locations, and lead staff). Any staff member with activity access can submit a request; a coordinator then approves it. Start the request On the overview, click Request activity, choose Camp, and click Submit. (Click Calendar view first if you want to check your preferred dates are clear.) Fill in the activity details In Activity details, work through the four sections in the left rail. Under General information add the Activity name and set the meeting date & time and pick-up date & time (camps capture both, not a single start/end time). Under Attendees pick the Student groups by house, year group, class or roll group, then add the lead staff member and a second-in-charge (with their role), and set insurance if it applies. Add the location details In Location details, enter each off-site venue. A camp supports multiple locations, so add an entry per venue with its name, address, phone, email, website and contact. Choose from approved venues, or enter one manually — if a venue you need isn't approved yet, request it first. Set alignment and purpose In Alignment and purpose, describe the camp's purpose and curriculum alignment, and upload the schedule file and the packing-list file. Book resources (optional) In Resource booking, book anything the camp needs across Finance, Equipment, Transportation, and Technology — or skip the step. If you start a booking row you must finish it (pick a category and a resource); Next stays disabled until you do. Complete the risk management In Risk management, fill in each category: Student lists, Activity based, Transport, and Staff capacity (log each risk and its mitigation, or mark the category "no risk"). Under Key contacts add the lead teacher, principal, deputy principal, first-aid teacher and the local emergency number (required, and must be a valid phone number). Complete the External provider and Requester clarification sections too. Review and submit On Review and submit, check the summary and click Submit. Submit stays disabled until every required field across all steps is valid — if anything is missing, an error appears against each field so you know what to fix. A success message confirms the request, and you land back on the overview with the camp showing as Pending. To stop partway, click Save and exit (enabled once you've entered an activity name) to keep it as a Draft you can finish later.

When the venue you need isn't already an approved venue, you request it first. This is its own three-step flow, separate from the activity request, and any member of staff can start it. Open the venue request On the Activities overview, click the Request venue card ("Not listed in Approved Venues? Request a venue first."). You can also start it from inside an activity request when you are picking a venue. The form runs in three steps — Venue details, Risk management, Review and submit — shown in the left rail. Fill in the venue details In Basic information, give the Reason for request and the Venue name, Address, Telephone, and Email (all required); a Website is optional but must be a valid http:// or https:// address if you enter one. In Contacts, add the venue's key Contact name, Contact email, and Position. In Students, set the Relevant learning area, Year groups, and Cost to students with its Currency. Attach the required documents Still on Venue details, the Attach documents section needs both a Public-liability insurance file and an emergency plan file — both are required. You can add any number of additional documents, which are optional. Complete the risk management step On Risk management, work through the venue risk assessment for each category — Student list, Activity based, Transport, and Staff capacity — logging the risks and their mitigations, or marking a category as no risk. Then complete the Key contacts and External provider confirmations and the Medical support section (venue first-aid qualification, first-aid kit, and defibrillator). Review and submit On Review and submit, check the summary, which flags anything still missing. Submit stays disabled until the venue details, contacts, students, both required documents, every risk category, and the key-contact and external-provider confirmations are complete. Click Submit: a success message confirms the venue request was created and you return to the overview. At any point you can click Save and exit to keep a Draft (available once you have entered a venue name); if you try to leave with unsaved changes, the form prompts you first.

A visit is the shorter, simpler off-class activity type. The request is a four-step guided form — Activity details → Resource booking → Risk management → Review and submit — and any staff member with activity access can submit one. It then goes to an activity coordinator as a Pending request for sign-off. Start the request On the Activities overview, click Request activity, choose Visit, and click Submit. To check a date first, use the Calendar view card. Fill in the activity details On Activity details, complete the four sections shown in the left-hand list. In General information enter the Activity name, Start date / End date, and Start time / End time (all required); a Cover image is optional. In Attendees, pick a single group — one house, year group, class, or roll group — and choose Parent consent from its dropdown. In Venue details pick an approved venue or enter one manually. In Alignment and purpose record the purpose and curriculum alignment and upload a schedule file. Book resources (optional) On Resource booking, book anything the visit needs across Finance, Equipment, Transportation, and Technology. You can skip this step entirely, but once you start a booking row you must finish it — pick a resource category and a resource — or Next stays disabled. Complete the risk assessment On Risk management, work through each category in turn: Student lists, Activity based, Staff capacity, Key contacts, External provider, and Requester clarification. For a visit there is no Transport category, and the local emergency number under Key contacts is not required. Review and submit On Review and submit, check the read-only summary. Submit stays disabled until every required field across all steps is valid; if anything is missing, an error message points to each invalid field. Click Submit — a success message confirms it and you return to the overview with the request showing as Pending. To stop partway, click Save and exit (enabled once you have entered an activity name) to keep your progress as a Draft; leaving with unsaved changes prompts you first.

An excursion request is a four-step guided form that covers the activity, who's going, the venue, and a risk assessment, then goes to an activity coordinator for sign-off. Any staff member with activity access can create one. The step indicator runs across the top of the page header, so you can also click it to jump between steps. Start the request On the Activities overview, click Request activity, choose Excursion, and click Submit. To check a date is clear first, use the Calendar view card before you start. Fill in the activity details On Activity details, complete the four sections in the left-hand list. In General information, set the Activity name, Start date / End date, and Start time / End time (all required), and add an optional cover image. In Attendees, pick at least one Student group (by house, year group, class or roll group — required) and add any optional staffing, transport, cost or parent-volunteer details; parent consent is set to Yes automatically for excursions. In Venue details, choose an approved venue or enter one manually — manual phone, email and website entries must be valid. In Alignment and purpose, add the purpose, curriculum alignment and an optional schedule file. Click Next. Book resources (optional) On Resource booking, optionally book what the activity needs from Finance, Equipment, Transportation and Technology. You can skip the step entirely, but once you start a booking row you must finish it — pick a resource category and a resource — or Next stays disabled. Complete the risk management On Risk management, work through each category in turn — Student lists, Activity based, Transport and Staff capacity (log each risk and its mitigation, or mark the category "no risk"). In Key contacts add the lead teacher, principal, deputy, first-aid teacher and the local emergency number (required, and must be a valid phone number), plus the optional nearest hospital. Complete the External provider and Requester clarification confirmations, then click Next. Review and submit On Review and submit, check the read-only summary. Submit stays disabled until every required field across all steps is valid; if anything is missing, an error message appears for each invalid field so you know exactly what to fix. Click Submit — a success message confirms it and you land back on the overview with the request showing as Pending. To stop partway, click Save and exit (enabled once you've entered an activity name) to keep your progress as a Draft. Leaving with unsaved changes prompts you first.

An overseas trip is a four-step request — Activity details → Resource booking → Risk management → Review and submit — and it carries the most controls of any activity type. Any staff member with activity access can submit one; an activity coordinator approves it afterwards. Start the request On the Activities overview, click Request activity, choose Overseas trip, and click Submit. The four steps run across the top of the page header; use Next / Back to move, or the step indicator to jump. Fill in the activity details Enter the Activity name, the Start date / End date and Start time / End time, and optionally a cover image. Under Attendees, pick your Student groups (by house, year group, class or roll group) and name the lead staff member and a second-in-charge. Set the insurance option, and set the Max no. of students cap and Enable waitlist — overseas trips are the only activity type with these. Overseas trips support multiple off-site venue entries, so add each venue (name, address, phone, email, website and contact). Finish the step with the activity's purpose and curriculum alignment, plus a schedule file and a packing-list file. Book resources (optional) Book anything the trip needs under Finance, Equipment, Transportation and Technology. You can skip this step entirely — but once you start a booking row you must finish it (pick a resource category and a resource), or Next stays disabled. Complete the risk assessment Work through each category — Student lists, Activity based, Transport and Staff capacity — logging risks and their mitigations, or marking a category "no risk". Under Key contacts, the local emergency number is required for an overseas trip. Then confirm the External provider checks and the Requester clarification items. Review and submit Step four is a read-only summary of everything you entered. Click Submit. A success message confirms it and you land back on the overview with the request showing as Pending. Submit stays disabled until every required field across all steps is valid. If anything is missing, an error appears for each invalid field so you know exactly what to fix. Note: To leave before submitting, click Save and exit — it saves your progress as a Draft and is enabled as soon as you've entered an activity name. If you try to leave with unsaved changes, an unsaved-changes prompt appears first.

As an activity coordinator you act on the requests staff submit — approving them, declining them, or sending them back for more information. The request opens in the same layout it was submitted in, with the decision controls in the header. Open a Pending request On the Activities overview, open the All requests tab, find a Pending request and click Review (the row action). The Review action only appears on Pending requests and only for coordinators. Read the submitted details The request opens read-only, showing everything the requester entered — the activity, participants, venue and risk assessment. Scroll through to check it before you decide. Choose a decision The decision controls sit in the header: Approve — signs the request off. A success message confirms it, the request becomes Approved, and you return to the queue. Decline — opens a notes box. Enter why and confirm; the request becomes Rejected and the requester is notified. Request more info — opens a notes box. Enter what's needed and confirm; the request moves to More info for the requester to update and resubmit. Decline and Request more info both require notes — the requester reads them back via View review notes on the request row. Edit on behalf if needed To fix something yourself rather than send it back, use Edit on behalf. This opens the request in its editable form; Back to approval returns you to the decision step without saving. Review a venue request the same way A venue request uses the same Approve / Decline / Request more info controls in its own review. Note: if the requested venue clashes with another approved event, Approve is disabled and a Venue conflict detected pop-up names the conflicting event. You can't approve until the clash is resolved.

Parents can sign up to help on an activity, and their sign-ups land here for an approver to action. Reviewing and approving parent volunteers is approver-only (activity coordinator, school leader, or super admin); general staff can see the list but not the approve or decline controls. Open the parent volunteers list On the Activities overview, open Parent volunteers. The tab opens filtered to Pending / More info, so the sign-ups waiting on you appear first. Read the table Each row shows the volunteer's parent name, the event, the child, their contact details, the role they offered, and a Status tag. Review a volunteer Click Review on a row to open the detail modal, where you can read the volunteer's submitted documents before you decide. Approve or decline In the modal, click Approve or Decline. To action several at once, select their rows and use the batch Approve / Decline actions. Remove an approved volunteer To withdraw someone you have already signed off, click Remove on their row.

The activities calendar is a month, week or day view of scheduled activities — handy for checking whether a date is free before you submit a request. Open the calendar On the Activities overview, click the Calendar view card ("Check your preferred date before submitting request"), or open Calendar view from the navigation. Choose how to view dates Switch between Month, Week and Day, and page forward or back through dates to find the period you need. Read an activity Activities are shown as coloured blocks, with the colour set by activity type. Click an event to open a pop-up with its name, type, dates, and the year group, house or class it's for. Note: The calendar is read-only — you can't create or edit an activity from it; it's only there to help you pick an available date.

When an emergency is declared, you take a stripped-down Emergency roll for your class. If a student who belongs to another class is physically with you, add them so they're accounted for in the headcount. Open the off-roll list On the Emergency roll, click Students not on roll. The button shows a live count once you've added anyone. Add the student In the modal, click Add, then search and pick the student. You can add an optional reason of up to 100 characters. The same student can't be added twice — try it and you'll get an Already added warning. Check the off-roll group Added students appear in a Not on roll group below your roll, each marked Present and counting toward your Present total. Every row has a Remove action and an Edit/add note action. Remove one if needed Click Remove on a row to take a student back off the list. A brief Undo appears if you remove someone by mistake. Submit the roll When everyone with you is accounted for, click Submit to send your class's emergency status, including the off-roll students.
documents.s: Add a student who isn't on your roll

documents.t: The roll opens on today by default. Use the date picker to look back at an earlier session for the same class. Open the date picker On the roll toolbar, click the calendar icon (Change attendance date). Pick a date Choose a day in the popover. The roll reloads on that date, showing how the class was marked. The date travels in the page address, so a link to a specific day's roll is shareable. For a teacher, a past session opens read-only — you can review the marks but the cells are locked, and you mark only today's column. An attendance officer can still edit a past-dated roll.

When a leader declares an emergency, coordinators get live screens to watch the whole evacuation and confirm every class is accounted for. The page you see depends on your role, and both pages exist only while an emergency is active. Open your coordinator page These screens appear automatically once an emergency is declared. As an emergency coordinator or school leader you get the Emergency coordinator page; as a muster-point coordinator you get the Muster coordinator page for your own point. If you don't hold one of these roles, the pages don't appear — you take the emergency roll like everyone else. Watch the whole school (Emergency coordinator) The Emergency coordinator page shows a live muster table of all classes and muster points so you can see at a glance which classes have submitted and where students still need accounting for. The figures update as teachers submit their emergency rolls. Confirm cleared classes A Cleared classes table lists the classes that are fully accounted for, so you can focus on the ones still outstanding. Watch your own muster point (Muster coordinator) The Muster coordinator page shows just your muster point's headcount and the cleared classes for that point — your slice of the evacuation rather than the whole school. End the emergency (leaders only) Only a school leader can end an incident: on the Emergency coordinator page they click Turn off emergency protocol and confirm. Coordinators see all the live data but can't end the emergency themselves.

Declaring an emergency flips the whole school into evacuation/lockdown attendance: every teacher's roll switches to a fast headcount. Only a school leader can do this — other roles never see the Emergency button. Click the red Emergency button In the top app toolbar, click the red Emergency button. This control only appears for school leaders, so if you can't see it you don't have permission to declare an emergency. Choose the incident type and message In the Initiate emergency protocol dialog, choose an Incident type (required) and, if you want, type a Message to staff (up to 100 characters). Confirm to start the emergency Click Confirm. This immediately notifies all staff and turns every teacher's roll into a stripped-down Emergency roll, and the emergency-coordinator and muster-coordinator screens become available. The action is logged with your name and a timestamp. Note: Confirming alerts everyone in the school at once and forces all staff into emergency attendance. Only declare a real emergency or a planned drill.

When the evacuation or drill is over, a leader ends the emergency to take every class out of emergency mode and return the school to normal attendance. Note: Ending an emergency is leader-only — it needs the emergency deactivate permission. Coordinators can see the live muster data but can't stand the incident down, so if the button isn't available to you, ask a leader to end it. Click Turn off emergency protocol With an emergency active, the Turn off emergency protocol button sits in the top app toolbar and on the Emergency coordinator page. Click it from either place. Confirm in the dialog The Turn off emergency protocol dialog opens. Confirm to end the emergency for the whole school. Check the confirmation A confirmation toast with a timestamp tells you the emergency has ended. Every class returns to its normal roll, and the emergency-coordinator and muster-coordinator pages close.

Each row on the roll opens a quick-glance card that shows the student's whole day across every class — not just your lesson. Open the row On the roll, click the expand chevron at the start of a student's row. The card loads its detail the moment you open it, so it may take a beat to appear. Check any alerts At the top of the card, alert icons flag safeguarding, medical, learning or custody concerns. Click an icon to read its detail. Read the student context The card shows the student's preferred name, house, first language and age where the school holds them. See their whole day Today · all classes is a timeline of every lesson the student has today, with your period ringed and a one-line summary such as "2 present · 1 late today". Because it's cross-class, it shows lessons you don't teach — so you can spot a student who's present in your class but absent later in the day. Glance at their rate An Attendance rate big number sits on the right of the card.
documents.s: See a student's day at a glance

documents.t: From the Attendance overview dashboard you can drill into any class's roll across the whole school — not just your own. This needs School leader or attendance officer / admin access; a regular teacher reaches rolls from their own calendar instead. Find the Class rolls table On the dashboard, scroll to the Class rolls table below the chart row. It lists every class's roll. Search and filter Use the Search box to find a class or teacher by name, and the filter to narrow to a single year group. Set a date range Click the calendar trigger to set a date range, so you can find a past session rather than today's. Open the roll Click a class name to open that roll. It opens with your extra editing powers where they apply, and inherits the class's year-group attendance setting — either AM/PM or Period, never both.
documents.s: Find and open any class roll

documents.t: When a roll is open, the toolbar lets you jump to one student or narrow the roll down to just the students carrying an alert. Search by name Type into Search students… in the roll toolbar. The roll filters to matching names as you type. Show only flagged students Use the filter control to show only students carrying an alert — Physical / wellbeing, Medical, Custody, or Learning. Combine and reset The alert filters combine with whatever is in Search students…, so you can search a name and an alert at once. Reset clears the alert filters and shows the full roll again.

When most of a class is present, you can set today's whole column in one go instead of marking each student. This needs Attendance write access (the same access used to take a roll); for read-only staff the column control is hidden. Open the column menu On the roll, click the action control on today's column header. The menu reflects the column's current state. Mark everyone at once Choose All present or All absent. Every student in today's column is set to that status, except any student who already holds an approved absence — bulk marking skips those, so it never overwrites a resolved absence. Clear the column if needed To start over, open the menu again and choose Reset, which clears your pending marks for today's column. Submit the roll Bulk marking doesn't save on its own. After the column is set, adjust any individual students as needed, then click Submit to send the roll.
documents.s: Mark a whole column at once

documents.t: When you need a paper copy of a class roll — for a substitute, an excursion, or a fire-drill backup — you can print it straight from the roll. Open the roll you want to print Open the class roll from your calendar, a roll reminder, or Felix. Print it On the roll toolbar, click the print icon. The attendance document is fetched and sent to your printer. Printing needs a live connection — if you're offline it fails with a message, so reconnect and try again.

Once you submit a roll it's locked, so you can't change a mark directly on it. To fix a mistake, you log a correction request through Felix, which an attendance officer then reviews and resolves. Ask Felix to correct the mark Open Felix and ask for the correction, for example "I need to correct an attendance mark" or "fix the roll". Felix confirms that submitted rolls are read-only and opens a correction form pre-filled for a recent session. Set the corrected mark and reason In the form, choose the corrected mark for the student and add a reason explaining the change, then submit. Wait for an officer to resolve it Your request goes to an attendance officer's Correction request tab, where they approve and apply the change. The correction request is the only way to change a submitted mark — you can't edit the locked roll yourself.

Attendance officers clear requests and unresolved marks from tabs on the dashboard. These tabs and the powers below are officer-only; teachers don't see them. Open the officer tab bar On the Attendance overview, the officer tab bar lists the work waiting for you: Leave requests (approve or decline parent-submitted leave), Class rolls (open any roll to edit), Unresolved attendance (marks that still need a resolution category), Correction request (teacher correction requests to action), and Resolved requests (the history of what you've already cleared). Pick a tab and work the list Open the relevant tab and action each item in turn. For Leave requests, approve or decline. For Unresolved attendance or Correction request, open the roll to make the change. Change a cell and choose a reason When you change a cell on a roll, a category picker opens so you set the specific reason rather than just Present, Absent, or Late — for example Absent then Excused: Sick or Holiday. Cells you've changed show a hover tooltip with the correction history. Use your officer powers You can edit past-dated rolls and change approved absences — the date lock and resolved-absence lock that apply to teachers don't apply to you. Submit the corrections Click Submit to save. Your submit sends partial corrections, so you don't need every student marked — the all-marked gate is teacher-only. Resolved items move to the Resolved requests tab.

After a drill or real incident ends, you can review what happened and how long each part of the muster took. This is leader-only: the Emergency history is reachable by school leaders, not teachers or attendance officers. Open Emergency analytics On the Attendance page, open Emergency. This shows a history table of past incidents — both drills and real emergencies. Read the history table Each row is one past incident, with timing stats such as average clear time. Use the filters to narrow the list by type, by term, and by year. Open one incident's full report Click an incident row to open Emergency details for that incident. It breaks down time taken per class and per muster point, and compares present against absent numbers. Print the report The details page is printable, so you can keep a record of the incident or share it for a debrief.

Taking the roll is the core teacher task: open your class, mark every student, and submit. Open the class roll From the Attendance page, click your class on the calendar, follow a roll reminder, or ask Felix ("take the roll"). The page header shows the class name, the period and student count (for example "Period 2 · 24 students"), and the date. Read the roll table The Attendance roll table lists every student on one page — there's deliberately no pagination, so nobody gets missed. Each row shows an avatar, the student's name (first name bold), and their Attendance %. On the left, you can see up to 4 prior sessions as read-only history, and on the right, today's editable column. You can only mark today's column; the prior sessions and approved absences cannot be changed. Mark each student Click the status icon in today's column to open the menu, then pick Present, Absent, or Late. The menu only shows options different to the current status. To mark all students at once, use the action control on today's column header (All present / All absent), then adjust individuals if needed. Bulk marking skips students who already hold an approved absence. Submit the roll When all the students have a valid status, the Submit button enables — click it. Submit stays disabled until no student is left on Not yet marked (the ··· default), so you can't submit a partial roll. It's also disabled while you're offline. A success toast confirms with "Attendance submitted"; if you came from a roll reminder and have more classes to complete, the toast offers a "Take roll for [next class]" shortcut. Note: Once submitted, a roll is locked — there's no direct edit. To fix a mistake, ask Felix to log a correction request, which an attendance officer resolves. Check what the icons mean The roll uses icons, not words. Click the information (ⓘ) icon next to the Attendance roll title to open the key. There are two status groups, statuses you set — Present, Absent, Unresolved late — and system statuses: Approved absence (resolved by an officer elsewhere, so not editable by you; clicking it opens the absence's details) and Not yet marked (the default before you mark, which still blocks Submit).

Once a school leader declares an emergency, every teacher's open roll switches into a stripped-down headcount. Every teacher does this — the Emergency button that starts and ends an emergency is leader-only, but taking the emergency roll is for everyone. Your roll becomes the Emergency roll When an emergency is declared, your open roll flips automatically — a red Emergency roll tag appears in the header, and all staff are notified. The table strips back to two columns, Student name and Emergency roll, so per-period history and Attendance % are hidden and nothing competes with marking. Mark each student Present or Missing Tap each student Present or Missing. To set everyone at once, use the mark all action in the column header, then adjust individuals. A live counter strip in the card header shows running Unmarked, Missing, and Present totals. Add a note where needed Add a note to any student to pass on detail — for example where a missing student was last seen. Submit your class's status Click Submit to send your class's emergency status. Unlike a normal roll, there's no all-marked gate here — you submit what you have, fast, and coordinators chase the rest. Emergency mode is deliberately minimal: no date picker, no print, no birthday cue. A confirmation tells you the roll has been submitted.

Attendance overview is the whole-school dashboard. School leaders and attendance officers see it automatically when they open Attendance — the same nav item that opens the teacher calendar for everyone else. Officers see the same dashboard as leaders, plus an extra set of officer tabs. Open Attendance overview Click Attendance in the main navigation. As a leader or officer you land on Attendance overview instead of the teacher page. Read the top tiles The top row tracks the things needing attention today: Roll reminders — the tile label shows a live count of classes that haven't submitted yet. Click View all to list them by teacher, class, period, and outstanding count. Students at risk — a live count of students below the attendance threshold. Click View all to open the at-risk list. View trends — jumps to Attendance trends. Read the chart row Three charts summarise the day, each with a short summary line: Today's attendance (a gauge you can filter by Present, Absent, or Late), Attendance errors (where corrections are coming from), and Attendance category (the Present / Late / Absent split). Open any class roll Below the charts, the Class rolls list shows the school's rolls. Search by class or teacher, filter by year group, and click a class name to open its roll. Work the officer tabs If you're an attendance officer, a tab bar sits on the dashboard with Leave requests, Class rolls, Unresolved attendance, Correction request, and Resolved requests. Open a tab to work through that queue. Leaders see the dashboard without these tabs.

The Attendance page is your teacher landing screen: three stat cards on the left and a calendar of your day's classes below. The same Attendance nav item opens a whole-school dashboard instead if you're a school leader or attendance officer. Open Attendance Click Attendance in the main navigation. As a regular teacher you land on the stat cards and your day's calendar. Read the three stat cards The cards summarise today across all your classes: Late students and Unexcused absences (both for today), and Absent students (this month, on assessment days). Each card shows a count with a "from yesterday" or "from previous month" change. See who's in a card Click a card's Show top 10 to open a list of those students. Open a class roll The calendar shows your classes for the day. Click a class to open its roll and start marking students. View analytics Click View analytics (top right) to open Attendance analytics. The link is only enabled if you have attendance-analytics access.

The analytics screen shows attendance patterns, a risk banner, and the at-risk student list. You need Attendance-analytics read access; without it the View analytics button stays disabled. Open the analytics screen On the teacher Attendance page, click View analytics (top right). You can also reach it from a View trends tile on a leader or officer dashboard. Check the at-risk banner An at-risk banner sits at the top. Its flagged-students action opens the at-risk modal listing the students currently below the attendance threshold. Read the stat cards Four cards summarise the picture: Attendance rate (which shows a "below threshold" warning when it drops low), Late students, Unexcused absences, and Absent students. Explore the trends charts The Trends section holds an attendance trend line, an absence-timing chart, and an absence-by-day chart. Use the by class filter to focus the charts on a single class. Work the at-risk table The at-risk table lists flagged students. Filter it by year group and by risk level to narrow to the students you want to follow up.

Attendance trends is a leader and officer view that shows when absence and lateness tend to happen, as pattern bar charts. You need school leader or attendance officer access to reach it — the View trends tiles only appear on the leader / officer dashboard. Open Attendance trends On the Attendance overview, click a View trends tile. It opens the Attendance trends page. Set the filters Use the period, class, and year filters at the top of the page to frame what you're looking at. Read the three trend lists Three bar lists sit down the page: Absence timing trends (when absences cluster), Tardiness timing trends (when lateness clusters), and Learning-area attendance trends (attendance by subject area). Each list plots its pattern as horizontal bars with a one-line summary above it.

The Extra curricular hub is where you find the school's clubs and teams — their requests, bookings, approved activities and assigned staff. Open the hub Click Extra curricular in the navigation. Two action cards sit at the top — Create extra-curricular activity and View calendar — above a set of tabs. Anyone with extra-curricular access can open the hub, but what each tab shows depends on your role. Choose a tab The first tab is the request queue: regular staff see Your requests (your own submissions); activity coordinators and school leaders see All requests (everyone's queue) plus a My requests tab that filters the same queue to activities you lead. The other tabs are Booking status, Supervising activities, and Staffing. Read the request queue The request tabs list each request under Requests (the name, a link), with its Submitted date, Type and Status. Search by request name and Filter by Status and Type together. Note: For approvers, All requests opens pre-filtered to Pending — it's the triage queue. Clear the Pending chip to see every status. Your own Your requests / My requests always show all statuses. Use the row action that matches the status Each request row carries one status-aware action. A New / Draft request shows Edit (pencil) and Delete (bin) to its author, and its name reopens the editable form. A Pending request shows Review (only if you can approve) and opens the Review request screen. An Approved request shows Replicate and its name opens the Activity details page. A Declined / Rejected or More info request offers View review notes. Check resource bookings The Booking status tab lists bookings tied to activities, with columns Event, Resource, Quantity, Picked up by, Return date and Status. Search by event name and filter by booking status. Browse live activities The Supervising activities tab ("All ECAs") lists only Approved and Rejected activities, with Name (a link to its details), Event type, Event start, Event end, Activity lead and Status. Search across name, type or lead and filter by Approved or Rejected. Approved rows offer Replicate; Rejected rows offer View review notes. Look up assigned staff The Staffing tab lists staff assigned to activities, with Name, Role, Phone, Email and Consent. Search by name and filter by role. Consent shows View to open an external member's clearance document, Internal for internal staff, or a dash when there's nothing to show. Know what each status means The coloured Status tag tells you the stage: New / Draft is saved but not yet submitted; Pending is submitted and awaiting a decision; More info means an approver has sent it back with notes for you to update and resubmit; Approved means it's live and open for enrolment; and Declined / Rejected was turned down — open View review notes to read why. Every table sets how many rows show per page (10, 25, 50 or 100).

Replicate reuses an approved activity as the starting point for a new request — handy for re-running a club or team each term without rebuilding the whole plan. Any staff member can do this from their own requests. Find an approved activity On the Extra curricular hub, open the All requests tab (or Your requests) and find an Approved row, or use the Supervising activities tab, which lists approved activities. The Replicate (duplicate) icon is the row action on Approved rows. Open the copy Click the Replicate icon. The four-step create flow opens pre-filled from that activity — venue, attendees, costs, resources, and risk content are all carried over. Note: Replicate creates a new request and never edits the original. The dates and the whole registration window are cleared, so you must enter current ones before you can submit. Adjust and submit Re-enter the Event start/end dates and times and the Registration start/end window, change anything else the new run needs, then work to Step 4 — Review and submit and click Submit. It goes in as a brand-new request for approval.

Edit and Delete are only available while a request is still New or Draft — before it's submitted. Once a request is Pending, Approved, or Declined, you act on it through Review, View notes, or Duplicate instead. Find your draft On the Extra curricular hub, open the All requests tab (coordinators and leaders) or Your requests tab (other staff). The Status column shows a coloured tag — look for a New or Draft request. Use the search box or the Status filter to narrow the list. Edit it Click the Edit (pencil) action on the row. The request reopens in the four-step create flow (Activity details → Resource booking → Risk management → Review and submit), pre-filled with everything you'd entered. Make your changes, then Submit on the final step (or Save and exit to keep it as a draft for later). Delete it Click the Delete (bin) action on the row, then confirm on the prompt. A success message appears and the request leaves the list. Note: Deleting a request is permanent — there's no undo, and a deleted draft can't be recovered.

Once an activity is approved, you manage everyone enrolled in it on the activity's own details page. Open the participants table Open the approved activity's details page and find the Registered participants table. The heading shows the place limit as Maximum (for example, Maximum: 20), and each row lists the student's Name, Year group/s, and Gender. Find a participant Use Search to filter the table by name, year group, or gender. Remove a participant Click the bin icon on the student's row, then confirm in the Remove participant dialog. A success message confirms the student has been removed. Note: Removing a participant takes them off the activity straight away. To re-enrol them, they have to register again (or be approved from the waitlist).

When an activity has a waitlist turned on, students beyond the maximum join it instead of being turned away. From the activity's details page you bring those students into the activity or take them off the list. Open the Waitlist table On the approved activity's details page, find the Waitlist table. It only appears when the activity has a waitlist. The heading shows the Maximum number of students, and the columns are Name, Year group/s, and Gender. Select the students you want to act on Tick one or more rows. As soon as a row is selected, a batch action bar appears with Approve and Remove. There are no per-row buttons — selecting rows is how you choose who to act on. Approve or remove them Click Approve to move the selected students off the waitlist and into the activity, or Remove to take them off the list entirely. Remove asks you to confirm and can clear several students at once. A success message confirms each action.

Requesting an extra-curricular activity is a long, gated, four-step planning form — Activity details → Resource booking → Risk management → Review and submit — that goes to a coordinator or leader for approval. Any staff member with extra-curricular access can request one. A progress indicator sits in the header, and a fixed action bar with Save and exit, Back, and Next runs along the bottom. Submit stays disabled until every required field across all four steps is valid; errors show inline as you go. Open the create flow From the Extra curricular hub, click Create extra-curricular activity on the Request an extra-curricular activity action card. To resume a saved draft instead, click Edit on its New/Draft request row. Fill in the activity details (Step 1) Complete the three sub-sections in the side rail. In General information, set the Extra-curricular name and Extra activity type, then the Event start/end and Registration start/end dates and times — each start must be before its end, and start dates can't be in the past. Optionally add a Create a Teams for this activity space, an Event image (≤10 MB, .png/.jpg/.jpeg, one file), or Fixtures documents (≤10 MB each, .pdf/.doc/.docx). Set the venue and attendees (Step 1) In Venue details, choose On-site location (add rooms, each with a room, configuration, and expected attendees) or Off-site location (add venues with full contact details); the section is locked with "Please select event date first" until the event date is set. In Attendees, add at least one Student group, write the Student requirements, set Max no. of students (greater than 0) and the Staff to student ratio, pick Cost to (Parent, Parents & School, or School) with its matching amount and Payment due date, and tick at least one Accessibility considerations option. Turn on Enable waitlist to hold students beyond the max. Book resources (Step 2 — optional) You can skip this step. To book, add resource rows in Select resources (each needs a category and a specific resource, plus a quantity greater than 0 for most categories). If you book anything, Resource collection then requires Picked up by, Collection date, and Return date. Complete the risk assessment (Step 3) Each risk area — Student list, Activity based, Transport, Staff capacity — must either list risks (each with a mitigation) or be marked as no risk; you can't leave one blank. Fill in Key contacts (lead, first-aid, principal, deputy, plus a local emergency number — all phone-format-checked; principal and deputy auto-fill), tick the External provider confirmation, and in Requester clarification tick the requirements confirmation and pick a Pre-event briefing status. Review and submit (Step 4) Check the read-only summary on Review and submit, use Back to amend anything, then click Submit. A success message confirms the activity is created. Once approved by a coordinator or leader, it opens for enrolment and appears on the extra-curricular calendar. Note: Save and exit keeps a draft you can resume later from its New/Draft request row — but it's disabled until the activity has a name. If you navigate away with unsaved changes and no draft, an unsaved-changes prompt warns you before the work is lost.

Coordinators and school leaders act on Pending extra-curricular requests — approving them, declining them, or sending them back for changes. Note: The Review action and the Approve / Decline / More info buttons appear only to staff with approve permission. A coordinator who isn't authorised for that activity can open the request but can't act on it. Open the request On the All requests tab, find a Pending request and click Review in the row (or click the request name). The tab opens pre-filtered to Pending for approvers, so it's already your triage queue. Read the full plan The request opens read-only on the Review and submit summary — activity details, venue, attendees, costs, resources, and risks. To drop specific students from enrolment, open the Attendees section and use Exclude students; those students won't be enrolled when you approve. This control is review-only. 📸 needs image: the read-only Review and submit summary with the Exclude students control in the Attendees section. (The Exclude students control lives in the gated Step 4 of the create/edit wizard and couldn't be reached during the autonomous capture pass without completing the full multi-step form — capture manually.) Choose an outcome Pick a decision from the page header or bottom bar: Approve — the activity becomes live and opens for enrolment. Decline — opens a notes box; the activity leader is notified with your reason. More info — opens a notes box; sends the request back to the leader to update and resubmit. Note: Decline and More info both require notes before you can confirm. Those notes are exactly what the author reads later via View review notes on their request row, so make the reason clear. Confirm A confirmation message appears and you return to the hub.

The extra-curricular calendar shows the school's scheduled clubs and teams across a month or week, so you can plan around them. Anyone with extra-curricular access can open it. Open the calendar Click Extra curricular in the main navigation, then click View calendar on the action card at the top of the hub. The calendar opens in the canvas pane. Choose the view and dates Switch between Month and Week, and page through the dates to find the period you want. The next upcoming activity is highlighted for you automatically. Read the events Each event is colour-coded by its activity type. Click an event to open a small details pop-up showing the activity name, type, start and end, and its year group, house or class.

The details page is the management page for a live, approved activity. Open the activity From the Supervising activities tab, click an activity name. The details page opens. This tab lists only Approved and Rejected activities. Read the header The header shows the activity name, an approval status tag, and an attributes row: Dates, Lead, Year groups, and Attendees. The Attendees value is shown as registered out of maximum, for example 18 / 30. Check the venue details The left column's Venue details shows the location type, venue or room, room configuration, capacity, address, and contact details. If a fixtures file was attached, a View fixture link appears here. Review the staffing The Staffing panel lists assigned staff with their role, phone, and email. External members show a consent link. See the participants and waitlist Registered participants lists everyone enrolled, and Waitlist lists anyone waiting for a place. Each table shows Name, Year group/s, and Gender, with the maximum places labelled on the table. Find post-event feedback After the activity's end date passes, a post-event feedback section also appears on the page.
Terms used across StaffXP and this guide. A · B · C · D · E · F · G · I · K · L · M · N · O · P · R · S · T · U · V · W · Y

Term Definition Agent A single-purpose AI capability behind Felix. Each one handles one job — writing a notice, drafting a class update, logging a reward. You never choose an agent by name; you describe what you want and Felix passes the request to the right one. AI Transparency Badge The control on a student progress report listing the data sources the report was built from. Alert Icons The row of four coloured icons over a student's photo — always Custody, Physical, Learning, Medical in that order. Full colour means the alert is active; muted means it isn't on file. Active icons open a pop-up; muted ones aren't clickable. All Activities An Activities overview tab listing every approved activity org-wide. Only shows for activity coordinators and super admins. All Requests The request queue coordinators and school leaders see instead of Your requests. In extra-curricular it opens pre-filtered to Pending as a triage queue. Approved Absence A resolved absence set by an attendance officer. Locked to teachers — clicking it opens the absence's details — and skipped by bulk marking so it's never overwritten. At a Glance The landing tab of a student profile: photo, core identity details, the alert icon row, shared documents, and the alert key. Attendance Analytics The screen holding the at-risk banner, four stat cards, the Trends charts, and the at-risk table. Needs Attendance-analytics read access. Attendance Overview The whole-school attendance dashboard that school leaders and attendance officers land on. Holds the Roll reminders, Students at risk and View trends tiles, three charts, and the Class rolls list. Attendance Roll The table listing every student in a class on one page — no pagination, so nobody is missed. Shows up to four prior sessions read-only on the left and today's editable column on the right. Attendance Threshold The attendance percentage range that defines one risk band. Set per school by a school admin in Customer Engagement (CE), as an unbroken run of ranges from 0% upwards. Without thresholds the compliance checker has nothing to measure against. Authorised Contacts The people cleared to collect a student, listed on the Caregivers tab with name, address and phone number.

Term Definition Booking Status A read-only tab on the Activities and Extra-curricular hubs listing resource bookings — Event, Resource, Quantity, Picked up by, Return date and Status. Resources are booked from an activity request's Resource booking step, not here.

Term Definition Canvas The panel that opens beside the Felix chat to show an agent's output in full — a report, a dashboard, a form. Most agents open it for you; a student progress report needs Open canvas clicking first. Caregivers The student profile tab holding Parent 1, Parent 2, Custody arrangements, Emergency contacts and Authorised contacts. Where the Custody alert sends you. Case Status The state of a wellbeing case: Active (blue, open and being worked), Resolved (green, finished and read-only), or Cancelled (grey, closed without resolution and read-only). CE Customer Engagement — the Dynamics 365 back office where your school admin configures StaffXP: attendance risk thresholds, agent schedules, reward values and milestones, and the intervention library. Most teaching staff have no CE licence — the settings reach you through StaffXP. Class Rolls The list on the Attendance overview from which leaders and officers open any class's roll across the school. Searchable by class or teacher, filterable by year group, with a date-range trigger for past sessions. Cleared Classes The table on the Emergency coordinator page listing classes fully accounted for, so attention goes to the ones still outstanding. Consent Flag The warning a class update raises against any student whose parents have not consented to their name, birthday or photo being shared. Every flag must be resolved before the update can be published. Correction Form The form Felix opens when you ask to correct a submitted attendance mark. You choose the session, the student and the corrected mark, then submit it to an attendance officer. Correction Request A teacher's request to change an already-submitted attendance mark, logged through Felix — it can't be raised from the canvas or the roll — and resolved by an attendance officer from their Correction request tab. The only way to change a locked mark. Custody Alert A student alert indicating a custody order limits who may collect them. Opens the Caregivers tab so authorisation can be confirmed before release.

Term Definition Do Not Disturb A toggle in the bell panel header that stops on-screen pop-up toasts. Notifications still arrive in the panel and the bell badge still updates. Remembered between sessions. Draft A saved but unsubmitted request. Only New / Draft requests offer Edit and Delete; Save and exit creates one, and enables once the request has a name.

Term Definition Emergency Coordinator The live page shown to emergency coordinators and school leaders during an active emergency. Holds the muster table of all classes and muster points, plus the Cleared classes table. Also where a leader ends the incident. Emergency Roll The stripped-down headcount every teacher's roll becomes when a leader declares an emergency. Two columns only — Student name and Emergency roll — marked Present or Missing, with no all-marked gate on submit. Enable Waitlist The setting that lets students beyond the maximum join a waitlist rather than being turned away. Available on overseas trips and extra-curricular activities. Exclude Students A review-only control in the Attendees section of an extra-curricular review screen. Students excluded there aren't enrolled when the request is approved. Extra Curricular The hub for the school's clubs and teams, holding the request queue, Booking status, Supervising activities and Staffing tabs.

Term Definition Featured The tab at the top of the Notices board holding starred notices. Featuring is a school leader action, applies to Active or Scheduled notices only, and has a daily cap. Felix The in-app assistant, and the way into every AI agent. Used to take a class roll in the chat panel, log an attendance correction request, answer questions across the platform, and run the agents — none of which have a navigation entry point of their own. Accepts typed or voice input.
Term Definition GEMS The school group whose schools use StaffXP. Your GEMS Microsoft 365 account is the login StaffXP signs you in with.

Term Definition IEP Individual education plan — the plan setting out the support and adjustments a student receives. Listed under Shared documents on a student's At a glance tab. Intervention Library The school's own record of what should happen when a student falls into each attendance risk band — the signals to watch for and the actions to take. Uploaded by a school admin in Customer Engagement (CE). The compliance checker recommends only from what it holds, which is what keeps its recommendations consistent and within school policy.

Term Definition Key Contacts The risk-management section of an activity or venue request holding the lead teacher, principal, deputy, first-aid teacher and the local emergency number. The emergency number is required for excursions, camps, overseas trips and extra-curricular activities, and must be a valid phone number.

Term Definition Last Updated / Next Update The labels shown with any scheduled agent's output, giving the date of the last run and the date of the next. The figures are as at the last run, not as at right now. Learning Alert A student alert indicating a diagnosed learning-support need. Links to the IEP and learning-disability documents. Leave Requests An attendance officer tab on the Attendance overview holding parent-submitted leave to approve or decline.

Term Definition M365 Microsoft 365 — the Microsoft account suite your school runs on. StaffXP signs you in with your GEMS Microsoft 365 account, the same one you use for email. Manage Notices The table of notices you've created, reached from the Notices board. Seeing it means you have editing access; school leaders also see everyone's notices. Medical Alert A student alert indicating an active medical plan — allergies, medication, or condition protocols. Points to the Medical tab and Wellbeing tab. Messages The notifications tab holding items addressed to you that usually carry something to do — pending requests, attendance summaries, approvals, wellbeing follow-ups. Clicking one opens what it's about. Milestone (Rewards) A reward-points threshold that issues a certificate to the student in the Learner Experience Platform and to their parents in the Parent Experience Platform. GEMS schools use three — 50, 450 and 1,000 points. Configured per school in Customer Engagement (CE). More Info A request status meaning an approver has sent it back with notes for you to update and resubmit. Read the notes via View review notes on the request row. Muster Coordinator The live page shown to a muster-point coordinator during an emergency, covering just their own point's headcount and cleared classes. MyDay The StaffXP home page, reached by clicking StaffXP at the far left of the nav bar. Tiles show today's schedule, assignments to mark, the to-do list, notices, birthdays and open wellbeing tasks. Its look shifts through the day.

Term Definition Not on Roll The group below an emergency roll holding students added from other classes. Each is marked Present and counts toward your Present total, with Remove and Edit/add note actions. Not Yet Marked The default attendance status (shown as ···) before you mark a student. Blocks Submit until cleared. Note Type A required classification on a wellbeing note, set alongside sentiment and priority. Notify Parents A wellbeing note setting that defaults to On. Turn it off before publishing if parents shouldn't be notified.
Term Definition Open Tasks The tab in Track my notes holding wellbeing tasks assigned to you across every case. Defaults to Open; change the status filter for completed and cancelled.

Term Definition Parent Volunteers The Activities overview tab holding parent helper sign-ups. Opens filtered to Pending / More info. Approving and declining is approver-only. PDF Portable Document Format — the file format a printed roll or a published class update is saved as. Pending A request status meaning it's been submitted and is awaiting a coordinator's decision. Physical Alert A student alert indicating a recorded physical accommodation — mobility, sensory, or assistive equipment. Postcard The card created when a reward or consequence is logged, seen by the student in the Learner Experience Platform and by their parents in the Parent Experience Platform. Whether it goes out per log or in a batch is set per school in Customer Engagement (CE). Priority The urgency set on a wellbeing note: Low, Medium, High or Critical. Prompt What you type or say to Felix to start an agent. Include the word that names what you want — dashboard alone returns nothing, rewards dashboard works. Push Notifications The small pop-up cards (toasts) that slide into the corner when a notification arrives. On by default. Only appear when push is on and Do not disturb is off.

Term Definition Replicate The row action on an Approved request that opens a pre-filled copy as a brand-new request. Dates and times — and for extra-curricular, the whole registration window — are cleared, so fresh ones must be entered. The original is untouched. Called Duplicate from the All activities tab. Resource Booking The optional second step of an activity request, covering Finance, Equipment, Transportation and Technology. Skippable entirely, but a started booking row must be finished — a category and a resource — or Next stays disabled. Review Notes The notes an approver must enter when declining a request or sending it back for more info. Read by the requester via View review notes on the request row. Risk Management The step in an activity, venue or extra-curricular request where each category — Student lists, Activity based, Transport, Staff capacity — either lists risks with mitigations or is explicitly marked "no risk". Visits have no Transport category. Roll Reminders An Attendance overview tile showing a live count of classes that haven't submitted their roll yet. View all lists them by teacher, class, period and outstanding count. RSVP The reply a notice asks for when it needs numbers. Staff respond yes or no, and whoever created the notice sees who is coming.

Term Definition Sentiment A required setting on a wellbeing note recording the tone of the observation. Staff to Notify The escalation contacts listed for a student on the Wellbeing tab of their profile. Staffing The Extra-curricular tab listing staff assigned to activities with Name, Role, Phone, Email and Consent.
