Consent shows View for an external member's clearance document, Internal for internal staff, or a dash. Status Pill The interactive control in a wellbeing case header used to move the case between Active, Resolved and Cancelled. Students at Risk An Attendance overview tile showing a live count of students below the attendance threshold. Students Not on Roll The button on an emergency roll used to add a student from another class who is physically with you. Shows a live count once anyone is added; the same student can't be added twice. Supervising Activities The Extra-curricular tab ("All ECAs") listing only Approved and Rejected activities. Approved rows offer Replicate; Rejected rows offer View review notes.

Term Definition Today · All Classes The cross-class timeline in an expanded roll row showing every lesson a student has today, with your period ringed — so you can spot a student present in your class but absent later. Track My Notes Your personal wellbeing workspace, reached from the Wellbeing landing page. Three tabs: Open tasks, Active notes, and Closed/resolved notes. Turn Off Emergency Protocol The leader-only control that ends an emergency and returns every class to its normal roll. Sits in the top app toolbar and on the Emergency coordinator page. Needs the emergency deactivate permission.

Term Definition Unresolved Attendance An attendance officer tab holding marks that still need a resolution category. Unresolved Late An attendance status a teacher can set, pending an officer assigning a specific reason. URL Uniform Resource Locator — the web address of a page.

Term Definition Value The behaviour a reward or consequence is logged against — for example Care — drawn from the school's values framework in Customer Engagement (CE). Each value carries a point score. Venue Conflict A clash between a requested venue and another approved event. Disables Approve on the review screen and raises a Venue conflict detected pop-up naming the conflicting event. View Analytics The button on the teacher Attendance page opening Attendance analytics. Stays disabled without Attendance-analytics read access. View Review Notes The row action on a Rejected / Declined or More info request that opens the approver's notes explaining the decision. View Trends The tile on the leader / officer Attendance overview opening Attendance trends — absence timing, tardiness timing, and learning-area attendance bar lists. Visibility The dates that control when a notice is shown on the board. Combined with audience type, this is why your board won't match a colleague's.

Term Definition Waitlist The table on an approved extra-curricular activity holding students beyond the maximum. Only appears when the activity has a waitlist enabled. Tick rows to reveal the batch Approve and Remove actions — there are no per-row buttons. Wellbeing Note A record of a concern, observation or positive note about a student, which opens a case you can track. Needs Wellbeing write access to create. The student is fixed once published and can't be reassigned.
Term Definition Your Requests The request queue general staff see on the Activities and Extra-curricular hubs, holding only their own submissions. Always shows all statuses.

Switch the StaffXP theme between light and dark to suit your screen preferences and lighting conditions. Open the theme picker in the User menu Click the User icon (top right). The Theme row sits at the top of the menu. Pick a theme Choose Light, Subtle light, Subtle dark, or Dark — it applies instantly across the platform. Note: Light mode reads best in bright rooms, dark mode in dim ones — but it's whatever's comfortable for you. You can also set this in Settings.

MyDay is the StaffXP landing page — your quick view of the day. Return to it any time by clicking StaffXP in the navigation bar. What's on it The tiles display what you need for the day: Today's schedule and timetable, assignments to mark, your to-do list, notices, this week's birthdays, and open wellbeing tasks. Quick links The Quick links tile is the fast way into EmployeeXP, Topics & FAQs, and View markbook. Note: MyDay's look shifts through the day — morning, midday, and evening — to match when you're using it.

The navigation bar sits across the top of every screen. Here's what's on it. The main links StaffXP (far left) is your home, called the MyDay page; click it any time to return. Next to it are the section links: Attendance, Notices, Activities, Wellbeing, and Extra curricular. The menu icon The first icon on the left opens Training, Reporting, and Administration links. The far-right icons Search — find pages or students. Notifications (bell) — opens your Messages and Alerts. User menu (person) — change your theme, open your profile, adjust settings, or sign out.

StaffXP uses your GEMS Microsoft 365 account — the same login you use for email. Sign in with Microsoft Open StaffXP and click Sign in with Microsoft. Enter your details Enter your GEMS M365 email and password, then click Sign in.

End your session — worth doing on any shared or public computer. Open the user menu Click the User icon in the top right corner. Sign out Click Sign Out at the bottom of the menu. You're returned to the sign-in page. Note: Signing out ends your session, so you'll sign in again next time. Always sign out on shared devices.

Personalise StaffXP — appearance, accessibility, and notifications — from one place. Open Settings Click the User icon ▸ Settings. Appearance Set your Theme and your Font size (Small, Medium, or Large) — font size applies across the whole platform. Accessibility Toggle High contrast mode (boosts legibility, simplifies the interface) and Reduced motion (minimises animations to reduce eye strain and motion sickness). Notifications Toggle push notifications on or off. Note: Every change applies instantly across the platform — there is no need to save.

Notices help you share updates and announcements with staff, parents, and/or students. Creating requires completing three sections: Information → Audience type → Review & publish. Open the notice form Go to Notices and click Create notice +. Fill in the information Add a Notice title, choose a Notice category, and write a Notice description. Optionally add a thumbnail, a date and time, reference links, or attachments — then click Next. Note: Turn on RSVP required to let recipients confirm attendance; you will not get a notification of their attendance. Confirming adds the event to their calendar automatically. Set the audience, visibility, and publish Set the Visibility dates. In the next step, choose the Audience type (who can see it), then review everything and click Publish.

Remove a notice for good. Deletion is permanent — there's no undo. Open the notice's details In Manage notices, click the notice's title to open its details window. Delete it Click Delete, then Confirm delete on the warning. Note: Deletion can't be undone. Only the staff member who created a notice (or a school leader) can delete it.

Update a notice you already created by changing its details, audience, or visibility. Note: You can only edit a notice that you created. Open Manage notices In the Notices tab, click Manage notices. Find your notice Click the edit icon in your notice's row in the Your notices list. Use the Active notices and Scheduled notices tiles to filter if needed. Make changes and save Expand the section you want to change in Edit notice details—Details, Audience type, or Visibility—edit the fields, then click Save changes. Note: Save changes only becomes active once you've changed something.

The Notices tab is the school’s noticeboard. You see notices as cards, grouped into tabs. Open the board Click Notices in the menu. The board displays a set of tabs — Featured, Your interests, and one tab per category (General, Sport, Cultural, Arts, Community). Read a notice Click a card to flip it over. The back gives you the full description, the activity date and time, the author, any attachments or links, and an RSVP button if you can RSVP. Note: You see only notices aimed at your audience while they're within their visible dates — so your board won't match a colleague's.

Select notice categories you want to follow. These appear first under the Your interests tab. Open the Interests dropdown On the Notices board, click the Interests dropdown at the top right next to the filter icon. Pick your categories Check the categories you wish to follow: General, Sport, Cultural, Arts, and Community. Uncheck to unfollow. Choices save automatically. Note: This is personal to you — it doesn't change what anyone else sees, and every notice is still available under its own category tab.

Manage notices has the table of notices you've created. Here, you can find, open, edit and feature them. Note: If you can see Manage notices, you have editing access. You see the notices you created; school leaders also see everyone's notices. Open Manage notices On the Notices board, click Manage notices in the top right corner. Find a notice The stat tiles at the top double as filters. Click Active notices or Scheduled notices to filter the table. Click the tile again to clear the filter. You can also Search by the notice title or Filter by status and category. Click a notice's title to open its full details, or use a row's edit icon to change it.

Some notices are events you can RSVP to. Notices that take RSVPs show an RSVP tag on the card front. Open the notice On the Notices board, click the card to flip it over, then click RSVP on the back. Accept the event A confirmation shows the event title and date. Click Accept. Note: Accepting adds the event to your Outlook calendar — it's a calendar add, not a yes/no reply to the organiser. You can only RSVP once; after that, the button is disabled, so you can't add it again.

Featuring a notice highlights it in the Featured tab at the top of the board. Note: This is a school leader action — other staff don't see the feature controls. Open Manage notices On the Notices board, click Manage notices, then use Search or Filter to find the notice. Feature it Click the star icon on the notice's row. A filled star indicates the notice is featured, and a Featured updated message confirms. Click the star again to unfeature. Note: You can feature Active or Scheduled notices, not Expired ones. There's a daily cap on featured notices — if it's reached, you'll see a message that the notice publishes to the non-featured section instead.

Notifications keep you up to date as things happen in the school day. They live behind the bell in the top bar, ready on every page. Open the bell panel Click the bell icon at the top-right of the header. The Notifications slide-out panel opens. When you have unread items, a red badge on the bell shows the count (it reads 99+ above 99). Choose a tab The panel has two tabs, each with its own unread count tag: Messages — items addressed to you, usually with something to go and do (pending requests, attendance summaries, approvals, wellbeing follow-ups) — and Alerts — school-wide operational or safety notices, such as transport disruptions, weather pauses, or drills. The bell badge is the combined unread count across both tabs. Scan the list Items are grouped under Today, Yesterday and Previous, newest first. Long items have a Read more / Read less toggle. Every notification shows the same blue information icon — the type and urgency are in the words, not the icon colour. Open a notification Click any notification row. This marks it read — there is no separate mark-as-read button. A Message then takes you straight to what it's about (for example the pending-requests queue, an attendance summary, or a student's wellbeing case), and the screen you land on is briefly highlighted so you can spot it. An Alert just marks read; alerts don't link anywhere. See the full history Click View all at the bottom of the panel (it shows a count, for example "View all (12)") to open the full Notifications page, where you can filter by All, Unread or Read and page through everything. What you receive differs from your colleagues: the system decides which notifications to send you based on your role and responsibilities. The bell, the panel and these controls are the same for everyone.

Clear your whole notification list in one go. Every signed-in staff member can do this; the controls are the same for everyone. From the bell panel Click the bell icon (top right of the header) to open the Notifications panel, then click Dismiss all in the panel header. The list clears straight away, with no confirmation step. From the Notifications page Open the bell panel, click View all at the bottom, then on the Notifications page click Dismiss all (top right). This version asks first: a pop-up reads "All notifications will be permanently dismissed. Continue?" — click Dismiss all to confirm or Cancel to back out. Dismiss all is disabled when there is nothing left to clear. What gets cleared Dismissing only affects your own list — it does not notify or change anything for anyone else. Any favourited notifications are kept; everything else is removed.

Remove a single notification you've dealt with so it stops cluttering your list. Dismissing affects only your own view — it doesn't notify or change anything for anyone else. From the bell panel Click the bell in the top header bar to open the Notifications panel. Hover (or keyboard-focus) the notification you're done with and click its dismiss (✕) control. The item is removed from the list straight away. Or from the Notifications page On the Notifications page, each row has its own ✕ button — click it to dismiss that item. This works on either the Messages or Alerts tab.

Do not disturb stops new notifications popping up on screen while you are busy, without switching notifications off. Every signed-in staff member has this control. Open the notifications panel Click the bell icon at the top right of the header (it shows on every page). The Notifications slide-out panel opens. Switch on Do not disturb Toggle Do not disturb in the panel header. New notifications stop showing the brief pop-up toast in the corner of the screen. Items still arrive in the panel and the bell badge still updates its count, so nothing is missed. The toggle is remembered between sessions, so turn it back off when you want pop-ups again.

Push notifications are the small pop-up cards (toasts) that slide into the corner of the screen when a new notification arrives and then auto-dismiss. They are on by default. Every signed-in staff member can change this setting. Open Settings Open the user menu (your avatar, top-right) and choose Settings. Switch push notifications on or off In the Notifications section, switch Push notifications on or off — the change applies instantly. A pop-up only appears when Push notifications is on and Do not disturb is off — either one switched off stops the pop-ups. Know what this does and does not change Clicking a pop-up does the same as clicking the notification in the panel: it marks the item read and opens what it is about. This setting only controls the pop-ups — the bell, the slide-out panel, and the Notifications page always keep working. To silence pop-ups just for a while without changing this setting, toggle Do not disturb in the bell panel instead.
documents.s: Turn pop-up notifications on or off

documents.t: The Notifications page is the full-history view of everything the bell panel shows, with filtering and paging the panel doesn't have. Every signed-in staff member can open it. Open the page Click the bell in the top header bar to open the slide-out panel, then click View all at the bottom. View all shows a count of how many items you have (for example "View all (12)"). There is no main-navigation link — the bell panel is the only way in. Switch between Messages and Alerts The page has two tabs. Messages are items addressed to you, usually with a "go here" action; Alerts are school-wide operational and safety notices. Here the count tag on each tab shows the total number of items in that tab — unlike the bell panel, where the same-looking tag shows only the unread count. Filter the list Use the All / Unread / Read filter to narrow what you see. Each option shows a live count for the current tab. Items are grouped under Today and Previous, newest first. Load older items The page shows the first 10 items. Click Load more to reveal another 10 at a time. Switching tab or changing the filter resets the list back to the first 10. Open or dismiss an item Click any row to open it: this marks the item read and, for a message, takes you straight to what it's about (alerts just mark read). Each row also has a dismiss (✕) button that removes that item from your list only — it doesn't affect anyone else.

A student profile is the single read-only record for one student — their details, contacts, alerts, and timetable. The quickest way in is their name, which is a link almost everywhere it appears. Click the student's name Find the student on any screen that lists them — a class roll, an attendance list, a wellbeing case, an emergency screen — and click their name. The profile opens at the At a glance tab. The same profile opens wherever you click from; the starting screen only sets the breadcrumb back-link, so opening from a class roll lets that trail return you to the roll. Or search by name Open the search in the top toolbar and type at least 2 characters of the student's name. Results appear after a short pause as you type, split into Pages (places in the app) and Students. Click the student row to open their profile. Searching for students needs search access — without it, the students section simply doesn't appear. Confirm you're on the right student The profile header shows the student's name, with their Student ID, House and Enrolment status as inline attributes. Everything here is read-only — you view and copy, you don't edit a student's record from this page.

Your profile page is a read-only view of your own staff account — name, role, contact and work details. It is reached from the user menu only and is separate from any student profile. Open the user menu Click your avatar in the top-right corner. Click Profile Choose Profile from the menu. The page opens showing your avatar and name, with Role and Department as header attributes. Read your details Below the header, three cards list what your organisation has on file: Personal Information — First name, Last name, Pronouns, Birthday. Professional Information — Work email address, Phone number. Work Information — Job title, Company, Department, Business address, Office location. Only fields that have a value are shown within a card; a card with nothing on file shows Not provided. Editing your details Everything here is read-only — this is a view of your account, not an editor. Profile data comes from your organisation's directory, so to change a detail, ask whoever manages your directory account.

At a glance is the landing tab of a student's profile — their photo and core details, a row of alert icons, and any shared documents. Everything here is read-only: you view and copy, you never edit a student's record. Open the profile Click a student's name anywhere it appears — a class roll, an attendance list, a wellbeing case — or search the name in the header search and pick the student. The profile opens on At a glance. Opening it needs student-profile read access. Read the student's details The Student details block shows the photo (or a placeholder) and the core identity fields: Name, Surname, Preferred name, Gender, Age, Date of birth, First language, and Nationality. An empty field shows a dash (—) — that's normal, not an error. Check the alert icons Over the photo is a row of four coloured icons, always in the same order: Custody, Physical, Learning, Medical. A full-colour icon means that alert is active for this student; a muted/greyed icon means it's not on file. The icons stay in place even when inactive, so the row reads the same for every student. Whether an alert shows depends on the student's data, not on your role. Custody — a custody order limits who may collect the student. Physical — a recorded physical accommodation (mobility, sensory, assistive equipment). Learning — a diagnosed learning-support need; refer to the IEP. Medical — an active medical plan (allergies, medication, condition protocols). Open an active alert for detail Click an active icon to open a short pop-up explaining it. Where relevant the pop-up links you on: Custody opens the Caregivers tab so you can check who may collect the student before releasing them; Learning links the IEP and learning-disability documents; Medical points to the Medical plan and Wellbeing tab. The Physical pop-up shows a general note only. Muted (inactive) icons are not clickable. Note: Before releasing a student to anyone, follow an active Custody alert through to the Caregivers tab and confirm the person is authorised to collect them. Open shared documents Shared documents lists any Individual education plan (IEP), diagnosed learning disability, or medical plan document attached to the student — click one to view or download it. If nothing is attached, the section says so. Use the alert key Alert descriptions at the bottom is a static key explaining all four alert types, so you can read the row even when you're new to it.
documents.s: View a student at a glance

documents.t: The Caregivers tab on a student's profile shows who the family is, how to reach them, custody status, and who's authorised to collect or be contacted — all read-only. Open the Caregivers tab Go to the student's profile and select the Caregivers tab. The sections read top to bottom: Parent 1, Parent 2, Custody arrangements, Emergency contacts and Authorised contacts. Read the parent contact details Each parent block lists First name, Last name, Parent preferred name, Relationship to student, Home address, the Same as residential address tick, Mailing address, Parent's email, Communication preference, Phone number, Work and WhatsApp, plus the parent's Visa and passport details. Parent 2 appears only when a second parent is recorded, and a Mailing address is shown separately only when it differs from the home address. Copy a value to your clipboard Home address, mailing address, email and phone numbers each have a copy button next to them — click it to copy the value, handy for dialling or pasting into an email. The copy button shows only when there's actually a value. Check custody before releasing a student Custody arrangements is a single read-only tick: Custody arrangements in place. This tab is where the Custody alert sends you, so check it before you release a student or contact family. Note: When custody arrangements are in place, confirm who is authorised to collect the student here before letting them leave with anyone. See emergency and authorised contacts Emergency contacts is a table of Contact full name, Emergency ranking, Address and Phone number — the ranking tells you who to call first. Authorised contacts lists the people cleared to collect the student, with Contact full name, Address and Phone number.

The Classroom management tab gathers a student's learning programme, the courses they're enrolled in, their overall attendance, and any diagnosed disability or learning difficulty. Like the rest of the profile, it's read-only — you view and copy, you don't edit here. Open the Classroom management tab On a student profile, open the Classroom management tab. Read the learning programme Learning programs shows the Curriculum type, Learning mode, Specialised program, and a free-text Timetable. Below them, the Courses table lists each course with its Name, Code, Educational institution, Begin date – End date, and Exit reason. The table reads No courses when the student has none enrolled. Check attendance Attendance shows the student's overall Attendance percentage. Read disability and learning difficulty detail Disability and learning difficulties records Diagnosed disability (Yes/No) with its Category and Condition, and Diagnosed learning disability (Yes/No) with its Category. Where a diagnosed learning disability document is on file, a link to it appears here; otherwise the section shows a "none attached" line. Any field with no value shows a dash (—) — that's normal, not an error.

The Demographics tab holds a student's fuller identity record — residency, transport, visa details, and any siblings enrolled at the school. Everything is read-only: you view and copy, you don't edit a student's record here. Open the Demographics tab On a student profile, open the Demographics tab. It sits alongside the other profile tabs. Read Student details The Student details block covers identity and enrolment: Name, Surname, Preferred name, Gender, Age, Date of birth, First language, Nationality, Academic year group, Commencement year, Roll group, Residential student (Yes/No), School transport (Yes/No), and Interest survey. Read Visa information The Visa information block lists Visa number, Visa type, Issuing country, Place of issue, Number of entries, Date of issue, Date of expiration, and Stay duration. Visa remarks only show when there are remarks on file. Check Enrolled siblings The Enrolled siblings table lists each sibling at the school with their Name, Relationship type, Academic year group, and Date of birth. If the student has none, it shows No enrolled siblings. Any field with no value shows a dash (—) — this is normal, not an error.

The Medical tab gathers a student's condition, medication, care and medical plans, vaccination record, and their doctor. Like the rest of the profile it is read-only — you view and copy this information, you don't edit it here. This is also where the Medical alert pop-up sends you for condition and medication detail. Open the Medical tab On the student's profile, click the Medical tab. Read Medical details The Medical details section lists the medical condition name, Severity, Medication required (Yes or No), and the Start date and End date of the condition. Open the attached plans Below the details, View care plan, View medication plan and View vaccination record open the documents on file. Each link only appears when that document exists; otherwise the section shows a "nothing attached" line in its place. View vaccination record opens a pop-up with the latest record — student info, the Is vaccinated and Parent consent ticks, vaccination and administered dates, and links to the vaccination card and card URL. Read Doctor details The Doctor details section shows the doctor name, plus the medical centre name, address and phone — the contacts to call about this student's care.

See what a student has on today — the day's classes, where they are, and what they're in right now. The timetable is read-only, like the rest of the profile. Open the Timetable tab On the student's profile, open the Timetable tab. It opens to Today's Timetable, the list of classes scheduled for the current day. Read the day's classes Each row shows the Period, Full class name, Room number, and Start and end time. Any field with no value shows a dash. If the student has no classes scheduled, the tab shows a "nothing scheduled" message instead of a list. Spot the class happening now The class in progress is tagged Now — a blue tag next to the class name — worked out from the current time against each class's start and end time, so it's an at-a-glance answer to where the student should be right now.

The Wellbeing tab on a student profile gathers every wellbeing note raised for that student, plus the contacts to escalate to. Like the rest of the profile, it is read-only — you view and copy here, you don't raise or manage a case from this page. Open the Wellbeing tab On the student profile, click the Wellbeing tab. Check who to notify Staff to notify lists the escalation contacts for this student. If no one is set, it reads No staff to notify. Read the wellbeing notes Wellbeing notes is a searchable table of every note raised for the student. Each row shows the Date, the Title, the Priority (Low, Medium, High or Critical, shown as an icon) and the Status of the wellbeing case (shown as a coloured tag). Type in the search box to filter, and set how many rows show per page — 10, 25, 50 or 100. When there are no notes the table reads No wellbeing notes yet. This table only shows notes. To raise a note or manage a case, work in the Wellbeing feature rather than here.
Common problems in StaffXP and how to resolve them. Use the contents list on the right to jump to a section, or press Ctrl+F to search this page.
Cause — A personal or non-GEMS Microsoft account is being used. Fix — Click Sign in with Microsoft and use your GEMS M365 email and password — the same login you use for email.
documents.s: I can't sign in to StaffXP

documents.t: Cause — What you see in the nav bar depends on your access. Attendance, Notices, Activities, Wellbeing and Extra curricular each need their own permission. Fix — Ask your school leader or administrator to confirm your access. The Training, Reporting and Administration links sit behind the menu icon at the far left, not in the main link row.
documents.s: A section link is missing from the navigation bar

documents.t: Cause — MyDay's look shifts through the day — morning, midday and evening — to match when you're using it. Fix — Nothing is wrong. The tiles and content are unchanged.
documents.s: The MyDay page looks different from this morning

documents.t: Cause — Font size is a per-user setting. Fix — Open the User icon ▸ Settings ▸ Appearance and set Font size to Small, Medium or Large. It applies across the whole platform and saves instantly. High contrast mode and Reduced motion are also there under Accessibility.
documents.s: The text is too small to read comfortably

documents.t: Cause — Theme is set per user and applies instantly, so there's nothing to save. Fix — Set it from the User icon (the Theme row at the top of the menu) or in Settings ▸ Appearance. Choose Light, Subtle light, Subtle dark or Dark.

Cause — At least one student is still on Not yet marked (the ··· default), or you're offline. Fix — Every student needs a valid status before Submit enables — this is deliberate, so a partial roll can't be sent. Check for unmarked rows, and reconnect if you're offline.
documents.s: The Submit button on the roll is greyed out

documents.t: Cause — A submitted roll is locked. There's no direct edit. Fix — Ask Felix to correct an attendance mark ("I need to correct an attendance mark"). Felix opens a pre-filled correction form — set the corrected mark and a reason, then submit. An attendance officer resolves it from their Correction request tab. This is the only route; you can't edit the locked roll yourself.
documents.s: I've submitted the roll and marked someone wrong

documents.t: Cause — All present and All absent deliberately skip any student who already holds an approved absence, so a resolved absence is never overwritten. Fix — Expected behaviour. Adjust individual students afterwards if needed.
Cause — Bulk marking doesn't save on its own. Fix — After setting the column, click Submit to send the roll. Use Reset on the same column menu to clear pending marks and start again.
documents.s: I marked the whole column but nothing saved

documents.t: Cause — Marking a whole column needs Attendance write access. For read-only staff the control is hidden. Fix — Ask an attendance officer or leader to mark the roll, or request write access.
documents.s: I can't see the column action control on the roll

documents.t: Cause — For teachers, past sessions open read-only — you mark only today's column. Fix — This is expected. An attendance officer can edit a past-dated roll; ask one to make the change.
documents.s: I can't change a mark on a past session

documents.t: Cause — Approved absences are resolved by an attendance officer elsewhere and are locked to teachers. Fix — Clicking the status opens the absence's details. To change it, ask an attendance officer.
documents.s: I can't change a student's approved absence

documents.t: Cause — Printing fetches the attendance document and needs a live connection. Fix — Reconnect and click the print icon again.
Cause — Attendance analytics needs Attendance-analytics read access. Fix — Ask your school leader to grant it. Without it the button stays disabled.
documents.s: The View analytics button is disabled

documents.t: Cause — The same Attendance nav item opens the teacher page for most staff and the whole-school Attendance overview for school leaders and attendance officers. Fix — Expected. From the overview, use the Class rolls list below the charts to open any class's roll.
documents.s: I open Attendance and get a dashboard, not my class calendar

documents.t: Cause — Leave requests, Class rolls, Unresolved attendance, Correction request and Resolved requests are officer-only. Leaders see the dashboard without them. Fix — Expected. Ask an attendance officer to work those queues.
documents.s: I can't find the officer tabs on the Attendance overview

documents.t: Cause — A roll inherits the class's year-group attendance setting — either AM/PM or Period, never both. Fix — Expected. The setting is per year group, not per roll.
documents.s: A roll shows AM/PM when I expected periods

documents.t: Cause — Declaring an emergency is school-leader-only, and the button lives in the top app toolbar rather than on an Attendance page. Fix — Ask a school leader to declare it. Taking the emergency roll, by contrast, is for every teacher.
documents.s: I can't see the red Emergency button

documents.t: Cause — Ending an emergency needs the emergency deactivate permission and is leader-only. Coordinators can watch the live muster but can't stand the incident down. Fix — Ask a school leader to click Turn off emergency protocol — it sits in the top app toolbar and on the Emergency coordinator page.

Cause — Emergency mode is deliberately minimal — no date picker, no print, no birthday cue, and per-period history and Attendance % are hidden. Fix — Expected. Those controls return when the emergency ends.
documents.s: The emergency roll won't let me pick a date or print

documents.t: Cause — During an emergency, students may end up with the nearest teacher rather than their own. Fix — On the Emergency roll, click Students not on roll, click Add, search and pick the student, and add an optional reason (up to 100 characters). They appear in a Not on roll group marked Present and count toward your total. The same student can't be added twice — you'll see an Already added warning.
documents.s: I have a student with me who isn't on my roll

documents.t: Cause — There is no all-marked gate on an emergency roll. Fix — Click Submit with what you have. Coordinators chase the rest. The live counter strip shows running Unmarked, Missing and Present totals.
documents.s: I can't submit the emergency roll because students are unmarked

documents.t: Cause — The Emergency coordinator and Muster coordinator pages only exist while an emergency is active. Fix — Expected. They close when a leader ends the emergency. To review a past incident, a leader opens Attendance ▸ Emergency.

Cause — Emergency analytics is leader-only — not available to teachers or attendance officers. Fix — Ask a school leader. They open Attendance ▸ Emergency, filter by type, term and year, and can print an incident's details page for a debrief.
documents.s: I can't find the emergency history

documents.t: Cause — You only see notices aimed at your audience, and only while they're within their visible dates. Fix — Expected. Every notice is still available under its own category tab for the audience it targets.
documents.s: My noticeboard doesn't match a colleague's

documents.t: Cause — You can only RSVP once. After that the button is disabled. Fix — Expected. Note that accepting adds the event to your Outlook calendar — it's a calendar add, not a yes/no reply to the organiser.

Cause — RSVP confirms attendance for the recipient by adding the event to their calendar. It does not notify the notice author. Fix — Expected behaviour. Collect attendance another way if you need a list.
documents.s: I created a notice with RSVP but haven't been told who's coming

documents.t: Cause — Manage notices only appears if you have editing access. Fix — Ask a school leader for access. If you can see it, you see the notices you created; school leaders also see everyone's.
Cause — You can only edit a notice that you created. Fix — Ask the author, or a school leader, to make the change.
documents.s: I can't edit someone else's notice

documents.t: Cause — Save changes only becomes active once you've changed something. Fix — Expand the section you want in Edit notice details — Details, Audience type, or Visibility — edit a field, and the button enables.
documents.s: Save changes is greyed out when editing a notice

documents.t: Cause — Featuring is a school leader action, and only Active or Scheduled notices can be featured — not Expired ones. Fix — Ask a school leader. If they hit the daily cap on featured notices, a message explains the notice publishes to the non-featured section instead.
Cause — Deletion is permanent. Fix — There's no undo — the notice has to be recreated. Only the staff member who created a notice, or a school leader, can delete one.
documents.s: I deleted a notice by mistake

documents.t: Cause — You can skip resource booking entirely, but once you start a booking row you must finish it — pick a resource category and a resource. Fix — Complete the row, or remove it, and Next enables.
documents.s: Next is disabled on the Resource booking step

documents.t: Cause — Submit stays disabled until every required field across all steps is valid. Fix — An error message appears against each invalid field, so work back through the steps and fix what's flagged. Common misses: the local emergency number under Key contacts (required for excursions, camps and overseas trips, and it must be a valid phone number), and every risk category either listing risks with mitigations or being marked "no risk".
documents.s: Submit is disabled on Review and submit

documents.t: Cause — Save and exit only enables once you've entered an activity name. Fix — Enter the activity name first. Leaving with unsaved changes prompts you before the work is lost.
documents.s: Save and exit is greyed out

documents.t: Cause — Only approved venues can be picked from the list. Fix — Click Request venue on the Activities overview and complete the three-step flow — Venue details, Risk management, Review and submit. Both a public-liability insurance file and an emergency plan file are required before you can submit. You can also start a venue request from inside an activity request while picking a venue.
documents.s: The venue I need isn't in the list

documents.t: Cause — Only New / Draft requests show Edit and Delete. Fix — Once a request is Pending, Approved or Rejected it can't be deleted. A Rejected or More info request reopens instead — to read the review notes or to edit and resubmit.

Cause — Decline and Request more info both require notes, which live on the request row rather than in an email. Fix — Use View review notes on the request's row to read exactly what the coordinator said.
documents.s: A coordinator sent my request back and I don't know why

documents.t: Cause — The requested venue clashes with another approved event. Fix — A Venue conflict detected pop-up names the conflicting event. The clash must be resolved before you can approve.
documents.s: I can't approve a request — the Approve button is disabled

documents.t: Cause — Review only appears on Pending requests, and only for coordinators. Fix — Ask an activity coordinator or school leader to action it.
documents.s: I can't see the Review action on a Pending request

documents.t: Cause — All activities only shows for activity coordinators and super admins. Fix — Expected. General staff see Your requests; coordinators and leaders see All requests plus a My requests tab for their own submissions.
documents.s: I can't find the All activities tab

documents.t: Cause — Replicate clears the dates and times deliberately, so you set fresh ones rather than copying the old schedule. Fix — Enter the new start and end dates (and the meeting/pick-up times if the activity type uses them). Submit stays disabled until they're filled. The original activity is untouched — Replicate creates a brand-new request.
documents.s: I duplicated an activity but the dates are blank

documents.t: Cause — Booking status is a read-only view. Fix — Resources are booked from within an activity request, on its Resource booking step.
documents.s: I can't change a booking on the Booking status tab

documents.t: Cause — The calendar is read-only — it's there to help you pick an available date before you submit. Fix — Use Request activity on the overview to start a request.
documents.s: I can't create anything from the activities calendar

documents.t: Cause — Reviewing parent volunteers is approver-only — activity coordinator, school leader, or super admin. General staff can see the list but not the controls. Fix — Ask an approver. They can also select several rows and use the batch Approve / Decline actions, or Remove someone already signed off.
documents.s: I can't approve or decline a parent volunteer

documents.t: Cause — For approvers, All requests opens pre-filtered to Pending — it's the triage queue. Fix — Clear the Pending chip to see every status. Your own Your requests / My requests tabs always show all statuses.
documents.s: The All requests tab isn't showing everything

documents.t: Cause — It stays locked with "Please select event date first" until the event date is set. Fix — Set the event start and end dates in General information, then return to Venue details.
documents.s: The Venue details section is locked

documents.t: Cause — Each start must be before its end, and start dates can't be in the past. Fix — Adjust the dates so both windows are valid and in the future.
documents.s: The event or registration dates won't accept my entry

documents.t: Cause — There are limits per file type. An Event image must be ≤10 MB, .png/.jpg/.jpeg, and one file only. Fixtures documents must be ≤10 MB each, .pdf/.doc/.docx. Fix — Resize or convert the file to fit and try again.
documents.s: My image or fixtures file won't upload

documents.t: Cause — If you book anything under Select resources, the Resource collection section then requires Picked up by, Collection date and Return date. Fix — Complete those three fields, or remove the booking rows if you don't need resources.
documents.s: Resource collection is asking for more information

documents.t: Cause — Each risk area — Student list, Activity based, Transport, Staff capacity — must either list risks (each with a mitigation) or be marked as no risk. You can't leave one blank. Fix — Work through each category and mark it explicitly.
documents.s: A risk category won't let me move on

documents.t: Cause — Edit and Delete are only available while a request is New or Draft. Fix — Once Pending, Approved or Declined you act on it through Review, View review notes, or Replicate instead.
documents.s: I can't edit my extra-curricular request

documents.t: Cause — The Approve / Decline / More info buttons appear only to staff with approve permission. A coordinator who isn't authorised for that activity can open the request but can't decide it. Fix — Ask an authorised coordinator or school leader.
documents.s: I can open a request for review but can't act on it

documents.t: Cause — Exclusions are set at review time, not afterwards. Fix — On the review screen, open the Attendees section and use Exclude students. Those students won't be enrolled when you approve. The control is review-only.
documents.s: A student needs to come off the enrolment before I approve

documents.t: Cause — The Waitlist table only appears when the activity has a waitlist turned on. Fix — Waitlists are set at request time with Enable waitlist. Without it, students beyond the maximum can't join.
documents.s: The Waitlist table isn't on the activity

documents.t: Cause — There are no per-row buttons — selecting rows is how you choose who to act on. Fix — Tick one or more rows. A batch action bar appears with Approve and Remove.
documents.s: There are no buttons on the waitlist rows

documents.t: Cause — Removing takes the student off the activity straight away. Fix — They have to register again, or be approved from the waitlist.
documents.s: I removed a participant by mistake

documents.t: Cause — The post-event feedback section only appears after the activity's end date passes. Fix — Expected. Check back after the activity has run.
documents.s: An approved activity isn't showing post-event feedback

documents.t: Cause — Creating a note needs Wellbeing write access (pastoral and student-support staff, leaders). It's also disabled when you're offline. Fix — Reconnect if you're offline. Otherwise ask for write access — read-only staff see the button greyed out.
documents.s: The Create wellbeing note button is disabled

documents.t: Cause — The student is fixed once you publish. The Subject section is hidden when editing. Fix — A note can't be reassigned to a different student. Cancel or resolve the note and raise a new one against the correct student.
documents.s: I picked the wrong student on a note

documents.t: Cause — Notify parents defaults to On. Fix — Turn it off before publishing on future notes. Staff notification works the other way — adding any staff member switches it on; leaving it empty leaves it off.
documents.s: Parents were notified and I didn't intend that

documents.t: Cause — It stays disabled until every required field is valid — Title (up to 100 characters), Note type, Description, Sentiment and Priority are all required. Fix — Complete the missing fields and Publish enables.
Cause — Note attachments are capped at 10 MB each and limited to .jpg, .png, .pdf, .doc and .docx. Fix — Resize or convert the file. Comment attachments are one file, max 10 MB, any file type.
documents.s: My attachment won't upload to a note

documents.t: Cause — A resolved or cancelled case is read-only. An info banner explains this on the case. Fix — Reopen the case by setting its status back to Active from the status menu, or by ticking it in the landing-page table and clicking Mark Active. It becomes editable again.
documents.s: Edit details, Add comment and Add task are hidden or disabled

documents.t: Cause — Tick-boxes only appear on the active notes list. Fix — Find the case in the landing page table, tick it, and use the batch action bar. That's the reliable route for status changes.
documents.s: I can't change a case's status from the Closed/resolved notes tab

documents.t: Cause — Batch status changes apply to everything ticked. Fix — The confirmation toast shows an Undo option for about 8 seconds. Clicking it reverts every note to its previous status, even across a mixed selection.
documents.s: I just resolved the wrong cases

documents.t: Cause — The Wellbeing tab on a student profile is read-only. Fix — Work from the Wellbeing area itself to raise a note or manage a case.
documents.s: I can't raise a note from a student's profile

documents.t: Cause — The heading reads All wellbeing notes only if you have view-all permission (leaders and coordinators). Otherwise it shows only notes you created or were assigned. Fix — Expected. Ask a leader if you need the wider view.
documents.s: The wellbeing table heading says "My wellbeing notes", not "All"

documents.t: Cause — The metrics cards are read-only summary figures, not clickable filters. Fix — Use the table's own search and priority filter instead.
documents.s: The metrics cards won't filter the table

documents.t: Cause — Tasks live across cases rather than in one list on the landing page. Fix — Click Track my notes on the Wellbeing landing page and open the Open tasks tab. It defaults to showing Open tasks — clear or change the status filter to see completed and cancelled ones.
documents.s: I can't find a task assigned to me

documents.t: Cause — Deleting a task is permanent. The confirmation warns that the action cannot be undone. Fix — The task has to be recreated. To move a task out of the way instead, set its Status to Cancelled rather than deleting it.
documents.s: I deleted a task by mistake

documents.t: Cause — The two views count differently. In the bell panel, the tag on each tab shows the unread count and the bell badge is the combined unread across both tabs. On the full Notifications page, the same-looking tag shows the total number of items in that tab. Fix — Expected. Use the All / Unread / Read filter on the page to narrow to what you want.
documents.s: The bell badge doesn't match the tab counts on the Notifications page

documents.t: Cause — Clicking a notification row marks it read. There's no separate control. Fix — Click the row. A Message then takes you to what it's about; an Alert just marks read, as alerts don't link anywhere.
documents.s: I can't find a mark-as-read button

documents.t: Cause — A pop-up only appears when Push notifications is on and Do not disturb is off. Either one switched off stops them. Fix — Check Do not disturb in the bell panel header, and Push notifications under Settings ▸ Notifications. Do not disturb is remembered between sessions.
Cause — Do not disturb only stops the on-screen pop-up toast. Fix — Expected. Notifications still arrive in the panel and the bell badge still updates, so nothing is missed.
documents.s: Items still arrive while Do not disturb is on

documents.t: Cause — The bell panel is the only way in. Fix — Click the bell, then View all at the bottom of the panel.
documents.s: There's no navigation link to the Notifications page

documents.t: Cause — The page loads the first 10 and pages from there. Fix — Click Load more to reveal another 10 at a time. Switching tab or changing the filter resets the list back to the first 10.
documents.s: The Notifications page only shows 10 items

documents.t: Cause — Favourited notifications are kept; everything else is removed. Fix — Expected. Note the two Dismiss all controls behave differently: in the bell panel it clears immediately with no confirmation, while on the Notifications page it asks first.
Cause — The system decides which notifications to send based on your role and responsibilities. Fix — Expected. The bell, panel and controls are the same for everyone; only the contents differ.
documents.s: I get different notifications from my colleagues

documents.t: Cause — Search needs at least 2 characters, results appear after a short pause, and searching for students needs search access. Fix — Type at least two characters and wait a moment. Results split into Pages and Students. If the Students section doesn't appear at all, you don't have search access for students — ask an administrator.
Cause — An empty field shows a dash (—). Fix — Normal, not an error. It means the school holds no value for that field.
documents.s: A profile field shows a dash

documents.t: Cause — Only active alerts are clickable. A muted or greyed icon means the alert isn't on file for that student. Fix — Expected. The four icons — Custody, Physical, Learning, Medical — stay in place even when inactive, so the row reads the same for every student.

Cause — Custody detail lives on a different tab from the alert. Fix — Click the active Custody icon on At a glance — it takes you to the Caregivers tab. Check Custody arrangements and the Authorised contacts table there before releasing the student to anyone.
documents.s: I need to know who can collect a student

documents.t: Cause — Student profiles are read-only throughout — you view and copy, you don't edit. Fix — Expected. Contact whoever maintains student records at your school.
documents.s: I can't edit a student's record

documents.t: Cause — Each link only appears when that document exists. Fix — Where nothing is attached, the section shows a "nothing attached" line instead. Expected behaviour, not a fault.
documents.s: A medical or learning plan link isn't showing

documents.t: Cause — Your profile page is a read-only view of your account, not an editor. The data comes from your organisation's directory.
documents.s: I can't change my own profile details

documents.t: Cause — None of the agents has a menu, button or tile. They are built as standalone products, and StaffXP reaches them through Felix. Fix — Expected. Open Felix and describe what you want. See How Felix and the artificial intelligence (AI) agents work for what each agent answers to.
documents.s: I can't find an agent anywhere in the navigation

documents.t: Cause — StaffXP has several dashboards, so dashboard on its own doesn't identify one. Fix — Name it: rewards dashboard, attendance risk dashboard. You don't have to match the wording in this guide exactly — close and near matches are recognised — but the identifying word has to be there.
documents.s: Felix returned nothing when I asked for a dashboard

documents.t: Cause — Felix matches on close spelling. A misspelling that is also a real word can't be told apart from what you actually typed. Fix — Check the name and student ID Felix offers before confirming. If several students match, they're all listed — pick from those. If Felix says it can't identify the student, retype the name in full rather than rephrasing the request.
documents.s: Felix picked the wrong student, or can't find the one I mean

documents.t: Comments are the follow-up timeline on a wellbeing case. Use them to log an update, an action you took, or anything worth recording against the case. Open the comment form On the case detail page, in the Comments tile, click the + (Add comment). Note: The + only appears for staff with wellbeing write access, and it is hidden once a case is resolved or cancelled. Reopen the case to comment again. Write the comment In Add comment, enter a Title (up to 100 characters) and the Notes text (up to 250 characters). Optionally attach one supporting file (max 10 MB, any file type). Save it Click Save. The comment appears at the top of the timeline, which shows newest-first. Once there are more than five comments, Show older comments reveals the rest. To change a comment later, use the pencil icon on that comment.
documents.s: Add a comment to a case

documents.t: A wellbeing note records a concern, an observation, or a positive note about a student, and opens a case you can track from there. Creating a note needs Wellbeing write access (pastoral and student-support staff, leaders); read-only staff see a disabled Create wellbeing note button, which is also disabled when you are offline. Open the form On the Wellbeing landing page, click Create wellbeing note (top right). It opens as a single Create wellbeing note window with Subject, Note, Link, Notifications, and Attachments sections. Choose the student In Subject, search for and pick the Student name. Their Student ID and Year group fill in automatically and are read-only. Note: The student is fixed once you publish. You cannot reassign a note to a different student later, so pick the right one now. Write the note In Note, enter the Title (up to 100 characters), choose a Note type, write the Description, and set a Sentiment and a Priority (Low, Medium, High, or Critical). All of these are required. Add links, notifications, or attachments Optionally, in Link attach a related Linked note; in Notifications pick staff to notify (adding any staff member switches staff notification on; leaving it empty leaves it off) and set Notify parents; in Attachments upload photos or documents (max 10 MB each: .jpg, .png, .pdf, .doc, .docx). Note: Notify parents defaults to On. Turn it off before publishing if parents should not be notified. Publish Click Publish note, which stays disabled until every required field is valid. A "Wellbeing note created" toast confirms it.

The Wellbeing tab on a student's profile is a read-only roll-up of every wellbeing note raised for that one student. Open the Wellbeing tab Go to the student's profile and select the Wellbeing tab. Check who gets notified Staff to notify lists the student's escalation contacts. Browse the notes Wellbeing notes is a table of every note raised for the student, showing Date, Title, Priority and Status. Search the list and page through the results. This tab is read-only — there are no create or edit controls here, so to raise a new note or change an existing one, work from the Wellbeing area itself.

Move a wellbeing case between Active, Resolved, and Cancelled. Resolve a case when it is finished, cancel one that is closed without resolution, or set a closed case back to Active to reopen it. Note: Changing a case's status needs Wellbeing write access (pastoral / student-support staff and leaders). Readers such as classroom teachers can open a case but cannot change its status. Tick the notes you want to change On the Wellbeing landing page, or on the Active notes tab in Track wellbeing notes, use the tick-boxes to select one or more notes. You can select several at once and change them all together. Choose the new status In the batch action bar, click Mark Resolved, Mark Cancelled, or Mark Active. A success toast confirms how many cases changed. Resolving or cancelling a case makes it read-only: no new comments, tasks, or edits are possible until you reopen it by setting it back to Active. Reopen a closed case To reopen a resolved or cancelled case, find it in the landing page table, tick it, and click Mark Active. The case becomes editable again. Tick-boxes only appear on the active notes list, so the table batch actions are the reliable way to change status, and notes on the Closed/resolved notes tab cannot be re-ticked for a status change from that tab. Undo a change Right after a change, the confirmation toast shows an Undo option for about 8 seconds. Click it to revert every note to its previous status, even across a mixed selection.
documents.s: Resolve, cancel, or reopen a case

documents.t: Track wellbeing notes is your personal workspace for the open tasks assigned to you and the wellbeing notes you own, split across three tabs. Open your tracking workspace On the Wellbeing landing page, click Track my notes at the top right. Check your open tasks On the Open tasks tab, see the tasks assigned to you across every case — Task title, Case, Student, Priority. This tab defaults to showing Open tasks; clear or change the status filter to see completed and cancelled ones. Search, filter by status and priority, and click a row to expand it for the description, status, created/updated dates, and Open case / Edit task buttons. Review your active notes On the Active notes tab, see the wellbeing notes you currently own, in the same table layout as the landing page. Look back at closed notes The Closed/resolved notes tab lists your resolved and cancelled notes. Open a case Click a Case link (in tasks) or a Case title (in notes) to open that case's detail page. The count in each tab label reflects what that tab will load, so you can size up your workload before opening it.

Change a note's content after it's created. The fields are the same as when you created it, pre-filled with the current values. Note: Editing a note needs write access (pastoral / student-support staff or leaders). Edit details does not appear for read-only staff. Open the case and start editing Click the Case title to open the case detail page, then click Edit details in the header. Edit details is disabled while a case is resolved or cancelled — reopen the case (set it back to Active) before you can edit it. Change the fields In the Edit wellbeing note modal, update the Title, Note type, Sentiment, Priority, or Description. You can also change Notify parents / staff, linked notes, or attachments. The Subject (student) section is hidden, so you cannot reassign a note to a different student — the student is fixed when the note is created. Save your changes Click Save. A success toast confirms the update. If you close the modal with unsaved changes, a warning asks you to confirm before discarding them.

Change a task's details, reassign it to a colleague, or move it through its statuses. Note: Editing tasks needs Wellbeing write access (pastoral / student-support staff, leaders). Classroom teachers with read-only access don't see the task edit controls. Open the task On the case detail page, open the task's ⋮ (options) menu in the Tasks list and choose Edit. Or from Track my notes → Open tasks, expand the task's row and click Edit task. Change the details In Edit task, update the Title, the Assignee, the Status (Open, Completed, or Cancelled), or the Notes. To hand the task to a different colleague, change the Assignee — the task moves to their Open tasks list. Save Click Save — it stays disabled until you've changed something and every required field is filled. A success toast confirms the update. Delete a task (optional) To remove a task, use Delete task and confirm in the prompt. Note: Deleting a task is permanent — the confirmation warns that "This action cannot be undone."

The case detail page is the full workspace for one wellbeing note. Open the case Click a Case title in any wellbeing table. The case detail page opens. Read the header The header shows the case title, an interactive status pill (Active, Resolved, or Cancelled), the student (avatar, name, ID, year group), and attribute chips: Note type, Staff notified, Sentiment, Priority, Linked records, and Attachments. Use the chevron button to collapse or expand these details. The Attachments and Linked records in the header are clickable: images open in a preview, and other files download. Work the case body The body has three areas. Summary is an artificial intelligence (AI)-generated case summary with a "last updated" label. Comments is the timeline of follow-up comments. Tasks lists the follow-up tasks for the case. Edit the details Writers see an Edit details action in the header to change the note. A resolved or cancelled case is read-only: an info banner appears and the Edit details, Add comment, and Add task controls stay hidden or disabled until you reopen the case from the status menu.

The Wellbeing landing page is the pastoral overview: a metrics strip across the top, then a table of your wellbeing notes below. Open Wellbeing Click Wellbeing in the main navigation. The page opens on the metrics strip and your notes table. Read the metrics strip The Metrics cards show this month's figures with a "from previous month" change. Total wellbeing notes combines every category, and there is one card per wellbeing category (Mental, Academic, Social, Emotional, Physical, Environmental, Community) with that month's count. The cards are read-only summary figures, not clickable filters. Browse the notes table Below the strip, the table lists your active notes with Case title, Student name, Priority and Case status. Search the table, filter by priority, and page through the results. The heading reads All wellbeing notes if you have view-all permission (leaders and coordinators); otherwise it reads My wellbeing notes and shows only notes you created or were assigned. Open a case or a student Click a Case title to open that case's detail page. Click a Student name to open the student's profile. Case status is shown as a coloured tag: Active (blue) is an open case being worked, Resolved (green) is finished and read-only, and Cancelled (grey) is closed without resolution and read-only. Priority is one of Low, Medium, High or Critical.

Assign a follow-up action on a wellbeing case to a colleague. Note: Creating a task needs wellbeing write access (pastoral / student-support staff and leaders). For read-only staff such as classroom teachers the + add-button does not appear. Open the case Click a Case title in any wellbeing table to open its detail page. Start a new task In the Tasks tile, click the + (Add task). The + is hidden when the case is resolved or cancelled, so reopen the case first if you need to add a task. Fill in the task In Add new task, enter a Title (up to 100 characters), search and pick an Assignee, and write the Notes (what needs doing, up to 250 characters). All three fields are required, and Save stays disabled until each one is filled. Save Click Save. A new task starts in an open state, so it appears in the case's Tasks list and straight away in the assignee's Open tasks tab under Track my notes.
documents.s: Create a task from a case
